paras: O Ziaulhuq Husāmuddin! You are the one with whose light, this Math(s)navi has become brighter than the moon. You are the source of hope. It is not known upto what stage, your great courage will take it. You have tied its neck and you alone know as to where you will drag it. It is moving along, but the mover is not visible. But he is not visible for the one who has no eyes. You are its beginner; and if it proceeds further, it is surely because of you. When you get annihilated in God, you survive in Him; As such it is God who is wishing as you wish, as God certainly fulfills the desire of the pious. Initially you were one for God, (Kāna Lillah) and later you attained a state when “God is for him” (Kāna Allāhu Lahu). This is how a devotee of God proceeds to attain higher levels. This math(s)navi thanks you a thousand times and its open pages are like raised hands to express thanks and seek supplications. God saw its thanks giving to Him through its hands and mouth; and in answer to it He enhanced His graces, benevolences, and went on increasing its size. There are promises of increases for those who are thankful. The Quran says: ‘If you are grateful, I will add more favours unto you’: “La‘inshakartum la aziidannakum”: (Ibrahim: 14: 7). This is like the reward for prostration which is God’s nearness. He has further said: ‘Bow down in adoration and bring yourself closer to God’: “Wa asjud wa aqtaribi”: (Alaq: 96: 19). Prostration of our bodies becomes the nearness of our souls to God.

sections.heading: Hajj of Ka‘aba, Hajj of God
paras: If there is an increase in this math(s)navi, it is due to your humbleness and submission and not because of its showiness and acclamation by the people. We are so happy with you and in such a way as the grapevine is in the spring season. You give us a command to pull and we start pulling. You are a master of patience and the key of expansion and with these you may lead us to the owner of the house of God just as a leader of a caravan leads a caravan to the house of God (Ka‘aba). Hajj is a visit and sighting of the house, but hajj of the Lord of the house is done well by learned men, whom you may lead. Your names Zia and Husam mean shining and sword. You are both the shining sun as well as a sword of faith combined into one, because both the shining and sword are certainly one. The sword of the sun is nothing but its shining. Light is the property of the moon and shining of the sun as stated in the Qurān: ‘It is God who made the sun to be a shining glory and the moon to be a light (of

sections.heading: Beauty)’: “Huwallazi Ja’ala Shamsa Dhiyaa,an Wa Alqamara Nuran”: (Yunus: 10: 5). Difference Between Light and Shine
paras: The Qurān calls the sun as shining and the moon as light. Consider the difference between shining and light. As the sun is at a place higher than a moon, consider its shining as greater than light. There are many persons who cannot find out their way into moon’s light, but when sun rises, everybody can find his way. The sun shows everything clearly. That is why bazaars are organized during the day time, so that the genuine and non-genuine may be clearly distinguished, sot that there may be scope for cheating and loss. As the sun’s brightness from its elevated heights reaches up to earth and all things in between, it is called as mercy of the worlds. So also, you are called as such because with your great knowledge and guidance every right man is protected. But misguiding impostures proclaiming their knowledge, hate you because under your great guidance, there hollowness gets exposed. This is like the counterfeit gold which hates a gold tester. So also, the greedy dogs of the world of attainments become your enemies. Prophets go against such of their enemies, and the angels pray to god to protect them, and say; “Keep these bright lamps protected how the blows; and breaths of the thieves. Thieves and counterfeiters are the enemies of light. O Hearer of the complains, protect the prophets from the attacks of both of them”.

sections.heading: Is Mathnavi, Only a Tale?
paras: So also, I pray to you, O God! cast brightness upon this fourth volume of the mathnavi from the fourth heaven were in present is the sun. So that the fourth volume may brighten the countries and cities from its bright place of the fourth heaven, as the sun does. One who considers this Mathnavi as a tale, gets lost and forgotten like a tale, and a man committed to some cause, considers it as a great wealth of support in his programs. Water of the Nile was not water but blood in view of the Copts; and for the followers of be. H. Mūsā, it was water, not blood. So also, the enemies of the words of this math(s)navi appear us as those with bowed heads in the hell. O ZiyaulHaq! you have seen the situation of this fellows! God has shown to you the results of their action. Your keen eyes that see the secret things, are themselves a secret. May these grants of seeing and observings, granted to you by God last forever. This narrative, which we are presenting to the people is a wealth to seekers of wisdom; which remained inconclusive earlier, requires to be concluded now to pass on full information. There are many in competent fellows, who get no wisdom from it. Do not get dishearten with them. Bear with their incompetence and conclude it for the sake of competents. This narrative could not be concluded in the third volume. Therefore, this may be linked up with it in the fourth volume.

chapters.title: Heated Things Become Lovely
chapters.subtitle: Conclusion of the narrative of the lover, who ran away from the police officer and entered into an unknown garden, where he found his beloved; and prayed with pleasure for the good of the police officers, saying: ‘But it is possible that you dislike a thing, which is good for you’: “asā an tukrihuu Shai‘an, wa huwaa khairun lakum”: (Baqara: 2: 216)

paras: We had been telling in that narrative that, that person out of the fear of the police officer drove his horse into a garden. He found in the garden that beautiful maiden in the sorrow of whose separation he had suffered for eight years. He had no possibility of even seeing her shadow. He had been only hearing about her beauty which was like the bird ‘Unqaa’ for him about which he had only heard, and not seen by anybody. The only exception was a meeting with her for a short time with great fortune, which had made her his beloved. After that, that proud beauty did not give him any occasion to look at. Neither any amount of flattery nor expenditure of any money could provide an occasion to look at her by that carefree, full contended, model of beauty.

sections.heading: Love Starts with Ease but Proceeds with Difficulties
paras: The lover of any object and profession gets his lips smeared with pleasure at first by God. Thereafter, when there is a progress, all kinds of hurdles fall upon him and they go on putting new and newer chains around his feets. And when he falls into it with all craze, the doors are closed and dowers are demanded. There he goes in search of at least the beloved’s fragrance, and moves forward with the feelings of hope and hopelessness at every breath. Everyone has a fruit of hope for him and at last, one day the door opens. Then again, the door is closed and he becomes the worshipper of the door, staring constantly at it extreme anxiety and hope.

sections.heading: Policeman Pleased with the Harsh Laws
paras: When that young man entered into the garden, he found as though his feet were caught in a treasure. God made the police officer as a cause for this, when out of his fear he ran toward the garden at the dead of night. He saw his beloved holding a lamp in her hand, searching for her finger ring in the stream of the garden. He was so pleased and enthusiastic at this sight that, he started praising God to bless that police officer saying: “By running away from him, I have caused loss to him, for if he had caught me, he would have got some bribe to ransom me. But I have deprived him of that. O God! Flow twenty times that much of gold and silver upon him. Rid him of his cruelties for which the police officers are well known. Make him happy a I am happy. Make him fortunate in this and that world and get him rid of the cruel character of the policemen and the doggishness. O God! It is a habit of police officer that he always craves for troubles for people. When the proclamation comes from the king criminalizing certain acts upon the peaceful people, he feels extremely pleased and happy that they find their lives in difficulties. As against this a news comes that king has shown mercy to the people and given them reliefs and grants, his soul falls into grief and extreme pain. The policemen have hundreds of such defects. but O my lord! Give protection to this police officer from all these”. In this manner, the lover had included the police officer’s name in his supplications as he had become a cause of such a great relief for him. That police officer was a poison for all others, but for him, he was an antidote; and he was the friend of the lover.

sections.heading: Nothing Is Good or Bad per Se
paras: Thus, there is none absolutely bad in this world; and note that badness is relative. So also, there no absolute sugar and poison so as to bind each other. One is a leg and another is a chain for it and what is sugar for one is poison for another. Snake poison is as important for snake as its life, but in relationship with man it is death. For an aquatic bird, water is a garden but for a landbird it is harmful and deathly. In this manner, you may consider everything to be as such, and there are hundreds of thousands. One person is like a devil for one, but for another, one is like a king. One says; a person is truthful and good while another says he is infidel worthy of being killed. For one, a person is like paradise; for another he is a personified, pain and destruction. If you want someone to be sweet as sugar, look at him with the eyes of his lover. Do not look at that beauty with your eyes, but do so with the eyes of the lover. Rather borrow their eyes and eyesight and look at it with these eyes and sight, so that you may get rid of hatred and narrow mind. That is why God has said; ‘He has become one belonging to him”. If you do like this; you will become on like God with an everlasting sight as He has further said; ‘When I love someone, I become his ears with which I hear and I become his eyes, with which I see (Qudsi Hadith(s)). Thus, He becomes His eyes, hands and heart so that he may be that fortunate fellow with whose impacts the unfortune ones become fortunate. A hatable thing becomes lovely and leader, when it leads towards the beloved, as had happen in the case of the hatable police officer, who became a cause of the meeting of the beloved.

chapters.title: Blessed for the Cruel and Bad
chapters.subtitle: Narrative of a preacher who in every preaching used to pray for the good of the cruel, hard-hearted, mischievous, unclean and misbelievers.

paras: There was a preacher who upon getting on the dais used to pray for the good of dacoits. He used to raise his hand and pray for God’s mercy upon the bad, mischievous and rebellious people. So also, upon all punsters and loss causers, upon all infidels and idol worshippers. He would not pray for the select and clean–hearted. He would pray only for the good of the vicious. People told him: “This is not proper and conventional. It is not generosity for the misguided to be blessed”. He said: “I have seen good. They committed so such cruelties and ill-deeds against me that they took me away from sins and lodged me in goodness. Whenever I inclined toward the world, I got troubles and beatings from them. Because of these I used to turn away from the world and seek refuge in the other world, its opposite place. These wolves put me on the right track. Thus, when they became the causes of my goodness, I decided in my wisdom that they are my benefactors and I owe gratitude to them and a duty bound to pray for their good”.

sections.heading: Pains and Problems Strengthen Man
paras: Gods’ servant cries and wails before God when he is in pains and sorrows. He makes a hundred complaint about his problems. And God says: “At last, pains and troubles straightened you and inclined you toward my flattery”. If you have to complain, you should complain against those grants that take you away from the right path and turn back from His door. The truth is that every enemy of yours is a medicine, and a good alchemy and appreciable thing. It is because of him that you ran toward seclusion and seek God’s support. In fact, your friends are your enemies that they keep you away from the God’s court and make you disinterested in it. There is an animal called Porcupine which becomes stronger and fatter upon the beatings with sticks. As you beat it, with the stick, it improves and becomes fatter. The self of the faithful is certainly like the porcupine which becomes stronger and fatter upon crushing. It is for this reason that the prophets get more troubles upon them than other creatures, to such an extent that their souls become stronger than those of others. The troubles that they face are not faced by any other group of men. Leather becomes soft and pliable after tanning and treatment with bitter and burning acids. If it does not receive such treatment, it remains dirty, foul smelling and useless. Consider man also as an untanned leather, which is becoming heavy and shabby because of unclean liquids in him. Therefore, give him a treatment by massaging him with bitter and harsh medicines, so as to make him smart, clean and grand in looks and more healthy. If you cannot do this by yourself, develop consonance with the trouble, that God compulsorily imposed upon you, because troubles given by the friend are cleansing as his knowledge of treatment is better than what you can think of. If you see the rectifying impacts of the troubles, you will consider them to be sweet and pleasing. And in consequence, you see yourself as more healthy and better; and feel assured that your defeat with troubles is actually your victory and you go to the extent of telling them: ‘O my troubles, you are very reliable! Better you kill me and finish me off.’ This is strange design of God, that cruel policemen become cruel to themselves by accumulating their sins, and others become better and more improved as a result of the imposed cruelties. The cruel fellow loses the kindness of character that comes as a product of faith; and the devils meanness surrounds him. He becomes a workshop of wrath and meanness. Consider bad meanness as the root of infidelity and ungratefulness.

chapters.title: Be Kind to Be Treated Kindly
chapters.subtitle: A person’s asking H.‘Īsā: ‘O spirit of God! of all the hardships, which is the hardest?’ And H.‘Īsā’s reply thereon

paras: A wise man asked H.‘Īsā: “of all the things in the world which is the hardest.” H.‘Īsā said: “My dear, it is the wrath of God with which hell shivers. Just as we shiver”. He asked: “What is way of protecting ourselves from it”? He said: “It is by keeping away our own anger. Swallowing of the anger is the best security for us.” Think, my son, of the anger of God, as soon as you get angry and control yourself. The Qurān has spoken of the faithful: ‘who restrain anger, and pardon men: “Wal kāzhimin al

sections.heading: Ghaizh Wa Al ‘Āfin ‘Aninnās”: (Al‘Imrān: 3: 134)
paras: The police officers who have become mines of anger have anger which is greater than that of the wild beast. Inspite of this they are required to maintain law and order. There is no other kind of mercy upon him excepting that he is prevented from his bad habit. [The Prophet has said: ‘One who does not show mercy, does not get mercy’: “Man Lā yarham lā yurham” – Hadith(s)].

sections.heading: Policemen Are yet a Must
paras: In fact, there is no scope for the administration of the world without there being policemen. But this inevitability must not put anyone in misguidance. Many things do happen in the world, of their own, without control, yet they cannot be considered as good. Man has no control on his urination, and it is absolutely required. Yet it cannot be equated with the clean water gushing forth from the spring, which also comes, of its own. Keep this matter apart and speak of that heart-burnt lover who was with his beloved in the garden, at whose beauty the moon feels shy.

chapters.title: Transgression of Limits
chapters.subtitle: The lover’s attempt to transgress limits and the beloved’s shouting at him

paras: When that simpleton saw her alone, he tried to hug and kiss her. His beloved shouted at him with extreme resentment and said: “Do not transgress limits and come forward; but keep yourself within the limits of discipline.” He said: “After all, there is loneliness and nobody is here. Water is available, and there is none as thirsty as I am. No one moves here often than the wind. Who else is here to prevent us becoming informal?” She said: “O the one mad after me! Do not behave like a fool! No doubt you are ill-witted having not heard anything from the wise. You have seen the wind moving about, but you should know that there is someone who is moving the wind”.

sections.heading: Winds Are Moved by God
paras: [The Qurān says: ‘It is He who sends the winds like heralds of glad tidings, going before His

sections.heading: Mercy’: “Wa Huwallazi Yursilul Riyāha Bushran Baina Yadi Rahmatihi”: [A‘raaf: 7: 57]
paras: She continued: “The fan of the working of God approximates upon the wind and moves it. A little wind that is under our control around us will not move unless we move the fan made by us. This little movement could not take place without you and your fan. The movement of the wind coming from our lips is under the control of our body and soul. Theses body and soul together, sometimes make the wind as breaths as messengers of good and praiseworthy messages and sometimes as abusive words and insults. From this example you may think about other winds, as wisdoms have the capacities to understand the whole by observing parts.”

sections.heading: Various Performances of Air
paras: “God makes the winds, at times to bring about spring and pleasures; the autumn season is deprived of these pleasures. On the people of ‘Aad, it was a destructive storm and for the Hood it was pleasant and fragrant. He makes one wind hot and poisonous and the other one pleasant and heralderof prosperity. Consider the performances of the winds of the breaths, on its basis with those of the other winds. Breaths are connected with graces and wraths. For one community they provide honey and for other poison. Fans move to please someone and for the mosquitos and flies they become the cause of calamity. When this is the case with ordinary man-made-fans, how can the fans of God remain without causing trails and tests. The winds of the breaths and fans are partial and they are either good or bad. So also, all kinds of winds are either good or bad. The winds from the north, east and west are all beneficial and good. “You may pick up a handful of wheat from a heap and consider that the entire lot is same as it is. How can all these winds move without the fans operating from aerial constellations of the heavens. The farmers after collecting the lots of grains pray to God to send winds to separate the grain from the chaff to collect the grain for the market and chaff for the fields. When the wind delays in its movement, you will see everyone praying and craving for it.

sections.heading: Actions of Air in Human Bodies
paras: Similarly at the time of birth of babies, sounds of pains come from the mother’s mouth full of air, to attract attention of others for help. If people were not to be aware that there is someone to move the wind, they would not pray to God to move. Nobody asks the wind to blow of its own. similarly, the shipmen pray to the Lord of all creatures to blow the required wind to meet there need. So also, in the case of toothache, breath of the mouth is blown by elders to kill pain with a belief in God. Armies also pray to God, the causer of causes to blow winds of victory for them; and also request for the totemmarks on paper as sought after from all relatives to reduce labour pain of women. Thus, everyone believes and confirms that it is Lord of the worlds who moves and sends the winds. If You cannot see Him, you may understand from His impacts. Body moves upon the commands of soul, but you do not see the soul, but from the movements of the body, you confirm its existence”. After hearing all this from the beloved, the lover said: “If I am wrong in the matter of good conduct I may be pardoned, but I am quite wise in the matter of searching and sincerity; and take me as your advisor”. To this the beloved said: “Your conduct has been seen already and you accept its deficiency. As regards the other thing: wisdom and sincerity, you know it yourself by means of your own argumentation. Your conduct is, as has been seen, and we can now know with certainty that your other claims may be still worse. Whatever spills from a full vessel is the same as the vessel is filled up with.”

chapters.title: Exposure of Sins
chapters.subtitle: Narrative of a sufi who entered into his house and found his wife with a stranger

paras: One day a sufi came to his house during day time as against usual practice. There was one outdoor for the house and his wife was with a cobbler. She was in copulation with him paramour due to her demands of the body. When the sufi started tapping his door during forenoon, both were helpless as there was no way of escape or excuse. It was not the usual for the sufi to come to the house at this time from his shop. But on the day, he deliberately returned to this house with some specific thoughts. His wife was certain that on no occasion he had come to the house at that hour without attending to his routine job. Unfortunately, her thinking went wrong on that day. Though God many a times hides our sins, as he is Sattar (the hider), But sometimes, he exposes them as a punishment. When you commit a wrong, be afraid of it and do not remain contended, as wrong is a seed and god causes his germination. Many a times, he puts curtains on the sins, so that man may feel shy of them, of his own, and develop modesty.

chapters.title: Punishment upon Repetition
chapters.subtitle: Another incident has an example

paras: When H. Umar, the king and the leader of the mumins handed over a thief to a soldier and avenger, the thief shouted: “O ruler after country, my wrong is for the first time. Pray pardon me”. To this the ruler said: “May God Save us; that he should show His wrath as revenge on the first occasion. To show his generosity, He hides the sins for many times; and then to establish equity. He catches the sinners, so that both of these attributes of His (Hiding and Forgiving) may be exposed, so that the first one may become the announcer of the good news and the later has his warnings”.

sections.heading: Continuous Wrongs
paras: The Sufi’s wife had committed wrongs on many occasions and these passed off with ease and so her wrongs appeared very simple to her. She, with her lowly wisdom did not know that a pot doesn’t come out unbroken from the stream every time. At some time, it breaks. She was caught by her fate in such a way as death catches a hypocrite in surprise showing no path of escape, no friend and peace and the angel of death stretches his hand for him. Such a situation come over to that woman in the privacy of her room and both she and her paramour were caught in terrible trouble resulting in their drying up. The sufi said to him in his heart: “O you two infidels, I shall take revenge of you but in a patient manner. But at this moment I shall pretend to not know of this act so that others were not come to know of it. One who owes right to take revenge of you does so in a way as tuberculosis, which kills in a slow manner. Its victims slowly melts like Ice, moment by moment, but feels every time that he is quite healthy. I shall catch you as hunters, catch the wolf by pretending that they are not aware of its whereabouts in the cave, though it is very much inside the cave. With their conversation, the wolf goes all the more confused. He gets caught having been under the impression that the hunters were unaware about its whereabouts.

sections.heading: No Way of Escape
paras: That woman had no place to hide, as there was no upstairs portion, nor cellars, nor the other doors. There was neither a baking clay oven to hide, nor a mat to roll it upon herself. Such will be the condition on the doomsday with no pit, wall to hide nor a way to run away. That is what God has said about this situation that you will not see anything crooked or curved, as stated in the Quran: “Nothing crooked or curved will you see in their place”: “Lā tarā fihā ‘iwajan walā amtā”: (Taaha: 20: 107)

chapters.title: Unmatched Marriages
chapters.subtitle: The woman’s hiding of her paramour under the mantle as a ruse and trick: Truly mighty is your treachery: ‘Inna kaidakunna ‘azeem’: (Yusuf: 12: 28)

paras: She instantly threw her mantle on him, made the man appear as a woman and opened the door and allowed him to go out. Under the mantle was a man in clearness and disgrace fully visible as a camel’s effort to climb a ladder. The sufi asked her in surprise: “What is this? I have not seen her anytime. Who is she?” She said: “She is the wife of one among the respectable men of the city, who shares great reputation and wealth. I had shut the door fearing that some stranger may not enter the house without knowing of her being here”. The sufi said: “Tell me fast, for what purpose she had come here, so that I may attend to her job, without expecting any thanks or reward from her”. She replied: “She had come here for seeking relationship with us. She is a noble lady. I do not know much about her. She has a son who is not in the city now. He is handsome, wise, smart and has good earnings. She wanted to see our girl in surprise, without advance intimation. But the girl has gone to the school. Then, she said: “Whether the girl is flour or husk, I shall certainly take her as a bride with all my heart”.

sections.heading: Un Matched Marriages
paras: The sufi said: “We are poor and have very little materials. That lady is very honourable and rich. How can our girl be a match for them to be married in their family? This is like a door, one shutter of which is made of wood and the other of ivory. There has to be a proper match between the bride and bridegroom in marriage as otherwise it will result in shame and unhappiness. How can the rich and the poor be of the same colour? Rubies and marble are not of the same genus. Half of the garment made of jute and the other of silk appears very defective to those who look at. Falcon can never become a friend of the pigeon? How can the fly be a secret bearer of ‘unqa?”

chapters.title: Dodging of the Sufi’s Wife
chapters.subtitle: The wife’s reply that the woman is not a seeker of dowry. Her desire is secrecy and reformation. And the sufi’s asking: What is that she wants to keep as secret

paras: The wife said: “I told her about all the excuses, but she said: “I am not a seeker of wealth. We are disgusted of fine clothes, silver and gold. We are quite contented and satisfied with material possessions. Rather, we are disgusted of wealth and unhappy with it. We are not greedy and collectors of money like common people. We are after a girl who is homely, clean-hearted and good-mannered. There are the qualities which provide comfort in both the worlds.” The sufi again started to talk about his poverty to hide his inner feelings. The woman said: “I have also repeated my points and clearly explained about our poverty. But that lady’s determination is stronger than a mountain. She is not afraid of a hundred-times-greater poverty. She insists that chastity is what she is after; and she expects truthfulness and inner concentration from us”. The sufi said sarcastically: “She has seen our possessions and materials and she sees our cleanliness also very clearly. A small house fit for only one person; so small, that it cannot hold anything else within it. Even a needle. As regards chastity, hiding of defects. Piety and goodness, she has better knowledge and better scopes to take lessons from than us. She is better than us in keeping secrets as secrets and their back and front. Our lacking of materials are clear before her like the sun. But she is more aware of our secret keeping and goodness. It is very clean that the girl has no dowry and servant with her, but even without looking at her, she is herself quite aware of her goodness and homeliness. There is no need for her father to speak of all this, as this is as clear to that lady as the brightness of the day”. All these narratives were told by the beloved in the garden to her lover. And she continued: “All this, I have narrated to you to know that when a wrong gets exposed (as his attempt to hug her), it should be accepted and repented upon and there is no need for self- praising. O the one claiming of high levels; your interpretations and beliefs are with you. Keep them with yourself. Do not try to misappropriate matters like the sufi’s wife. You have also spread a net of treacheries. You feel ashamed before the people but not before God.

chapters.title: God Knows, Sees and Hears
chapters.subtitle: To explain about the reasons for calling God as all Knowing, all Seeing and all Hearing: ‘Alimun, Samirun, Basirun’

paras: She continued: “God has called Himself as ‘all Seeing, so that you may always keep in mind that He is continuingly looking at you. He has also called Himself ‘all Hearing’, so that you may keep your lips stitched to avoid talking of wrong things. So also, He has called Himself ‘all Knowing’, so that you may fear Him even in respect of evil thinking.

sections.heading: Wrong to Call God as First Causer
paras: These names of God are not just for identification, and are eternal from the very beginning. The black negro is called as kafoor (white), though this name is against his quality, yet he is called as such, only for the purpose of identification. God’s names have been derived from His eternal qualities and attributes, which contain their meanings, irrespective of whether there are things to be seen, heard and to be known. He is not understandable as the first cause as stated by some philosophers; because if He is considered as the first cause, He gets related to the first effect. He has His qualities irrespective of whether there are effects or not. Many things have come into existence as effects. Yet, there are many that are yet to come. If we consider Him only as a Causer, it can be in respect of the things already created. He has not yet become a Causer in respect of things that have not yet come. Thus, He becomes existing only in respect of things in existence until now and not for those yet to come in future. Thus, this understanding of God is defective. He cannot be understood in relationship with created things alone, as the philosophers think. He is the creator of material, moral, spiritual, sensible and insensible and all other matters.

sections.heading: Accept God as per Attributes
paras: If God is not accepted as His attributes speak of Him, and names are only for identification, then it becomes funny, ironical and treacherous just as calling a deaf man as hearer and a blind man as seer. Or, as calling a shameless fellow as modest and a black ugly fellow as beautiful. It is not improper for a new born baby to be called as Haji or Ghazi on the quality of his father. But to use these words to praise him, when he does not have these qualities, is wrong and ridiculous. God is away from those qualities with which the ignorant refer to him.

sections.heading: Pangs of Love; Punishment from God
paras: She continued: “I had understood you even before becoming close to you, that you have good face but bad conduct. I had understood you even before meeting you that you are quarrelsome and hardened. When my eyes give me pain and become red, I feel the pain even though I do not see my pain and reddened eyes. You found me to be a lamb without shepherd and thought there to be none to take care of me. Lovers suffer the pangs of love and cry, because they engage in looking out of context. They consider unprotected deers and those held in prisons as belonging to them. This results in the shooting of the arrows of God upon their hearts, out of His concern for the weak to warn them that He is their Protector and that they should not cast unworthy eyes upon them.

sections.heading: God Is Aware of Everything
paras: I am no lesser then a lamb and the baby deer, that I would remain unprotected. I have that Protector who is the only One to govern His country. He is well aware of even that wind that passes around me. He knows whether the wind is hot or cold. So also, for everyone. Therefore, let not any sick person think that God is far away from him or not seeing him. The lustful self does not have the light of the soul. But I was observing the blindness of your heart through my heart. Lustful self is deaf and blind of God. I have seen your blindness from a distance. That is why, I did not enquire about you for eight years, as I had seen you full of ignorance and confusion. One who has himself fallen in a furnace need not be enquired about his condition as his situation is quite clear.

chapters.title: Dung for Furnace: Gold for the Rich
chapters.subtitle: To explain that the world is a furnace, piety is a bath and the rich are its dried-dung providers

paras: Craze for the gains of the world is like a furnace, of a bath which provides the brightness of piety through hot water. The share of the pious out of it is cleanliness as he is in the bathroom where he cleans himself; while greedy rich are the suppliers of dried-dung to it as fuel to the furnace to heat water. God has put greed in their hearts so that they may build beautiful baths and provide hot water for bathing. That is: the pious go there to clean themselves and the greedy to serve them. They are interconnected.

sections.heading: Ignore Furnace, Go to Bathroom
paras: You should ignore the furnace and heating part of the bath and go into the bathroom. In fact, going away from the furnace is a kind of cleanliness. One who is connected with the furnace is like the servant of the one who leads patient and cautious life. When he enters into the bathroom, he comes out of it with a good-looking, bright face. So also, there are markings of those engaged with the furnace. Their clothes are covered with dust and smoke. If you cannot look at his blackened face, you may smell him, as smell is a guiding stick of the blind. What they are can be seen and felt with the smell. Even if you cannot smell, you may talk to him and understand his back ground and worth through his words.

sections.heading: Collection of Dung as Gold
paras: The rich fellow with gold, owner of the bath proudly says: “I have collected and twenty baskets of dried-dung to my house”. Your greed is like fire in the world. Dung also creates such fire. Every flame of that fire has a hundred mouths. Use of dung provides gold to the owner of the bath. This makes a wise man assess that gold is as filthy as dung, though it is bright like the burning dung. It is the heat of the sun that dries up the wet dung to burn like fire. It is the sun that has converted stone into gold so that it may create a hundred sparks in the furnace of greed. When one says that one has collected so much of gold, it means that one has collected so much of dung. Such a statement may be felt as insulting, but you may hear the owners of furnaces proudly saying to others: “You have collected only six baskets of dung during the whole day, whereas I have collected twenty baskets very easily. “One who has lived around the furnace and not seen clean atmosphere becomes sick upon smelling the fragrance of musk. If you engage yourself with furnaces, you will also become one like him and lose your capacity to enjoy the fragrance of musk. This is a loss and not a profit.

chapters.title: Good for Good; Bad for Bad
chapters.subtitle: Story of the tanner who fell unconscious on entering into the market of perfumes

paras: A tanner went to the market to buy what was needed by him. On the way, when he passed through the market of the perfumers, he became unconscious, buckled and fell down. The fragrance spread over by generous perfumers caused giddiness to him and he fell down there itself. He fell down like a dead body in full unconsciousness in the mid-noon on the road itself. People collected around him reciting la howla (all movements are by God) and started giving him treatments according to their knowledge.

sections.heading: Too Many Treatments
paras: One kept his hand on his heart and rubbed; and another started sprinkling rose-water. This man was unaware that this accident happened in the garden because of the rose only. Another person rubbed on his head and hand. Another burnt agar and oud with sugar in fire to make him breath the fragrant smoke. Another removed his clothes for free flow of air on his skin. One person bowed down to feel his breaths and another smelt his mouth to find out whether he has consumed some intoxicant. Another wise person kept his hand on his pulse to find out from its beating, the cause of his unconsciousness, or to know whether he has consumed liquor or hashish or something else. All the people were unable to find the reason. Then they informed his relatives about his falling unconscious there, as nobody could do anything to know his affair.

sections.heading: First Diagnosis, Then Treatment
paras: He had a fat bother, very clever and wise. He came fast and brought a little shit of the dog, passed through the surrounding people, weeping and said: “I know the reason for his sickness. If you understand the reason for sickness, it becomes easy to cure him. It is very difficult to treat a patient without proper diagnosis, on trial-and-error basis. Once the reason is found out, all speculations are eliminated”. He said to himself: “A vein of his brain has the smell of the dog’s shit, layer upon layer. So much that with foul smell around him he is engaged in leather tanning from morning to night to make his earning. For months and years, he has become habituated to this foulness, and therefore, the fine fragrance of perfumes has upset him.

sections.heading: Treat as per Patient’s Nature
paras: That is why the great medicine-man, Galen has advised to give “to the patient what he is accustomed to, as the sickness is caused by something that is apposed to habit.” Therefore, his treatment is with a medicine he is accustomed to. Because of this, he has become like a dung-pushing worm. Such a worm goes unconscious upon smelling the rose. Shit of the dog is the medicine for him, as he is habituated to its small. The Qurān also says: ‘Impure women are for men impure’: “Al khabiith(s)ātu lil khabiisth(s)iin”: (Noor: 26: 24). Understand the meaning of this statement well.

sections.heading: Advice Ineffective on the Crooked
paras: Good advisers try to treat a man with ambar and rose to open the doors of guidance. Good words do not go in consonance with vile persons. Be sure that such words are not fit and suitable for them. Crooked persons got more crooked and shocked with the fragrance of godly inspirations upon the prophets and they told them: “we take you as bad omen’: “Innā tatayyarnā bikum”: (Yāsīn: 36: 18). What you say is a cause of sickness and disease for us. Your sermons are a bad omen for us. If you speak much to us, we shall resort to stoning you. We have been brought up in entertainment and pleasures and accustomed to them. We have never cared to account for advice and instructions. Our food is falsehood, self-praise and laughter. We feel your advice as nauseating”. This is the pitiable situation for these deniers that they give opinion to their wisdom to sharpen it. Foul smell of infidelity and idolatry has gone beyond limits for them. Leave the affairs of these people for something. Let us go to that unconscious tanner.

chapters.title: Bad to Be Treated Badly
chapters.subtitle: Secret treatment of the unconscious tanner by his brother with the smell of dirty shirt

paras: That young man chased the onlookers away so that they might not see his treatment. He kept his head nearer to sick man’s ear as though he is praying for him in secret and kept the dog’s shit on his nose, as he had already smeared his palm with it, which he had considered as the treatment of the sick man’s dirty brain. His dirty brain smelt the foul smell, as it was very suitable for it. After a little while, the virtually dead body started moving and people thought that it was due to some magic spell he had put into his ears. He recited the spell and blew it into the ear and the dead fellow got back to life with its support.

sections.heading: Pleasure in Obscene Talks
paras: The movements of the mischievous fellows are like this, when talks of fornication, style and coquettishness of women and the spells of their eyebrows are referred to. Whoever not getting benefitted with the fragrance of musk, is one accustomed to foul smell. That is why God has called the idol worshippers as unclean: “innamal mushrikūna najasun”: (Tauba: 9: 28). They are created in the beginning itself in filth. The worm that takes birth in dung can never accustom itself to ambar, because there has not been the sprinkling of light upon it. He is only the rind having no pulp. He does not have the heart which is the pulp of human body. Had God’s light sprinkled upon him even by a part of it, he would not have thought of bringing up chicken from under the heap of cow dung, as the Egyptians used to do by keeping the eggs underneath it to hatch. This was their high skill that even from a dirty environment, they bought up smart, healthy, lively chicks.

sections.heading: Good Ones from Bad Environment
paras: Thus, sometimes even from dirty environment come out not domestic, mean birds, but birds with great wisdom and intelligence. That is; noble men of high character and ideal. The beloved continued: “But you are not like them, but you are devoid of that light as you keep your nose for foul smell. Your cheeks and face have become pale because your separation from great things. You are a yellow-dried-up-leaf and a raw fruit. The cauldron has become black and smokey because of burning on fire, but the meat that is cooked in it has remained uncooked”. The beloved lady continued: “For eight years, I gave you the heat of separation, but because of your hypocrisy even a little of your defect has not gone. You are unripe and you will never ripen how much ever warmth is provided to you even for thousands of times. The bunch of your grapes has remained unripe, stoney and hard whereas other bunches have dried up and become currants”.

chapters.title: False Claims of the Lover
chapters.subtitle: The lover’s treacherously seeking pardon, and the beloved’s realization of this trick too

paras: The lover said: “Please forgive me. I was only testing you, so as to be sure whether you are a free hand or seclusive. I know this well even without a test, but mere thinking is not as good as observation. You are like the sun which is quite apparent and well known. What loss would be there, if I conduct a test. You are as good as I am and therefore, I am actually testing myself everyday for losses and gains. You know that the enemies of the prophets also tested them; and in answer to them they showed miracles. I have tested my eyes through light and O my dear, evil sight are away from your eyes. “This world is like a ruin and you are like a treasure hidden in it; and I searched for the treasure, you should not feel wronged. I showed a foolishness act to you. By doing what I did I only wanted to enable myself to speak of your goodness before your enemies. So that when my tongue takes your name, my eyes may stand up in your favour as dacoit of your honour, I accept it and seek punishment, and for that, I have brought the sword and shroud. O my great commander, do not kill me with anything other than your sword. O my beautiful moon! I have no more strength to bear your separation. Cut off my hands, feet and head with your own hands as I belong to your hands and not of others. “You once again speak of separation. Do not speak of this. You may speak of anything but not this. The occasion to talk has come only now to speak of my difficulties, but there is very little time left now and I cannot speak anymore I have only spoken of my apparent conditions which are like the rind, but the invisible feelings are still hidden inside. If we remain away from each other as we are now, even the scope for expressing will go away. If any mistake is committed by me, I seek your pardon for it and hope to be pardoned. I only made a test. Please consider my helplessness, when I myself feel ashamed of what I have done”.

chapters.title: Beloved Refuses to Believe
chapters.subtitle: The beloved’s rejection of the lover’s excuses as tricks

paras: That moonlight beauty opened her lips and said: ‘it is a day in my side and a night on yours. At a time of taking proper decisions, why do you speak of dark excuses before the wise people. You are giving excuses but the secrets of your heart are as bright and clear as the day before us. Inspite of this, when I am hiding what I know, as a token of respect for the speaker, you are going beyond limits without concern for our gracefulness. Learn the lesson of seeking pardon from your father, H. Ādam upon his sin.

sections.heading: H. Ādam’s Repentence
paras: H. Ādam voluntarily lowered himself and stood at the place of footwear. He did not present any excuses before the One who knew his secrets and stood up on his legs to express his guilt and sought pardon. He sat upon a lot of ashes and did not jump from one branch of a tree to the other. Straight away he said: “O Lord! We have wronged our souls”: “Rabbanā zhalamnā anfusanā”: (A‘raaf: 7: 23). He saw witness of the angels standing in front and back of him, through his soul, who were hidden from the physical eyes. He found them holding a two-pronged spear upto the heaven. Similarly, Angels told H. Sulaimān: “O Sulaimān! Become humble like the ant, so that the double two-pronged spear may not tear you off.”

sections.heading: Mere Words of Repentance Are Useless
paras: Do not stand anywhere other than a place of truth even for a moment. There is no such sincere servant for man as the eye. Truth only is the proper guide for man. This looking at things is not with the external eyes but with the inner sight of the soul. If one without the inner sight repents and without his inner voice, it is no repentance. Inspite of blabbering words of repentance he remains as dirty as ever. O Ādam! You are not blind of the eyes, but when fate comes to play its role, eyesight becomes blind. H. Ādam had the inner sight, but he was humble before the fate as decided by God. It takes long periods of life to find out this inner light and to remain without falling into the deep well.

sections.heading: Outer Light and Inner Light
paras: In the case of the blind, his fate always accompanies him and falling repeatedly becomes a part of his nature and a routine affair. If he falls into dirt, he does not really know as to of what is the foul smell from; whether it is of his own body or from outside. If musk is sprinkled upon him by someone, he will find its fragrance as from him alone and not as grant from a friend. Thus, two bright eyes are a very great grant, better than the support of hundreds of mothers and fathers. And in particular the eyes of the heart which have seventy layers; each layer being a bright light, and the sensible light of the eyes is borrowed from this light. How regrettable, I cannot explain the seventy layers of this light, as there are dacoits sitting and waiting to snatch so as to misuse them. They have put a hundred knots under my tongue and out of fear, I dare not speak of all that. How can a good horse with its, legs bound walk well? Excuse me! The knots, that they have put on my tongue are big chain stronger than the ropes, which tie the horse’s legs. What I have to say relates to the secrets of God which are like pearls relating to God’s authority which is like a grinding stone which would grind and powder the pearls. Such being their subtlety, I am not in a position to speak fluently in the matter. However, powdered pearls are useful to brighten the eyes to remove cataract Therefore, even if I cannot explain them in detail, they are not without benefits. There is no need for these pearls to regret upon being broken, as they become the light of the eyes upon breaking. With this hope and confidence, I say something about these matters hoping that God would set them right and eliminate deficiencies.

sections.heading: Admit Mistakes: Become Greater
paras: Wheat upon breaking into pieces becomes flour and comes to shop for sale in a better capacity. Therefore, O beloved! Stop using slippery words of flattery, become humble, when a mistake has come out of you. The special children of H. Ādam believe in following his path of saying: “We have committed hardship upon ourselves as he had said”: “Rabbanā zalamnā anfusinā”: (A‘raaf: 7: 23). Place your needs before us and do not argue just as the arrogant accursed Iblis had done. He put the blame upon God saying: “I did not bow to H. Ādam as I am better than him, as you created me from fire and him from clay”: “Anā

sections.heading: Kahirum Minhu Khalaqtani Min Nārin Wa Khalqtahu min”:(A‘raf: 7: 12). If You Feel That
paras: his obstinacy had hidden his defects, then you may also resort to it and be quarrelsome and see the consequences. That Abu Jahel sought for a miracle from the Prophet like the haughty Ghuz Tursk. He quarreled with him and put a demand for a miracle from that great king, H. Muhammed Mustafa. That doggish fellow demanded, and the Prophet showed him the miracle of the splitting of moon and the praises made by pebbles. He saw the miracles but these increased his doubts. On the contrary, H. Abu Bakr did not demand the miracle and simply said: “This graceful face cannot say anything other than truth”, and I believed in his prophethood. How can a person like you have a right conduct a test upon a friend like me?

chapters.title: Conducting Trials on God
chapters.subtitle: Challenge of a Jew to H. Alī: ‘If you have so much confidence in God, fall down from this high fort’. And H. Alī’s reply to him

paras: One day an enemy, not aware of the honour and greatness of God asked H. Alī Murtaza, while they were standing upon the rampant of a very high fort: “O cautious one, are you well aware of the protection provided by God to men?” He replied: “Yes! He is a Protector of His own, without depending upon others, right from the time we were in the semen and also during our childhood”. Then the Jew said: “Then, you may fell yourself down from this fort and develop your confidence in full in Him. So that I also may develop confidence in your confidence and also develop good faith in you with an evidence”.

sections.heading: Lowly One Not to Test the Great
paras: Then, H. Alī told him: “Keep quite and withdraw your words so that your life may not be caught in difficulties because of such outrageous courage! What right does a humble servant have to test God through trials? What right does a servant have even to think of this non sensible thing. O ill-witted, foolish fellow! Do you want to put God on trial? It is God who has a right to test his servants at any and all times, so as to make us see ourselves in our true colours, and about what beliefs we have in secret about Him. Did H. Ādam say to God, that he committed the wrong to test God’s attitude upon commitments of wrong by us? And that he wanted to see the extent of His restraint, generosity and forgiveness? Should anybody have the courage to think so? As your wisdom is wrong, your excuses for the sin are all the more wrong.

sections.heading: Put Yourself to Tests
paras: How do you know of testing the Authority that has held aloft the roof of the sky above? You do not know the difference between good and bad. First, put yourself into trial, and then think of others. If you put yourself in trial and know your own worth, you will not even think of putting anyone else, on trial, nor will you have the time to do so. If you find yourself as of the worth of a grain of sugar, you will consider yourself to be fit to be one belonging to paradise. Which is the mine of sugar. Be also sure, that God will not send sugar for you without first putting you on trial. And also know, that if you are worthy in God’s view, He will not send you to the lowly place of footwear without trial.

sections.heading: Difference Balances for Different Weights
paras: Does anywise man throw a precious pearl in a toilet full of filth? No well aware man will throw wheat grains in a lot of husks. If a disciple tries to put his master and guide in trial to test him for his worth, it is clear that the disciple is an ass. If you try to test him on the path of faith, be sure that you are putting yourself into trial because of your suspicious nature. Your outrageousness and ignorance will be totally exposed and you will become naked in the process of trial. If a particle tries to weigh a mountain, its weighing balance makes in accordance with the weight and worth of the thing to be weighed: large balances for weighing heavy things and small one for small things. A God’s friend is kept in a different kind of balance.

sections.heading: Wisdom, Scholarship, Inner Inspiration
paras: Testing a guide is like keeping the guide under your control. When he cannot be weighed in the balance of your small wisdom, he will break that balance itself. Your guide is not only in respect of ideas emanating from scholarship and wisdom but also from inner spiritual inspirations of heart. If you try to understand him through the weighing balance of your lowly wisdom, you do not find him fitting in it and therefore, you will fail to understand him. You have to take the balance of the inner spiritual guidance from him. You have learnt a little of this spiritual information from him. They are like the marks put on by a sculptor. These marks cannot test the abilities of the sculptor. Therefore, do not be audacious to control your master by testing him on the basis of a little knowledge that you have taken from him. In case the disciple carries in a test of their master, the very means of conducting the test are those that are taught by the master himself. The sculptures are just a few creations of the sculptor. There are many more yet to come from him, which exists in his knowledge and thought which are many times larger than the already made sculptures. A few cannot stand up against the large numbers of the master.

sections.heading: Misfortune Starts with Insinuations
paras: Remember well that the moment the insinuation of conducting a test upon the master comes to you, your misfortune starts and tries to destroy you in full. In this situation, you should immediately turn towards God and fall in prostration to Him. Wetten the place of prostration with your tears and pray to God to save you from such doubts. The time at which the object of conducting the test came to you, you should consider it to be the time when your masjid got filled with the Khurrub grass. [This is a kind of grass upon the growth of which the building upon which it grows collapses. This grass is considered as a symbol of destruction] Therefore, immediately upon coming of such insinuation, take an about-turn and turn your face towards God, so that, that great conductor of Trial may take you under His protection from insinuations, and other trials by men, jinns and trials themselves. O Hisamuddin come forward and narrate the facts relating to the constructions taken up by H. Dawood (of Masjid-e-Aqsa upon which this Khurrub grass had started growing).

chapters.title: Building of Masjid-E-Aqsa
chapters.subtitle: Narrative of the Masjid-e-Aqsa and the growth of Khurrub grass upon it and H. Dawood’s intention to construct well before H. Sulaiman but avoiding to do it immediately

paras: Upon H. Dawood’s determination to build Masjid-e-Aqsa with stones, God sent a inspiration to him to forget it as that house is not destined to be built by you. It is not among our decisions that you should be the one to build and heighten it. H. Dawood said: “What is wrong with me, O knower of the secrets that you are asking me not to build the masjid?” God said: “You have killed many persons for me of their crimes; and you carry the burden of the oppressed upon your neck. Many persons became victims of your melodious voice and lost their lives. Your voice has caused many killings with its melody by engaging many beautiful souls”. H. Dawood said: “I was dominated by you and intoxicated in you. My hand was tied with your hand. Is it not a fact that one dominated by the king is in needy of mercy?

sections.heading: Fana Fillāh and Bāqi Billāh
paras: Is it not that the dominated fellow has no existence of his own? God said: “O dominated one! Where is your going out of existence? Getting dominated is relative to the Dominator. A dominated fellow who got separated from himself very much exists with greater strength and is better than all other existing things. He “lost his existence” is in the sense that he annihilated himself in the attributes of God. This annihilation results in his ever-lasting existence in God. He attains the position of annihilation in God and exists with God (Fana fillāh and bāqi billāh). All souls go under the control of, and also all bodies are within the range of the arrows of the one who is dominated by Our benevolence. He is not helpless but is dominant upon others because of Our friendship and closeness.

sections.heading: Power of Dominated by God
paras: The highest level of a servant is to be under Our total control and his own control upon himself being totally lost. This kind of control has a great taste of control, because of which one annihilates himself in God. The taste of any food or drink in the world is a branch of the taste of that annihilation of the self. Though, he has lost interest in any of the worldly taste, this loss itself has a great taste, which he has attained. One dominated by God becomes a carrier of His mercies and gets lost in the ocean of His mercies. But his getting lost is not such that anyone else can dominate over his kind and generous acts and goodness. He becomes a warden of all existences, without any doubt, disputation and pomp. He does not have anyone to be his equal. He is not dependent upon any special markings. He is not dependent upon time, and this and that; that is; he attains a position beyond space and time. He has no difficulty of any kind; no one tells him, and no one can seek answer from him. Do not talk too much on this matter as God alone knows best

chapters.title: Animal Soul and Human Soul Compared
chapters.subtitle: Exegesis of the statements: The faithful ones are brothers; and scholars are like a single soul; and in particular the oneness of H. Dawood, H. Sulaimān and other prophets. If you do not have faith in any one of the prophets, your faith is not perfect. And it is also a symbol of oneness that if you destroy one house our of a thousand, all get destroyed and not a single wall will remain intact as per the Qurān: “We do not differentiate between any of the prophets”: “Lā nufarriqu baina ahadim mir rusulihi”: (Baqarah: 2: 285) And one hint is enough for a wiseman. And this is more than one hint.

paras: There came an address from God to H. Dawood: “O chosen, good-featured-prophet! Do not put your heart in anxiety because of this information. Do not allow grief to enter into yourself and do not be sorrowful. If that masjid does not come about with your efforts and strength, your son will take up that job. If this place cannot be constructed by you, certainly it will be constructed by your son. Be wiser to know that what is done by him is your own act. Consider it as the old united effort of all the faithfuls. The faithful are many in numbers. But in fact, they are all one. Their bodies are many but their soul is one. Wisdom and soul that are in the oxen and donkeys are different from the wisdom and soul of humans. Then again, the wisdom and souls of humans are different from those of the saints and prophets.

sections.heading: Animal Soul Different from Human Soul
paras: Animal soul of each animal is different, distinct and separate. It is not one. Do not search for oneness in the soul which is connected with materials and air. If it takes food, it takes only for itself and gets satisfied and others have no impacts of it. If it carries a weight, it alone carries and no other soul. The pleasure of one animal soul is a cause of pain of another; rather it gets pleased upon another’s death. When it sees another’s materials, it gets feelings of jealousy. The souls of the wolves and dogs are different, but the souls of the lions of God are one.

sections.heading: Souls of Prophets and Saints Are One
paras: I have spoken of the souls of the saints and prophets in plural. But this plural number is in relation to their bodies which become hundred bodies. This is like the light of the sun falling from the sky. It is but one; but it gets divided into hundred parts on the basis of its falling on different houses and their compounds. If you remove the walls of the house, they all become one. There will be no difference in the light falling upon this house and its compound and upon others. Similarly, when bodies of the faithful do not exist anymore, then souls will become a single soul.

sections.heading: Sameness and Resemblance
paras: These discussions create differences and difficulties in understanding, this is not sameness but resemblance (example). There are many differences between the person (body) of the lion and the brave man, physically. But while considering the bravery of both as one. That is; that man is similar to the lion on bravery alone, but not the same as lion in all respects. Nothing in the world is comparable to human soul with which I can compare. I can only give an example, yet with some defects, so that your mind may be rid of difficulties.

sections.heading: Animal Soul Explained
paras: In every house, lamps are kept at night, so as to eliminate darkness with their light. Consider the lamp as a body and its light as soul. This light comes about when there is oil and wick in the body of the lamp. Similarly, the human body is in need of food and nourishment to exist. This is like oil for the lamp. The wick has fine senses: (hearing, seeing, smelling, tasting and touching). They are dependent upon food as well as rest (sleep) of the body. Without food and sleep body cannot survive; and yet a time comes upon it, when with both food and sleep, it cannot surview. That is to say, even with oil and wick the lamp has no existence when the bright light of the day shines upon it. Similarly, the body of man inspire of food and sleep searches for death during sickness, when senses slowly become weak and ultimately die along with body. This is with regard to the animal soul. Thus, all senses of the body are destructible. They get annihilated before the light of God on doomsday. [Apart from animal soul, which all animals including man have, man alone has another soul: human soul with its extraordinary spiritual and intellectual senses]

sections.heading: Senses of Human Soul Don’t Die
paras: But destructible senses of the human soul do not get annihilated in full like grass. They are like the stars and moon, which cease to be visible upon the arrival of sun. This is just as the itching and injury caused by the flea become ineffective, when you see the snake rushing towards you. Or, like a naked man jumping into water to avoid the biting of honeybees. But the bees do not fly away from him, but will be circumambulating upon his head, and bite him whenever he raises his head. In like manner, human soul temporarily vanishes but does not cease to exist. For example, devilish insinuations are like honeybees and water is like protection from God by taking these and those names of His actions and attributes. Start taking the gulps of the water of godly thoughts in full patience and concentration to protect yourself from earlier thoughts and insinuations. As they slowly go away and totally vanish, it is as though the clean godly water rids you of them, and head to foot, you adopt the qualities of that water. Just as the honey bee fears water and does not dare enter into it, your devilish insinuations also fear you and run away from you. Thereafter, you may go out of water, if you want to, as from the esoteric and internal aspects, you become one among others of the servants of God imbibed with the quality of that godly water.

sections.heading: Human Soul Merges with Attributes of God
paras: You become one among such servants, because many of them who have died and gone away from the world are not obliterated but their souls are sunk deep in the qualities (attributes) of God. The qualities of them all are like the qualities of God, but are as invisible and dull as the stars are before the sun. if you do not believe me in this regard. You may read this in the Qurān: ‘When lo! They will all be brought up before us’: “Fa izā hum jamī‘un ladainā muhdharūn”: (Yasin: 36: 53). Muhdhaūna, that is, those brought up before God cannot be the annihilated ones. This makes you to be certain that souls continue to live. They do not cease to exist.

sections.heading: Fate of Animal Soul
paras: The animal soul has no existence along with God as against the human soul. The ceasing to exist is a torture for it and it is hidden behind curtains, whereas the human soul is not behind curtains, but has joined with the Absolute Truth. I have explained to you about this animal soul with the example of a lamp. Do not think of its unity with God. You may connect your human soul with the clean souls of the great pious searches of Truth.

sections.heading: Animal Souls Not Collective
paras: Your hundred lamps (as animal souls) whether they are put out or still bright, are not one but separate and distinct from each other. That is why they are in quarrels, but you never hear of any quarrels among the prophet; because the light of the prophets was from the great sun, God, but our light of the animal soul is from the lamp mixed up with smoke. One is put out, other burns for a day; another is well bright and yet another is dim. Animal soul survives with food and it also dies with good and bad qualities. If lamp of animal soul extinguishes or rolls up around itself. Its house becomes dark but not the neighbor’s house. When the light of that house still continues, it means that each is a different lamp. This is the example of the animal soul and not of the godly soul. Godly soul is like moon. When the moon rises in the darkness of the night, every hole of the house receives its light. Consider this moonlight as one for the hundred houses because its light does not cease on any of the houses. So long as the sun is bright between the horizons, it becomes a guest of light of every house. And later, when the sun sets, the light of all lives (houses) gets lost. This is an example of light, and not light itself. This example is a guide to you and dacoit for your enemy. Example is like a spider which builds a dirty curtain for itself. With its own saliva it puts a curtain upon itself and blindfolds the senses of its own eyes. This should be taken only as example for partial understanding. It is like holding the neck of the horses, when you will be gainful. You can ride on it. Instead of this, if you catch its legs, you will receive kicks. Do not try to ride on the horse of the vicious self without the bridle of the guide. Make your wisdom and faith as your guide. May god protect you! Do not consider this path as dull and lowly. It is bright path, but it is difficult for the souls to have patience in this path. Come let us go to narrative of the Masjid-e-Aqsā along with good natured H. Sulaimān, the prophet of God.

chapters.title: Construction by Spiritual Means
chapters.subtitle: Rest of the narrative of the construction of the Masjid at the hands of H. Sulaimān

paras: H. Sulaimān started the construction of the Masjid which is clean and prosperous like the Ka‘abā and Minā. There appeared a glory and grandeur in its construction as against other constructions which are dull and slow. Every stone that was broken from the rock for its construction used to speak at the start: “take me out”. Light used to fall from these rock pieces just as from the water and clay when H. Adam’s form was being made. The stones used to move, of their own without being carried by carriers; and the doors and walls of the masjid came to life themselves. God has said the walls of paradise are not dull and rough like the other walls made of materials. The Qurān says: ‘Verily the home of the hereafter, is life indeed’: “Innad dārul ākhirata lahiyal haiwān”: (Ankabut: 29: 64). This is like the human body, the doors and walls of which are also made of clay, yet it is a great house as an empire. When this human body can talk, why not those stones when specially gifted?

sections.heading: Materials of Paradise Are Different
paras: Trees, fruit and clean water of paradise also talk with its dwellers; because paradise is not made with the help of implements but with the action of your faith. This building of the world is made of lifeless water and clay, but paradise is built with lively worship. This worldly building is full of hindrances like of its makers and materials but that heavenly building is built upon the foundation of knowledge and good acts. The thrones, forts, crowns and apparels of a paradise engage themselves in talks with the dwellers therein. Its carpets also get rolled up themselves and the house gets swiped of dust without broomstick. The throne of the paradise moves without anybody carrying it. Its door and door chain produce sweet tunes like the singers and qawwals. You may question as to how a house can be cleaned without brooming. To find out this, you may consider the house of your heart which is full of griefs and sorrows of sins. It becomes clean without brooming just by repentance. There is a life of permanence of the paradise in your heart. But it cannot be explained by words of mouth. Therefore, there is not scope to explain, but there is scope to realize through your own effort, meditation and concentration.

sections.heading: Practical Advice Better
paras: After the construction of the masjid was over under the supervision of H. Sulaimān, it was safe and secured. H. Sulaimān used to go into it every morning in order to preach to the people. Sometimes, he would advise them in words, speeches and songs and sometimes by acts, demonstration, and humble prostration. Practical advice attracts the people more, as it reaches into the ears of the hearers as well as the blind. And in this, thoughts of issuing commands and seeking obedience do not come about. It has greater effect upon the subordinates.

chapters.title: Instructions by Demonstration
chapters.subtitle: Narrative of the initiation of the Khilafat of H. ‘Usmān and his sermon that one who advises by practice is better than the one who speaks in words

paras: When H. Usman got the opportunity of reaching upon the pulpit of the Prophet, he started with the third step. The prophet’s pulpit had three steps. The prophet used to sit on the top step. H. Abū Bakr in his days of Khilāfat used to sit upon the second step. H. ‘Umar during his days used to step upon the lowest third step. (steps in the order of height). The two califs did as such in the honour of Islam and the Prophet. H. ‘Usmān, during the days of his Khilafat sat upon the top first step, as the Prophet used to sit. A senseless person asked him: “The earlier two califs have not sat upon the top first step, as it was considered as the place of the noble Prophet. Why do you claim superiority upon the earlier two califs, when you are lower in status than them”? He said: “If I sit upon the third step, it is liable to be thought that I am following the example of H. Umar. If I take the second step as my place, people will say that I am like H. Abū Bakr. The top most, first step is the place of the noble Prophet; and nobody will ever think of me being like the Prophet.”

sections.heading: Falling of the Light of God
paras: After this, that graceful, H. ‘Usmān sat at this place in silence for a long time upto the time nearer to the prayer of ‘Asr. Nobody was dare enough to say: “Please recite or speak or get up and go out of the masjid.” Every big and small person was stuck dumb with the impression of his might. The hall and terrace of the masjid were full of the light of God. One who had bright eyes observe this light, and even the bird felt the warmth of this light, thinking that the bright sun is in full brightness. This warmth opened up all eyes, so that the eyes could see what all has been heard about. Warmth of the sun has a sharpness causing narrowness of the heart; but this was causing widening and enlargement of the heart. When the blindman becomes warm with this original light, he speaks out loudly that he has brightened eyes: “I am no longer blind.” But, O simpleton! You are very much intoxicated to feel so much. There is yet some distance to get the eyes brightened. This is only a little gain for the blind from the sun’s warmth (not its light). Put efforts to get that light which is a hundred-time greater light than this. God knows this best.

sections.heading: Unseeable and Strange but Realizable Situation
paras: When this is the situation of elation of that fellow who has seen just a semblance of it, what is its impact upon one who has observed it more or in full. Its impacts cannot be explained in words and through intelligent arguments. Even a philosopher and wise man like Bū Alī Sīnā (Avicenna) cannot explain it. This observation can be only by one’s own efforts. Even if the tongue becomes hundred times more effective, it cannot speak of it, or set aside the curtain from it with its hands. If someone tries to do it, God’s sword will cut his hand off. What is a hand for this purpose? The head itself will be cut off, which carries on mischiefs out of its ignorance. I speak of this as I am compelled to use the linguistic phrases as there is no such curtain which can be set aside nor is there a hand that can do so. This is like a saying that the auntie would be uncle were she to be a man. This is only a speculative thought based on ‘ifs’ and ‘buts’ which in practical reality is impossible. With my tongue even if I speak of the observation which is absolute and clear, totally devoid of doubts, for lakhs of years, it is far far less. It can never be complete.

sections.heading: Impacts of Heavens and Stars on Earth
paras: But at the same time do not get frustrated. When God wishes He can pass on that Light in an instant from the distant heaven. Sun, moon and stars in the heavens are millions of miles away from the earth, but their light reaches instantly. They have hundreds of impacts even upon deep mines with the might and power of God. When their lights eliminate darkness from such long distances, the star of Truth with its godly qualities is greater in power. O seeker of help! Sky is at a distance of a journey of five hundred years, but in putting its impacts, it is quite nearer to the earth. Saturn is at a distance of three and a half thousands of years of journey, but its impacts are acting every moment upon earth. Yet they are like passing shadows, which get wiped off as they are of no worth before the sun. The greatest impact upon earth is of the sun. similarly, the impacts of the clean souls of the prophets and saints fall upon the stars and the heavens. To look at in a cursory manner these dwellers of the heavens are the makers of components, but the inner qualities of (humans) like prophets, saints and scientists cast their impressions upon the heavens. They are the makers of the inner components of heavens. [Heavens, stars etc. are observed, studied and understood by humans. Left to themselves they are of no worth and power. They have had their impacts upon earth for millions and millions of years and upon other creatures on earth. But no creature bothered about them. It is only men, who came as the last of the creatures, tried to understand them. But for man, the existence of anything in the universe is of no consequence. This is the greatness of man as referred to in ayath: ‘We did indeed offer the Trust to the heavens, the earth and the mountains; but they refused to undertake it, being afraid thereof, but man undertook it’ (Ahzāb: 33 72). This Trust is the responsibility to study and control over things, as God Himself does to the extent of man’s limitations. Man is also referred to as God’s vicegerent. No other creature though as huge and lofty like heavens and mountains dared to do that job. This is what Rumi means to say: “The inner qualities of humans are the makers of the components of heavens. The inner components of stars such as the sun is Hydrogen, which is getting converted into Helium; and in this process it is releasing immense energy in the form of light and heat. The basic inner component, Hydrogen, is also made by man on earth. The process that is taking place in the sun is nuclear reaction, which also man is carrying on upon earth. All this is not by man’s physical power but with his inner faculties: wisdom and spiritual power, will power etc.; whatever we may call suiting to contexts. They are all inner qualities of man ― Translator]

chapters.title: Man Is Macrocosm
chapters.subtitle: To explain that philosophers of physical things call man as a Microcosm (small universe), but the philosophers od God (saints) call man as Macrocosm (large universe) for the reason that those philosophers look at man’s physical shape, but the saints look at man’s inner qualities

sections.heading: H. Muhammed, Father of All Humans
paras: From the point of view of size, you are a small world, but from that of the inner qualities you are a large world. To look at, the branch of a tree is the source of fruit, but in reality, the branch exists to carry the fruit. If the object of the gardener was not fruits, he would not have sowed the seed of the tree (If the object of nature was not bring up man, the world would not have been created). Thus, the tree is created by and for the fruit, though apparently the fruit comes out of the tree. That is why Prophet Muhammed said that: “H. Ādam and other prophets will be behind me under my flag of the praise of God on the doomsday, but I am not proud of it”. In other words, the object of the creation of H. Ādam and his children is to create Muhammed. As a further clarification, that collection of all perfectness, the noble Prophet said about himself and his followers: “We are the last of the peoples but ahead of all others. Though apparently, I am the son of H. Ādam, but in reality, I am a great grandfather. It is ultimate end that is important and not its initiation.
