It is to me that the angels prostrated as my light was already hidden in H. Ādam. He was called upon the seventh heaven to seek the benefits of my light. Thus, my father is created out of me just as the tree is created out of the fruit.

sections.heading: First Intention, Then Action
paras: What comes first is the thought (intention) and then comes action; and in particular the intention which is related to the earliest beginning (creation), when nothing existed. When a searcher of realities himself in search, realizations do not come to him immediately. They take much time. Further, all the objects sought after by him do not come about. They come out and go in a gradual process, one after another. However, up to the point that are yet to come, it is not a long way. They are very fast moving. But this realization one after another is like going into a forest, with full confidence where too many trees are met on the way. In such a case the delay in realization cannot be hard on the soul.

sections.heading: Fast Movements of Soul and Body
paras: At every moment a man’s heart goes to the Ka‘abā. It is just by the act of thinking which is by the mind. But God’s grace can make the body also go fast like the heart. This distance of time and space is for the body and not for the soul. But the doors of the adobe of God are never closed. When God converts the body to move fast like the soul, its marching also becomes free from the measurements in terms of miles and furlongs of space and time, and it can also move instantly. Thus, there are a hundred hopes for you to proceed. Proceed! And do not engage yourself in mere talks. Though you are blinking, your eye lids are closed due to sleep, but you are in a boat and the boat can take you to your place even when you are in sleep. There is every hope and possibility that God will make you observe matters with closed eyes.

chapters.title: Prophet Muhammed Is Like Noah’s Ark
chapters.subtitle: Exegesis of the hadith(ŝ): The example of my community is like the Noah’s ark. Attach yourself to it and get saved, one who ignores it, sinks

paras: It is for this reason that the Prophet said: “I am like an ark in the flood of our time. Myself and my companions are like the Noah’s ark. Whoever takes it support gets relieved”.

sections.heading: Support of Prophets, Saints Needed in Life
paras: When you are with your guide, you are away from wrongs. You are moving about in your affairs during day and night, you are safe in the ark. You are under the protection of the life- giving power in sleep, yet you are continuing your journey. Do not keep yourself away from your shaikh, who is like the prophet of your days and work under him and do not rely upon your own thoughts and effects. You may be strong like a lion, but when you go on your way without a guide, you will go wrong like the fox and get disgraced. Be warned, do not think of flying high without the wings and feathers of the guide, so that so many get the support of the guide’s army.

sections.heading: Guide’s Wrath Also Helps
paras: At one time, the waves of his benevolence are by your side and at another time, the fire of his wrath will be by your side. But do not consider his wrath to be opposite of his grace. Look at the impacts of both as the same. At one time he makes you green like the green and great. Sometimes he makes the body of the seeker fertile enabling it to grow plants of fragrant flowers. This is seen and taken care of and felt by him alone and none else, just as the fragrance of paradise is felt by men of clean inside and none else. In order to feel the fragrance of the guide, keep your inside free from wrong thoughts about the guide. So also that, through a God’s friend you may feel the fragrance of paradise as the Prophet had said by referring to H. Uwaise Qarani, a saint from Yemen. The prophet had said: “I feel the fragrance of Benevolent God from Yeman’s side. [H. Uwaise had not seen the Prophet physically. He had not gone out of Yemen due to some personal problems. But through spiritual means he knew well about the prophet and become a devout Muslim]

sections.heading: Step by Step Progress
paras: If you stand in the ranks of those Mi‘rajis (elevated), quality of annihilation in God spread out its feathers just as the Burrāq had carried the prophet to heaven. This elevation is not like the going up of the dust upto the moon but like the elevation of the tasteless cane becoming sweet with sugar, as in sugar cane. It is not like the smoke going up to the sky and getting annihilated, but like the attainment of wisdom of a baby from mother’s womb to the highest level. [ For this, the baby has to enter into the world grow physically and mentally in a slow process, becoming wiser step by step in a slow and systematic manner until reaching complete adulthood]. The horse of annihilation (fanā) in God is a very good horse (burrāq). After annihilating you, it gives you an everlasting life (baqā). Its hoofs kick the oceans and mountains and ultimately leave behind every sensory thing of the world.

sections.heading: Spiritual Knowledge in the Ark
paras: Keep your steps in the ark and move on, just as the soul goes to the beloved; as the beloved is the soul of the soul. Your soul gets merged with the soul of the beloved. There is no role for the hands and feet in this journey as the soul had descended into this world from the world of non-existence (‘adam). This talk of elevation and descendance, annihilation and everlastingness tear off the curtains of wisdom and thinking. It cannot be understood through wisdom and argumentation. It is for the hearer with clean and clear ears both the physical ear and the internal spiritual ear. He has to hear carefully with all attention with the physical ear and then pass on to inner spiritual ear. O heavens! Pour the heavenly, spiritual pearls upon this discussion, and world of material possessions and worldly wisdom! Be ashamed of your lowly state. O heaven, if you pour your pearls, you will not be at loss. Your pearls will become six times more. And your non-living, dead contents will become great speakers and hearers. What all you pour upon this discussion is for yourself only, as your entire capital will increase by a hundred times, just as the case of that gift which queen Bilqīs of Sabā had sent to H. Sulaimān.

chapters.title: Queen of Sabā’s Gifts to H. Sulaimān
chapters.subtitle: Narrative of the sending of gift by queen Bilqīs of Sabā to H. Sulaimān

paras: Queen Bilqīs of sabā dispatched forty camels fully loaded with gold bricks to be presented to H. Sulaimān. When the caravan entered into H. Sulaimān’s territory, the entire land was found to be made of gold. The travelers went upto forty miday stations and found gold on the way to such an extent that the value of gold was entirely lost in their view. Many a times they discussed that they should go back with their gold as gold in their hands cannot be taken to the gold mine. They said: “We are engaged in a silly job. This region is made of pure gold and it is foolish to take gold here as gift”.

sections.heading: H. Sulaimān Had No Interest in Gold
paras: O the one taking the gift of wisdom before God! Wisdom is His path is lesser in value than its dust of its path. When the carriers of gold found out the worthlessness of the gift, they felt ashamed in carrying it forward and thought of going back. Then they thought: “What have we to do? No doubt, it is worthless and outdated. But we are servants of commands. Whether it is gold or mud, we have to carry it in obedience to the command of the master. If they say that we should take the gift we shall do it, but obey the command. Anyway, we have to carry the gift”. Without hesitation, they went fast towards the throne of the king of the world.

sections.heading: Do Not Give, but Take Gifts
paras: When H. Sulaimān looked at that gift, he laughed and said: “What had I asked you for was none other than the change of your faith. I had not asked you to give me a gift but I asked you to become capable of receiving the gift. I have received such wonderful gifts from the unseen (god) which a man cannot even think and hope of. You worship the star that makes gold. But look toward the One who makes the star. You worship the sun. by doing so, you disgrace your highly worthy life”.

sections.heading: Sun, a Servant of God
paras: Sun is a cook for us appointed by God, (which it does by bring about crops and grains and fruits). I make a fool of myself by considering it as God. What do you do when the sun gets into eclipse and becomes dark? How can that darkness goes, other than by pleading in the court of God to get rid of this again. When you get into troubles at mid night how can you complain to the sun and seek redressal when it is not there? Usually, great calamities come about during the night when your god is absent. There is no scope for your god’s help then.

sections.heading: Bow to God: See the Sun at Midnight
paras: On the contrary, if you bow down before God in sincerity, you get rid of the stars, and share god’s secret with God, and know of the affairs of the universe. If you do like this and become a sharer of God’s secret, I can speak to you, so that you may see the sun even at midnight. Clean soul has only the east with shining sun. there is no difference of day and night for its rise. Day is a duration when the sun is shining and so long as it is shinning there is no darkness and night. When the sun of Truth shines, there is no darkness any time; there is only brightness.

sections.heading: Sun’s Brightness, a Tiny Spark
paras: Just as a particle does not shine before the sun, so also the sun of this world does not shine before the radiance of the clean lights of Truth. Before that light, its eyes go blind and bewildered. You will see this sun as a tiny particle before the light of the dominant and limitless light of the imperium (‘arsh). But man’s eyes will see it as mean, humble, unstatic, when his weakness is provided with such might as to see that great light. It has an alchemy (chemical) that converts a cloud smoke into a star. It is such a wonderful chemical that when half of its spark fell on darkness, it got connected into sun. this is a wonderful chemist, who with his single act provides so many properties to Saturn in the glass house of the heavens. You may consider similarly in respect of other stars. The physical eyes are dominated over by the sun. therefore, go in search of God’s eyes, so that others including this bright sun may be dominated by you. The sun is nothing but a collection of sparks of light. [In today’s understanding the sun of full of energies of heat and light because of the nuclear conversation of Hydrogen, with One Proton into Helium, with two protons ― Translator]. This is because of the reason that the inner eyesight consists of godly light, but the external eyesight looks at light which is a product of heat. Fire becomes very dark before this light.

chapters.title: Spiritual Godly Light
chapters.subtitle: Miracles and light of shaikh ‘Abdullāh Maghribī. May his secrets remain pure

paras: H. Abdullāh Shaikh Maghribī said that: “he did not see the darkness of the night for sixty years. This was due to the mediocrity of my soul during both day and night”. Some sufi said that they would go behind him during the night time to test its veracity. They said: “He was proceeding like a full moon in a forest full of ditches and thorny bushes in front of us. Without turning behind, he used to tell us: “Be careful there is a ditch. Turn to left side. And after some time, he would say, turn to the right as there are thorns under the feet. When morning arrived, we kissed his feet, as they were totally clean of any dust. And his feet were clean like those of the bride. They did not have any mark of dust and mud nor of any injury of thorn pricks and injuries from stones. God made Maghribī (western) as Mashriqī (eastern). The west was converted into the light-giving east. The light of the sun of the suns was very bright. He was the care-taker of the elite and masses. How can that great light be not so, which can create thousands of suns. Go in full satisfaction with his light among the pythons and scorpions. The clean light moves forward and leads the seekers of Truth, and tears into pieces all the dacoits that come in the way. Consider this statement of God and read in the Qurān: ‘The day that God will not permit to be humiliate of the Prophet and those who believe with him. Their light will run forward before them and by their right hand, while they say: “Our Lord! Perfect our light for us and

sections.heading: Grant Us Forgiveness’ : “Yawma Lā Yukhzīl Lāhu Alnabiyyī Wa Allaziīna Āmaū Ma‘ahoo : Nūruhum Yas‘ā Baina Aidīhim Wa Bi-Aimānihim Yaqūlūna Rabbanā Atmim Lanā Nūranā
paras: waghfirlanā”: (Tahrim: 66: 8). Though this light increases on the doomsday, but in order to test it, you may ask for it from God. As He grants light of the soul to the non-living as well as to the mist. And God knows best those who recognize.

chapters.title: Greed in the First Trap in Life
chapters.subtitle: H. Sulaimān’s returning the messengers of Bilqīs with their gifts and his asking her to give up the worship of the sun and develop faith in God

paras: H. Sulaimān said to the hesitating messengers: “Gold is for you, but it is only the heart that is for us. Take gold from us also, and also keep it upon your gold. Keep this blindness of the body on the genital of the female zebra. [Female zebra generally dies while delivering its calf. Therefore, to avoid its pregnancy, the owners used to put a golden ring on its genital ― Qazi Sajjad Hussain]. Gold is worthy for the zebra’s genital. Lovers of God have faces of pale and yellow colour like gold. Because their faces are the observation points of God, just as a gold mine is the observation point of the sun, where is the observation point of the sun and where is that of God, the Master of all wise-men? Hold on to me and make me as your shield to protect you, even though, even now you are within my hold. Lover of the grains, the greedy bird is upon the terrace with open wings held within the trap.

sections.heading: Grain Also Watches Greedy Bird
paras: The moment it fell in love with the grain, it was trapped by its love, well before getting caught in the net. Consider the look that it casts upon the grain as the knot that it puts around its own feet. The grain says: “As you are stealthily looking at me, I am stealing your patience and peace of mind. When your right has dragged you toward me, do not think that I am ignorant of you and your desirers. When your right went after me, be sure to know that I am not unaware of you”.

chapters.title: Greed Finally Causes Faith
chapters.subtitle: Narrative of the grocer, the weights whose balance were made of clay; and a mud-eating buyer of sugar, stealing the clay from the weights, and the perfumer’s observing the theft but keeping quite

paras: A fellow in the habit eating clay went to a grocer to buy white, grainy, fine sugar. This grocer was a hypocrite and very cunning who had weights for his balance made of clay. He told that man: “O young man! My sugar, without any doubt is very fine, but the weights of my balance are made of clay. If you agree with this, you may buy my sugar”. The young man said: “I am in need of sugar for a purpose, whatever the weights of your balance may be made of”. Then he said to himself: “What is even a stone before a mud-eater? Mud is more tasty than sugar”. This was like a marriage broker woman who told a young man: “My son, I have found out a very beautiful bride for you. She is very grand, but there is one matter with her. She is seclusive and daughter of a sweet-meat-seller”. That young man said: “This is all the more better. His daughter will be very fatty and sweet”. The mud-eater told the grocer: “If you do not have a weight of stone, but of clay: it is all the more better and fine. Clay is a fruit of my heart”. The merchant kept the muddy weight in one of the pans of the balance with full confidence instead of the stoney one. And started breaking the sugar for the other pan of an equal weight. As he did not have a ready tool to break the sugar lump, he stood there for a long time, and made the buyer seated in wait. His face was turned toward the other side and the mud eater getting impatient started stealing the clay from the pan in fear that the shopkeeper might not come all of a sudden, and his eyes may not fall upon him in surprise. The grocer looked at this and kept himself all the more busy as though telling: “O yellow-faced-fellow: steal more mud. If you steal mud, you are causing your own loss. You feel afraid of me but I fear that you are eating very little. Though I am engaged otherwise, I am not a fool to see that you take more sugar from me. If you weigh the sugar later, you will know as to who was foolish and careless”.

sections.heading: Beauty Causes Love and Also Pangs
paras: The bird looks at the garden with much pleasure; and the grain also looks at it similarity from a distance. Though you are deriving pleasure by looking with crazy eyes upon a beautiful face you are actually eating your inside after roasting it. The impact of the beauty is causing distance in your inside. The ogling from a distance is like an arrow and poison for you. Your love for her increases and patience gets reduced. Wealth of the world is a net for the weak birds and the wealth of the next world is the net of the noble birds. So much so, there is a large net in this world. In which strange birds are caught. H. Sulaimān continued: “I am Sulaimān. I do not want your country, but I want to release you from all kinds of dangerous traps. Your worship of the sun is a deadly trap. As of now, you are the slaves of your wealthy country. But the real master of the country is the one who struggles and gets out of the deadly destructives. You are a prisoner and a salve of the country but you call yourself as its king and ruler. You are a slave of this world, which has enslaved your soul too. How long do you call yourself as its master”?

chapters.title: Worth and Pleasures of Worship
chapters.subtitle: H. Sulaimān pleading of the messengers and giving them gifts and eliminating their pains and anxieties and explaining of the reasons for the refusal of their gifts

paras: H. Sulaimān said: “O messenger of the Queen! I now make you as my messengers and send you to her. My rejection of the gift brought by you is better than my acceptance. Speak to Bilqīs of the strange things you saw about the forests of gold. That you moved upon gold upto forty midway stations. And also, how you felt ashamed of presenting such a gift to me. This is to make her know that we are not greedy of gold. We have carried gold from the producer of gold. Tell them that He is the one, who, if he wishes, can make all the mud of the earth into gold and precious pearls. “O desirous of gold! God will make this earth as silver on the doomsday. He says: “We are quite unconcerned with gold as we are experts in making these men made of mud into gold in entirety”. Where do we beg for gold from you? We can make you such, that you can become alchemists and makers of gold. Give up all this even if it is the country of Sabā, as there are many other worlds out of this world of water and mud. What you call as a throne is a yoke within which one is immobilized. What you consider as a place of command and control and capital of government is a place of the watchman.

sections.heading: Worship Itself Is an Empire
paras: You have no control upon your beard itself, but you claim yourself to be the commander of every good and bad things. Your beard becomes white without your intention and command. O man of crooked desires! You should be ashamed of your own disobedient beard. One who keeps his head before God is the mater of the country. Apart from this earthly world, he has hundreds of other countries under his command. But the taste of one prostration of God appears to be better than two hundred such countries. After such a prostration, you will cry upon these kingdoms and say that you do not want them, and pray to God to give you the kingdom of this prostration. Kings of this world, because of their bad nature, are deprived of the fragrance of the wine of subordination to God. As otherwise, like H. Ibrahim Ad-ham, they would have got disgusted and estranged, and given up the authority of kingship.

sections.heading: God Made Greedy to Rule upon Greedy
paras: But God, in order to sustain and continue this world has put a seal upon their eyes and mouths, so as to make the crown and throne sweet for them to feel proud of their collection of taxes from the worldly people. Even if you collect gold as much as heaps of sand, ultimately it passes on to others in inheritance. Kingdom and gold will not be the companion of your soul. Give them up and buy an eye black by applying which in your eyes, the world may appear worthless to you. So that, you may know that this world is narrow like a well, and think of holding a rope to go out of it as H. Yūsuf did, so that when you come out of it, your soul may exclaim in pleasure: “Ah there! Good news! Here is fine young man!”, just as the travellers of the caravan said when H. Yūsuf came out of the well.

sections.heading: Optical Illusions
paras: There are many reflections and optical illusions of the eye sight in the worldly well. The least of them is that, at its bottom, stone appear as gold. With immature brains and for fun, children while playing, see the pieces of earthen pots as goods and gold. Those gnostics of God, who understand God is the right manner become alchemists and makers gold to such an extent that gold mines lose all their wealth and value for them.

chapters.title: Search for Halāl Provisions
chapters.subtitle: A dervish’s seeing of a group of shaiķhs in his dream and requesting them for the provision of permissible halāl food on the ground that he gets deprived of worship in effort to earn; And then directing him towards the bitter and sour fruits on the hills and their becoming sweet under the guidance of those people

paras: One of the dervishes narrated an incident that: “I saw a group of saints hidden from the people like khizr, in my dream. I asked them as to from where I can get halāl food, which should not be hard to get. They took me towards a hill track and plucked fruits from the trees saying that God has made these fruits sweet for your mouth under the impression of our concentration. This is a halāl, clean and unlimited food for you. You can eat them without any trouble of putting efforts here and there. And with this food there came about such strength to talk that the taste of talks baffled the wise. I said to the Lord of the world: this is putting me in a trial. Give me a grant which should be hidden from the people. I lost my capacity to talk and I felt quite contented. With the pleasure of this taste, I laugh like a ripe, split up pomegranate. I said to myself: “there cannot be anything else in paradise which has entered into my nature. I cannot now have a desire for anything else. I shall not ignore this and look toward sugarcane and apricots. A little of my earlier earning has remained with me, which I had kept stitched in my sleeve”.

chapters.title: Kings of the Other World
chapters.subtitle: The dervish’s thinking of that left over little money to be given to a wood cutter, as he did not need it anymore with the miracles of those great guides; And the saintly wood cutter’s feeling unhappy at his thoughts

paras: There came one fire wood collection dervish to the forest, very tired and weak. I thought within myself: “I am now not in need of making a livelihood. Later also, I need not worry for it. Untasty fruits have become sweet for me. This is like a royal food for my body. As I do not have to bother about my food, a few small coins that I have can be given to him. Let me give this little wealth to this man so that he may remain satiated for two-three days”. That man came to know of what was going on in my mind, as the lamp had in it the light of God. The secret of every thought for him was, like a lamp within a glass chimney. Nothing from my heart remained hidden from him. He was well aware of every thing of my heart. In response to my thoughts, that man of strange thoughts, murmured something slowly within himself: “You think like this in respect of the kings! It is they, who provide food to you through their blessings. Who else can provide for you other than them? I could not understand the words that he murmured, but the impacts of disapproval were felt by my heart. He came toward me like a frightening lion, kept the bundle of firewood under him. The way in which he kept the bundle of firewood caused shivering in all the seven parts of my body (two hands, two legs, chest, back and head). And he said: “O my Lord! If your special servants are alive and are prosperous blessers with pleasing steps, I seek that benevolence from You, which should become an alchemy”. Instantly the bundle of firewood became one of gold. I saw that very moment, that firewood has become gold, shining in all brilliance as fire. I fell down unconscious for sometime and after some time came to normalcy. Then he said: “O God! If those great men are very self-respecting and are runners away from publicity, then You may make this into a bundle of firewood”. It became firewood instantly as it was earlier. Instantly, those branches of the tree from gold were converted into firewood. At this, my wisdom and observing capacity go baffled. After this, he lifted the bundle of firewood and left with hop and fast steps towards the city. I thought of going after that great king and put some questions of intricate matters to him and hear the answers. But I was under a terrible state because of the grandeur of that great man. I felt my feet bounded.

sections.heading: Different Ways for Different People
paras: There is a different way to go before the common and special people, excepting when they, on their own, extend invitation. In such a case surrender yourself to them, as it is with their mercy and absorption. Consider such a support from them as very opportune, when those at the top level of closeness to God, called siddīq’s, are about to be close to you. Not like the fool who immediately after becoming close to such a king, slowly and silently goes astray, just as a fellow was granted the thigh of a fat sacrificed sheep, as against others, who were given other parts; and this thankless fellow started saying that it may be the thigh of a cow, as he had not seen such fatty thigh earlier. O blabberer of falsehood, this is not a thigh of the cow! It is appearing to be so because of your foolishness as of an ass. These great gifts are given by the kings of the other world without expecting anything in return from you. This is their affection and pure grants.

chapters.title: H. Sulaimān’s Greed to Spread Goodness
chapters.subtitle: H. Sulaimān’s greed to hasten the return of the messengers to bring back Bilqīs soon for the sake of faith

paras: This affection is like the dragging of Bilqīs and her armies towards himself in a battle saying: “My dear ones! Come fast towards me as the waves in the ocean of generosity are rising high, spilling without any reluctance. O recipients of guidance! We have made an open invitation to you as Ridhwān, the gate-keeper of paradise has opened up its doors”. He further said: “O messanger! Go fast towards Bilqīs and tell her to fall in love with my religion and again tell her followers also to come here as God has invited them all with perfect security and peace. Tell them all: “O seekers of wealth come fast as the doors of grants are fully open now. Come forward: even those who do not want this wealth, as by coming here, the craze for this wealth will come into you also to seek from all honest, faithful friend. You may say good-bye to your kingdom. Just as Ibrahim Ad-ham did, so as to get the rulership of the everlasting kingdom”.

chapters.title: Sound of Drums upon H. Ibrahim Ad-Ham
chapters.subtitle: Reasons for H. Ibrahim Ad-ham’s giving up of the kingdom of Khorasan and migration

sections.heading: Impacts of Sounds and Music on Souls
paras: One night, that king was sleeping on his throne and the guards were watchful on the terrace. The intention if that king in keeping the guards was not to seek protection from thieves and drunken fellows. He knew well that he was just, and as such his heart was fully at rest at the occurrence of any unwanted event. In fact, justice is the guard of all objects and jobs, and not the beating of the drummers upon the terrace. But he, like sufi’s had the object of the hearing of the sound of rabab only to get remained of the sounds of Alast, that came about before the beginning of the world and made before God by the souls of all humans.

sections.heading: Music Originated from Where
paras: Sounds of the large pipe and drum appears to them as the sounds of Isrāfil’s bugle of the doomsday. Philosophers say that the tunes of musical instruments are taken from the sounds created by the revolutions of the heavens. [Mathematician and Philosopher Phythagorus (540 – 510 BC) has said that there are twelve locations in twelve sings of the Zodiac, seven sounds from the seven stars known at that time (Sum, Moon, Mercury, Venus, Mars, Jupiter, Saturn, which were supposed to be orbiting the earth); twenty-four compositions of the day and night; and forty-eight during every week of the year ― Qazi Sajjad Hussain]. It is the sound of the revolutions of the sky that musicians produce through their mouths and instruments. Some say that models of these heavenly sounds penetrate into our throats and instruments through the medium of air. The faithfuls say that all these tunes are converted from our rough sounds into pleasing sounds of the impacts of the songs of the houries, flowing waters of the streams and clappings of the leaves of the trees of paradise. We were all parts of the body of H. Ādam and we have heard all these tunes when he was in paradise. Though water and mud, of which we are made have put us in doubts, yet sometimes a little of these are recalled to our memory. But as these tunes heard by us got mixed up with mud, their high pitch and low pitch do not give that pleasure as the original ones of the paradise give.

sections.heading: Impacts of Music upon Lovers
paras: This is the water getting polluted with urine and filth, which have spoiled its purity and made it acidic, yet this polluted water has its original qualities. Even urine, which contains water extinguishes fire when poured upon it. Similarly, the impacts of the paradisiacal tunes do have some effects that they extinguish the fires of sorrows and anxieties of the heart. This is the reason why music becomes the food of those in love as it rouses the thoughts of the meeting with the beloved. This happens in both the cases of the lovers of worldly objects as well as of God. His thoughts get strengthened; rather the instrumental tunes and oral sounds and words provide physical shape. The fire of love increases and sharpens just as the thirst of a thirsty man increases with the sound produced by the apricots falling in water.

chapters.title: Dropping of Apricot on Water
chapters.subtitle: Story of a thirsty man, who was dropping apricots from atop the tree on the water in a deep unreachable pit to hear the sounds of its falling in water which caused a rhythm for him and exited him.

paras: A thirsty man climbed upon an apricot tree, plucked and threw apricot in a deep pit containing little water. It was in such depth that he would not reach the water. Apricots fill in water, produced a sound and created bubbles. A wise man passing by said: “Stop this young man! Apricots will make you thirsty. Many fruits that fall in water go away from you in the depths of water. See here, many of your apricots are falling in water and water drags them inside. What is the gain for you? Until and unless you come down from the tree, water would cause your apricots to disappear.

sections.heading: Acts with Ulterior Objects
paras: The young man said: “With this dropping. My object is not to gather apricots. Observe this act carefully and do not keep yourself at the apparent. My object is to hear the sound of water and see bubbles on water. What else can a thirsty man do in the world other than moving around the water tanks. He moves around streams of water holes and the sounds of water just as a haji moves around the Ka‘abā. In similar manner, O Husamuddin, you are the object of this math(s)navi. I seek you and your support. I rely upon grants and support. The Math(s)navi moves towards your flag with its roots and branches. Rise and fall of this math(s)navi is within your authority and you have accepted it. Kings accept whatever is gifted to them, whether they are worthy or not; once they accept, they do not throw them away. You have sown the seedling and now supply water to it. When you have provided an expansion of heart, open up all the upcoming knots. My object through these words is to bring both your hidden affairs. I write them to hear your voice through them. What I am writing is what you are speaking about.

sections.heading: Man, Non-Man and Ape
paras: Your voice for me is the voice of God, as you, being a love of God are not different from Him. Unification with God is something which cannot be explained. It only be understood. This unification with God is not with anything other than man, and not with the non-man looking like man, I am saying non-man, and not ape. Not even the man for whom God is only a lord (Rabbianna). They cannot understand any other attributes of God. The real man is none other than the one who recognizes the soul; rather the soul of the soul. There are many men. But they are only physical men, only to look at. They are not real men. You have not spent a few moments to understand the secret of man. You are only like a living statue caught in meaningless speculations. You have not even cared to understand the meaning of:

sections.heading: “You Did Not Throw, but God Threw” : “Mā Ramaita Izramaita Walā Kinnallāha Ramā”:
paras: (Anfaal: 8: 17). [ This refers to the Prophets throwing of dust towards the army of the Makkan kafirs at the beginning of the battle at Badr. This had a great psychological effect on them that they felt disheartened, confused and frightened. On the contrary, it emboldened encouraged and enthused the Muslims. God’s saying: you did not throw, but God threw refers to God’s action through the agency of man]

sections.heading: Deliberate Deniers
paras: The land of your body is like the kingdom of Bilqīs. She gave it up for the sake of H. Sulaimān. You may also do likewise as the kingdom of H. Sulaimān was not this material world but the spiritual world of God. O Husamuddin! I feel disgusted with those who do not recognize the worth of this great work of Math(s)navi. I say: Lā howla (I do not care), not upon what I am saying, but upon him who suffers from strange meaningless insinuations. He makes unnecessary speculations upon my saying instead of going deep to understand the meanings. He has only insinuations deliberate rejections and unwanted speculations. When this is the situation of that fellow, there is no remedy but to say Lā hawla and keep quiet; particularly when opposition are coming into the mind, (and not mouths). As my words, O Husamuddin, are stuck up in your throat and do not come out, I become silent. I do not want to say anymore. You alone may say, it you want.

chapters.title: Annoyance Caused by Incompetents
chapters.subtitle: In the explanation of a piper who farted while playing pipe and kept his pipe on the backside saying: take it yourself if you can play better

paras: A piper was playing his pipe well. Suddenly he farted and the sound of his farting annoyed and angered whim. He kept down his pipe, sat upon it and said: “If you can play the pipe with your own better, take it and play with it”.

chapters.title: Decent Behavior with Indecent
chapters.subtitle: Bearing with indecent behaviors of men and being soft and considerate for them

paras: O muslim! Maintain decency in the seeking of guidance towards the path of goodness. And also, you have to bear with the indecency of the indecent fellows. When you see someone saying that so and so is an ill-natured fellow in bad habits, consider him to be of bad habits as it is out of his bad nature that he speaks ill of others. A man of good habits remains away from bad people, and when he goes nearby to them, bears with their indecency.

sections.heading: Resentment of Guides with Disciples
paras: But your guide sometimes complains against you, but it is not due to anger, disagreement, and personal ill will. It is not a complaint, but an effort to train up and clean the spirit, as have been the grievances made by the prophets. Consider their non bearing of the misconduct of their people as one in accordance with the will of God, as otherwise their capacity to bear with and forgive wrongs in firm in them. They have crushed their instinct of non-bearing with vices and maintained self-composure. If they have deviated from this fore bearing, it is a godly act. O Sulaimān! You know well the difference between the crow and the falcon. You have got the capacity to understand the words of the birds as a special miracle from God. Be well with all the birds: good and bad. Bulbul is very talkative. Do not get disgusted of its much talking. Do not be angry with it and snatch its feathers. So also do not thrash the falcon and chakor. This applies to hundreds of disciples of the shaikhs who miscalculate their inner qualities and greatness like Bilqīs, who miscalculated that H. Sulaimān would be pleased with gold. Remember: when the noble Prophet was injured in the battle of Uhad, he had prayed to God: “O God! Show guidance to my people as they do not have any knowledge”:

sections.heading: “Allāhumma Ihdi Qawmi, Fa Innahum Lā Ya‘lamūn”

chapters.title: God Is in Everything
chapters.subtitle: H. Sulaimān’s warning to Bilqīs to stop bringing partners with God and to migrate from her country to attain faith in God

paras: Be careful O Bilqīs! Come to me, as otherwise you will be in difficulties. Your army will become your enemy and turn against you. Your guards will pull down your doors. Your life itself will become your enemy. All particles of the earth and heaven are the armies of God to put you under trial.

sections.heading: Non-Living Armies of God
paras: You have seen the wind as it did with the people of ‘Aad. As the Qurān says: “And the ‘Aad – They were destroyed by a furious wind, exceedingly violent”: “Wa ammā ‘Aadun fa uhlikū

sections.heading: Bi Rīhin Sarsarin ‘Ātiyatin”: (Haqqah: 69: 6)
paras: You have seen water as to what it did through the floor (during the days of H. Nooh). [ As the Qurān says: “We over whelmed in the flood those who rejected our sighs”: “Wa

sections.heading: Aghraqnā Allazīna Kazzabū Bi Āyātinā”: (A‘raaf: 7: 64)
paras: See what violent river did to attack Pharaoh. As the Qurān says: “Then Pharaoh pursued them with his forces but the waters completely over whelmed them and covered

sections.heading: Them Up”: “Fa Atba‘ahum Fir‘awnu Bijunūdihī Faghashiahum Minal Yammi Mā
paras: ghashiyahum”: (Taaha: 20: 78) See also as to what earth did with Qārūn. He was swallowed by the earth, as the Qurān says: “Then we caused the earth to swallow him up”: “Fakhasafnā bihī wa

sections.heading: Bidaarihil Aradha”: (Qasas: 28: 81)
paras: And what God did by sending a flight of birds upon the elephants of Abraha, the Abyssinian who had come to demolish Ka‘abā at Makka. This is explained in detail in surah Fīl (ch: 105). And also, what a mosquito did by entering into the skull of Nimrod. H. Dawood threw three stones upon his enemies with his hand which broke into three hundred pieces and defeated them. Similarly, stones were rained upon the enemies of H. Loot and they dived into the black waters; as the Qurān says: “To bring on them a shower of stones of clay”:

sections.heading: Linursila ‘Alaihim Hijā Ratan Min Tīn”: (Alzurriyaat: 51: 33) Man’s Limbs Are His Army
paras: If I narrate the support given to the prophets by the non-living matters of the world, this Math(s)navi will become so voluminous that even forty camels will be disabled from carrying its weight. The hands themselves of the infidels will stand as witness against them, standing as an army of God, obedient to Him. As the Qurān says: “That day shall we set a seal on their feet bear witness, to all that they did”: “Al-Yawma nakhtimu ‘alā afwāhihim

sections.heading: Wa Tukallimunā Aidīhim Wat Ash-Hadu Arjuluhum Bimā Kānū Yaksibāna”: (Yasin: 36:
paras: 65) O the one in opposition to God in his acts and words! Know that you are in the midst of His armies. Every part of your body is an army of God. Working in unison. They are obedient to you in their respective acts. If God tells your eyes to trouble you, they go in pain and cause hundred calamities to you. If He tells your teeth to trouble you, you will get terrible pain as punishment. Read the book of medicine and read the chapter on pathology to know about the activities of the every part of your body is the same. It is not easy to maintain enmity with these lives. You cannot get rid of their troubles. Leave aside the armies of devils and fairies that are out of your body. Consider the armies of God within your soul itself that are making serious attacks on you (your body) from inside in the form of various diseases. “O Bilqīs! Give up your kingdom and come over to me! If you happen to join with me, you will become the owner of all kingdoms. If you come over to me, you will know that earlier you were like a picture drawn on the walls of public baths, which is lifeless. [ This refers to the culture of painting of pictures on the walls of public baths]. These pictures, whether of a king or a rich man, are just paintings, without any life and pleasures of life. They are decorations for others, who feel pleased and gape at them with open eyes and mouths”.

sections.heading: Man Cannot Live Alone
paras: As a man, you have kept yourself in battles with yourself. You do not consider yourself as one like yourself but consider yourself as superior to others. You identify yourself with whatever that pleases you and swear that you are with it and all others are not. You consider yourself to be very near to God as against others and also that being in this state, you have nothing to do with others. But, if you remain away from others for some time, you will come to know of the disgustion of loneliness and feel yourself in grief and anxieties. You will know how much you are in relationship with other creatures.

sections.heading: Man, Not Different from God
paras: You think that you are a worshipper of God. This means that you have marked yourself and God as different. You do not realize that you are an exposition of that singularity. He is exhibiting Himself through you. But without knowing this you consider yourself alone as good, beautiful and lovable, and in love with Him. You are a bird on your own, your own net and your own hunter. You are the throne; you are the floor and you are the terrace. That is; you are the clay, the earthen pot and the potter and in the end, you alone are its buyer.

sections.heading: Man’s Heart Greater Than World
paras: God alone is the substance, who is subsisting, on His own, and what all that come out of Him are his accidents. He is the Absolute and everything else is His offshoot and connected and dependent upon Him. You are a descendent of H. Ādam, and like him, see every particle of everything within yourself as H. Ādam used to do. Because, he had understood the reality of all outer things and of God. What all is there in the stream is in the pot also. Whatever is there in the house is also there in the city. This world is like a pot and man’s heart is like the stream. This world is just a small house and man’s heart is a city full of wonders. Man’s heart is a larger world than the entire world, which is but very small in comparison with the heart.

chapters.title: Reasons for H. Sulaimān’s Concern
chapters.subtitle: Explanation by H. Sulaimān to Bilqīs that efforts to bring her to faith are purely sincere upon the command of God. He does not have an iota of concern for her beauty, shape and her country. When the eyes of your soul open with the light of God, you will know the Truth of all this

paras: Be warned O Bilqīs! I am an inviting prophet! Just like death destroys all passions so also, I have crushed all passions. I am not obedient to lust. And, if I have lust, I am a ruler upon it and have command over it. I am not a prisoner of lust and beautiful idols. I am not inviting you to meet my lust as you may feel, as you are a woman. The prophets, as men have inclination toward women, but they are not obedient to them. My base is on idol breaking. Like the Truthful H. Ibrahim and all other prophets. If I, as a prophet enter into an idol home on my way, the idols fall in prostration before me. Both H. Muhammad and Abu Jahal entered into the idol home. But there is a great difference in their entrance. H. Muhammad entered and the idols kept their heads before him, and when Abu Jahal entered, he kept his head before them.

sections.heading: Controller of Lust, Controlled by Lust
paras: This world is an idol home of lust. It is a nest in which both prophets and infidels live. But lust is obedient and submissive to the noble people. Pure gold does not burn out in the fire pit but comes out brighter. Idol worshippers are impure, and noble people are like pure gold. Both of them are in this furnace. But when the impure gold enters into it, it becomes black, but pure gold brightly exposes its goldenness. As soon as gold enters into the goldsmiths smelting pit, it brightly laughs like the sun.

sections.heading: Body: a Curtain, Hiding Truth
paras: Our body is like a curtain in the world and we are hidden in river water under the curtain of grass on its surface. Do not look at the king of faith as mud, as such a look was cast on H. Ādam by Devil. Ordinary people remain hidden in water under the grassy surface of water. But that is not so with the prophets with spiritual powers. They are like the bright sun which cannot be smeared with a handful of dust. Even if you smear it with a hundred layers of dust and ash, it will tear them off and its light will flash out. What after all is a scrap of grass to hide the face of water. What is the worth of mud to hide the face of sun. Get up, O Bilqīs1 like Ibrahim Ad-ham and set fire, and smoke out this kingdom of three-four days. Let me speak out about the affairs of Ibrahim Ad-ham at this point to show as to what was the reason of his giving up his kingdom.

chapters.title: Ibrahīm Ad-Ham’s Narrative Continued
chapters.subtitle: Left over narrative of H. Ibrahīm Ad-ham. May his sou; be refreshed

paras: H. Ibrahīm was upon his throne at night when he heard sounds of falling steps and people’s talks upon the terrace of the palace. He said to himself: who is so bold to do like this? He thought; it cannot be a man. It must be some ghost. He called out from the window as to who was there. Some strange people lowered their heads and said: “We are searching for camels”. He said: “Who has ever searched for a camel on the terrace?” Then they said: “Then how are you trying to meet God while you are holding a great status, and sitting upon the throne?”

sections.heading: Strange Talks About the Unseen
paras: This happened, and thereafter nobody saw him. He disappeared like a fairy. His inner qualities were hidden, but he was before them in his body. People do not see things other than beard and torne clothes to identify a saintly person. When H. Ibrahim Ad-ham disappeared from the people’s sight, he became famous like ‘Anqaa’, the invisible bird. The soul of the large bird ‘Seemurgh’, went towards the Caucasus Mountain. People all over started talking this and that about it. This is how people value unseen things. Similarly, when the light of H. Sulaimān from the east, where H. Sulaimān ruled (Palestine), went towards Sabā, there was a great hullabaloo among the people and Bilqīs. All dead men woke up and their souls started flying in the air. They were giving the good news to each other that; sounds are coming from the heavens. These sounds strengthen the faiths of all; and the branches and leaves of the heart become green. H. Sulaimān’s message was like the bulge of Isrāfīl, which raises the dead from the graves. This is a good and fortunate information for you. What is known about the affairs of H. Sulaimān has been explained here. These incidents have passed. God only knows about these events in certainty.

chapters.title: Talk to the People as per Their Capacities
chapters.subtitle: Rest of the narrative of the people of Sabā and H. Sulaimān’s advice and guidance to the followers of Bilqīs in accordance with their understanding as a bird catcher catches the birds in accordance with their sounds and choice of food.

sections.heading: People Condemn Even Generosity
paras: I enthusiastically narrate to you the affairs of the people of Sabā, when the message of H. Sulaimān reached the fertile land of Sabā. Their bodies which were deprived of souls got mixed up with the souls, as though separated children rejoined their parents. Lovers remain hidden from the people. Generous people show generosity and distribute their wealth to the poor, which gets hidden behind the remarks of the people calling it extravagance, in condemnation. They frighten them also of ensuring poverty with loss of money. Souls are covered up and hidden by the bodies and remain disgraced. But when they defeat and dominate the bodies, they become honourable. Those in love remain satisfied with love. Whatever the result, they last forever, and ever remembered. Those deprived of love should get up and prepare themselves to feel the fragrance of H. Yūsuf.

sections.heading: Teach About What Is Needed
paras: H. Sulaimān know the language of the birds. He could talk to each bird in its language and speak to it as per its capacity to understand matters. When God taught him the language of birds, He also taught him about their skills and capacities. Teach the bird which believes in fate (predestination) about the losses of this belief and prepare them to put efforts. Give the lessons of patience to the birds with wounded wings. Keep a patient bird in good books and show forgiveness. Show the directions of Caucasus Mountain to Aaqaa to proceed. Teach the pigeon to learn the lessons to protect itself from the falcon and teach the falcon to maintain dignity and self-control. Make the helpless bat deprived of possessions, to become a friend of light. Teach the lessons of maintaining peace to the quarrelsome chakor and to the roosters the marks of the early morning, you may proceed from the hoopie to the level of eagle. Thus, guide them in the appropriate manner, as God knows best.

chapters.title: Bilqīs’s Love for Throne
chapters.subtitle: Bilqīs’s freedom from her kingdom, getting intoxicated with the pleasures of faith and leaving of all possessions excepting her throne and consequent stoppage of inner impacts

paras: When H. Sulaimān whistled with the message of God at the birds of Sabā, he tied them all, expecting those which were lifeless and featherless. Or, those who were deaf and dumb by birth like the fishes. I am sorry! What I said is wrong, because if a deaf fellow keeps his head before God’s inspiration, God’s inspiration will grant him also the capacity to hear.

sections.heading: Love Changes Attitudes
paras: As Bilqīs had made a determination with all heart and soul and also regretted upon her earlier misguidance of star-worship, she gave up her wealth and kingdom in such a way as the lovers give up their concern for name and disgrace. Those well brought up slaves and maids appeared like rotton onions to her. Gardens, forts and streams of water appeared as furnaces out of love for the faith. When man is overtaken by love and anger, he finds good things bad and worthless. Gems appear like grains of corn. This is the impact and honour of love. This is the meaning of ‘No’ (Lā). That is, when faith in God comes, all things cease to have any meaning and worth. And thereupon this, the phrase: “No god but He (Allāh)” ( Lā ilāha illa huwa) comes to his mind. Everything else appears worthless. And moon appears like a blackened Cauldron.

sections.heading: Man’s Love for Material Companions
paras: Bilqīs had regret in giving up everything: possession, treasury and all articles excepting her throne to lose which she felt sorry. And H. Sulaimān came to know of her feelings as there was a way from his heart to her heart. He was the One who had heard the sound of an ant and the secrets of those far far away. He had heard the voice of the ant which had told its companion that H. Sulaimān and his troops are coming on their way and they might crush them under their feet; and they should protect themselves in their holes. He came to know of this and also of that ancient arch of the sky. He saw from a long distance that lady who had developed faith in God and consonance with Him, but was feeling much for separation from her throne. If I tell you the reason of her love and devotion to the throne, it will be a very lengthy discussion. Though the nib and the pen have no sense and life, as they are not of the genus of the writer, yet they are the writer’s companions and dear friends. They cannot be separated. Similarly, the fools of every artizan have no life but are his companions and lovable friends of the living being. I could have explained the reasons behind this aspect in detail; if the eyes of your understanding had been clean.

sections.heading: Worldly Connections Go Slowly in God’s Love
paras: Bilqīs did not carry the throne along with her as it was very large. She could not dissemble it to carry as it was so finely crafted that dissembling would ruin its beauty. Its parts were so linked with each other as parts of a living body. H. Sulaimān said to himself: For the present she has infatuation for the throne, but as she gets elevated in spiritual attainments, she will totally forget the throne and crown. Some margin has to be given to past undesirable connection for the time being. When man gets merged with God and becomes one with Him, he ceases to have his own existence and starts to live in everlasting God. That is: he first attains fanā and later attains baqā. At this state, the grandeur and worth of bodies and materials lose their value with their connection with the grandeur of God. When pearls are extracted from the ocean, nobody looks at the dust, rubble and rubbish floating on it. When the flames-throwing sun rises, the tail of the constellation, Scorpio goes out of sight. Anyway, at this stage of the transfer of her body and soul, the transfer of the throne is also required, so that at the time of her meeting with me, she should not have distraction in her heart. This childish need must be met with.

sections.heading: Old Connections Increase New States
paras: This is very easy for me to do but very dear for her, as it happens that on the dining sheet of the fairies, ghosts also sit for dining. Further this throne will be an article from which to learn lessons [Just as Ayāz, the slave of king Mahmood Ghaznavī inspite of his elevation to high level and of being the closest confident of the king, used to look at his country made footwear and old trone clothes every day, which he had kept in the treasury to recall his old days of poverty and learn lessons from and thank God and the king for his elevation]. Her throne would make her remember how she had been under trials and misguidance earlier, and to which high state she got elevated.

sections.heading: Evolution of Man from Mud Onwards
paras: Man has also elevated from the lowly state of mud, and gradually elevated to the forms of sperm, clot of congealed blood, then into lump, then made into bones, clothed the bones with flesh and then developed into a full-fledged man. (Almu‘minūm: 23: 14). These examples have been placed before us by God to say: O ill-intentioned fellow, see from where I have brought you to where. You should be ashamed of your present status and ashamed of earlier status. These grants were given to you in order to eliminate the sense of shame which you had as lowly mud. You had refused to rise up with the inert property of mud. When you were converted from lowly, but living sperm. You got the capacity of progress, which God provided. Your birth as man, became evidence of your earlier refusal to grow from muddy state. This evolution from earth to man through different intermediate states should have made you thankful to God. This evolution was a medicine to cure your inertness as mud. But having become man you became more thankless, which became a disease of yours. Mud, certainly does not posses this quarrelsomeness and refusing power. At that stage of mud, you were without head and heart and therefore you did not have thinking, and therefore capacity of rejection.

sections.heading: Man Has Further States of Progress
paras: So long as you were a non-living mud, you refused to go on the line of progress and evolution. And progress from human body to spirit, it indicated that you still continue to be in the state of mud. Your case is like that of a man who taps the door from outside, but the owner of the house says from inside that he is not there. The door tapper will understand from the owner’s denial that he is very much inside, and will never give up tapping. His denial itself is a proof of his being inside. By your very change from one state to another in the womb and subsequent changes upon coming out, indicates that one state ends and gets finished and another new one comes. This itself is a good example of rebirth after death or raising of the dead on the doomsday.

sections.heading: What Chemical Reaction Created Life?
paras: From your evolution form the stage of mud to the stage of your denial of rebirth, there have been many creations and deaths. Surah Al Insān or Al dahr (S. 76 of the Qurān) clearly speaks of what I said: “Man, over a long period of time was nothing and unmentionable. God created him from a drop of mingled sperm to try him and gave him the gifts of hearing and sight. God showed him the way to see whether he would be grateful or ungrateful”. (Free translation of the first two ayats) Water and mud coming together do say that there is no denial. They say through their activity that they are alive when they are together by bringing forth various forms of life; and when they separated, they become dead; and again, when they come together, they become alive. But after attaining the highest possible level man says: “No. There is no rebirth. I can explain this in a hundred ways, with very subtle fine and refined references, but the ill-witted stumble in catching the point. Therefore, I resort to silence on this matter to proceed from Sabā to the transfer of the throne of Bilqīs.

chapters.title: Effort to Bring the Throne
chapters.subtitle: H. Sulaimān’s effort to bring the throne of Bilqīs, well before her arrival

paras: H. Sulaimān said to his people that her throne should be brought there fast. A very tricky Jinn, said he would bring it by design well before the dispersal of the gathering. His minister, Āsif bin Barkhia said that he would present it before him in a moment with the power of Ism I-A‘zam (great name of God). Though the jinn was a great master magician but the throne came over there with Āsif’s breath of the great name. the throne came to their presence instantly by the act of Āsif and not of the designs of the jinns.

sections.heading: Miracles, as Observed by Worshippers
paras: H. Sulaimān said: “May the praise of God be upon this and a hundred graces of God upon it, which I have seen earlier”. Then, he looked at the throne and said: “O fools fall before sculptured stones and engraved wood. Both the prostrator and the prostrated are unaware of life and soul having seen only a little impact and few acts of the soul in craftsmanship. Sometimes, when the prostrator was flabbergasted and caught in amazement, he sees the stone making gestures and speaking. As he played the game of dice of service with it in inappropriate manner, the unfortunate fellow mistook the carved-out lion as real. God, the Real Lion, showed His generosity to please him, He threw a bone before the doggish idol to show a strange act, saying: “Though this dog is not on the right path, but throwing bones is our usual grace”.

chapters.title: Foster-Mother, Haleemā’s Prostration to Idols
chapters.subtitle: Narrative of H. Haleemā, foster mother of the prophet who after fosterage, had lost him and shivered and prostrated to the idols; and their giving evidence of the greatness of the prophet’s works

paras: I tell you the narrative of the secret of H.Haleemā, the Prophet’s foster-mother, so that this narrative may eliminate your grief. When the fosterage of the prophet was stopped, she carried him on her palm, like rose on stalk. She protected him from all good and bad to hand this emperor over to his grandfather, H. Abdul Mutallib. When she brought this great trust, she was in fears and entered into the precincts of the Ka‘abā and Hatīm. She heard a voice in the air: “O Hatīm; a very great sun shines upon you. Lakhs of suns of the light of generosity will come upon you today. That great grand king, whose ambassador is a great fortune, is bringing his gifts to you. O Hatīm; certainly, you are going to see the descendance of H. Jibra’il once again and you will become the destination of elevated souls. Souls of the clean people in groups and batches in all enthusiasm from all directions will enter into you”. H. Haleemā was taken aback upon this voice, as there was none before and behind her. All the six dimensions were empty of men and this voice continuingly coming and she was making intentions sacrifice herself upon it. She seated H. Mustafa on the ground to find out the source of that pleasing voice, which was revealing the mysteries of his prophethood. She was looking in all directions to find out the king who was revealing the secrets. Oh God! Such loud voice is coming from right and left but where is the one who is sending the message? When she could not see, she became very anxious; and losing all hopes, she started shivering like a thin cane. The she came back to that guiding child and did not see H. Mustafa in that place. Anxieties upon anxieties fell upon her; and with grief she felt darkness all around. She ran towards the houses nearby shouting as to who looted my pearl. The people of Makka said: “We donot know. We did not even know whether there was a child there”. She wept so much and lamented that, others too started weeping. She went on beating her chest and crying so much that others also started crying.

chapters.title: Seeking Guidance from Idols
chapters.subtitle: Narrative of an elderly Arab who directed her to seek help from the idols

paras: An elderly man walking with the support of a staff came over to her and asked: “O Haleemā! What has happened to you that you have set such fire from your heart, that other hearts have burnt out in grief?” She said: “I have been the foster-mother of Ahmed. I had brought him here to be handed over to his grandfather. When I entered into the Hatīm, I heard many voices in the air. I heard so many voices that I seated the child on the floor to find out as to whose voices they were, as those voices were very fine and pleasing. I did not find any mark of anyone on any side. Also, the voices did not stop for a moment. After searching everywhere in utter surprise, I returned to the place but to the great grief of my heart, I did not find him”.

sections.heading: To Seek the Help of Idols
paras: The old man told her: “Do not grieve my dear child! I shall point out to you of one kingly friend. If he wills, he will inform you about the child, as he knows very well the path in which the child has passed and as to where he has reached”. Then Haleemā said: “Please tell me. I shall sacrifice my life for you; O elderly man of good conduct and voice! Point out to me that great king, who is aware of my childs whereabouts”. He took her to the Makka’s well known idol ‘Uzza saying: “he is reliable in giving the information about hidden matters. Whenever we have come to him with faith in him, we have got back thousands of lost things”. The old man fell down before the idol and said: “O God of the Arabs! O ocean of grace! O ‘Uzza! You have shown many graces. You have released us from many nets. Arabs have a duty to honour you and the right to get your graces, so much, that they have become obedient to you. This Haleemā Sa‘adia, with full hopes upon you has come under the shadow of your cane. A young child of hers is lost and his name is Muhammed”.

sections.heading: Muhammed’s Name Frightens the Idol
paras: As soon as the name Muhammed was taken by him, all the idols there fell down upon their faces in prostration and said: “O old man! go away! What is this searching of that Muhammed, who is the cause of our downfall. Because of him, we fall down and hit with stones. We have become defective and fake. All those imaginary incidents that the idol worshippers and lustful fellows have seen in us during the period from the crucifixion of Jesus to the prophethood of Muhammed (Farrat) will vanish from their minds, as the time of the holding of his great count has arrived. Tayammum (ablution with clay) comes to an end, when water becomes available. Go away, you old man! Do not create mischiefs. Be careful not to rouse our jealousy for Ahmed. Go away, you old man for the sake of God, so that you may also not burn in fire just as we are to burn under the decision of God. What is it, you are pressing the tail of the python? Do you know as to what news you have brought for us? Oceans and deep mines have gone panicky at this news and all the seven heavens are in shivers”.

sections.heading: Strange Development at Hatīm
paras: When the old man heard these words from the stone, he threw away his staff. With those sounds, fears and shivering he got so frightened that his teeth rattled. He was shivering like a naked man in winter, telling: “What a calamity?” When H. Haleemā looked at him in this condition, she fell into anxiety and said: “O old man! Though I am in troubles, but I am caught in wonders upon wonders. Sometimes, air talks to me and sometimes stones teach me good manners. Wind talks to me in words and rocks and hills convince me of many things. Sometimes, my child is taken away by the unseen, and the unseen is dressed in green from the sky. Whom I have to talk to; whom I have to complain? Now I am feeling extremely anxious. I am afraid, I feel I have gone mad. I do not want to speak of the unseen wonders for the child’s honour. I say only this much that I have lost my child. If I tell the people about other things, people will consider me mad and put me in chains”.

sections.heading: Idols Do Not Claim Godhood, Man Makes Them
paras: The elderly man said: “Be pleased, O Haleemā! Offer the prostration of thanks to God and stop pinching and patting your face (as women did while expressing grief). Do not be anxious! The child will not be lost; but he is the one in whose greatness the entire world will be lost. Every moment with all care, full of jealousy and concern, there are for him lakhs of caretakers and guards from both front and backside. Have you not seen how those treacherous idols fell down on their faces in prostration when they heard the name of your child. This is a very strange development on the face of the earth. In this long life of mine, I have not seen anything like this. When the idols of stone are much distressed at this, imagine its impacts upon the living sinners. Stones have become their god, without their own intentions. They are innocent and helpless. But it is men who have chosen to become their slaves. The helpless stone is so frightened, as you have seen. Just imagine the difficulties of the criminals who act with their own will”.

chapters.title: Pleading of H. Abdul Mutallib
chapters.subtitle: Hearing of the news of getting lost of H. Muhammed by H. Abdul Mutallib, his grandfather; his searching for him all over the city and crying at the door of the Ka‘abā and praying to God; and hearing of a voice from inside the Ka‘abā

paras: When the grandfather of H. Mustafa came to know of H. Haleemā’s woes and loud cries and shouts, which reached a distance of a mile, he realized as to what the matter was. He also started beating his chest and crying. He came over to the gate of the Ka‘abā in great pain saying: “O knower of the secrets of the nights and days, I do not see any such abilities in me which would make me your secret bearer. I do not see any worth in me to be at the door of this prosperous place. I do not possess a head to prostrate to You, nor my tears are such as to wake up my fate. But I have seen on the face of that bright single pearl great signs of your benevolence. That great pearl is not one like us, though he is one amongst us. We are like copper and Ahmed is like alchemy. The wonders that I have seen in him have not been seen in any friend or foe. The grants You have bestowed upon him are such that none can present an example of it, even after a hundred years of austerities and meditations. What all I have seen in him, is like a pearl from your ocean. I have come before You with him alone as a recommendation, and pray to You to tell about his whereabouts as You are well aware”.

sections.heading: Mud Converted into Many Things
paras: There came a voice from inside the Ka‘abā: “He would show his face right there. He is in possession of two hundred fortunes from us and is under the protection of two hundred of our angels. We shall expose his external qualities upon the whole world and keep hidden his inner qualities. Water and clay were a mine of gold and we are their converters into gold out of which, sometimes we make an anklet, and at times, finger rings. Sometimes we make scabbards for swords and at times the neckband of the lions. Sometimes we make the decorative flowers of the throne and sometimes crowns to be worn by the kings. We love this clay very much and give it various shapes as it always sits in obedience before us. Lakhs of lovers and beloveds come out of it roaming about in search in cries and lamentations.

sections.heading: Inner Qualities of Mud
paras: Our jobs are against the desires of the blind rejectors of Our greatness who are always at loggerheads with Our acts. We have given this greatness to mud to offer it to the needy by making it to meet their needs. Mud exists in the form of dust to look at but its inside is full of great lightful qualities. Its outside is always at loggerhead with its inside. Its outside is like a stone but its inside is like a gem. Its outside says we are only this much, worthless; but its inside tells the outside to look properly on its front and back. The outside says: “the inside is nothing”, but the inside says: “you do not know my worth. Wait for sometime to see what I am thus, both of them are opposed to each other and only that will be victorious which carries on its job patiently. It is We who make beautiful shape out of its ugly shape and make it smile to expose its inner, hidden beauty. This is for the reason that mud appears always to be in sorrows and cries, but deep within it, there are lakhs of smiles. We are the revealers of the secrets, and that itself is our job to bring the secrets from inside.

sections.heading: Hide and Seek Game of Mud
paras: Though the thief always prefers to be silent to hide his acts, the police officer compels him to spill it. These heaps of mud have stolen many of Our valuable things, but We put them under trial and compel them to accept their guilt. Many wonderful children are born to these heaps of mud and greatest of them all is Ahmed, the Prophet. Both earth and the sky are so happy and pleased that from them is born such a great king. Out of the pleasure of his birth, earth became so large as the sky and its mud became full of flowers to speak of his greatness. O fortunate mud! Your outside is at war with your inside, one is such a clash will have a soul full of light. Your clash is in the path of God and keep it up, until God becomes inimical to your enemy’s colour and smell. Be sure: the darkness of your outside is with the light from inside which is like a sun, which does not set.

sections.heading: Great Men Do Not Care for Good Looks
paras: Whoever is in trials and struggles to come towards us, will be in a place under whose feet is the sky. He gets elevated so high. Your outside complains to us for its darkness, but your inside is in great pleasures as though a garden within another surrounding garden. A person in search of Us, like the sufī, is weary of apparels, and not good to look at, which he deliberately maintains so that the spoilers of his light may not come nearby to him. Gnostics (knowers of God) are horrible to look at like the porcupine, which is protected under its own hard thorny feathers. Gardens hide their flowers and expose their thorns to keep the hands of the flower puckers away from flowers. O porcupine! You have made your thorny feathers as your guards and kept your head deep within your bounds on the chest, like the Sufis, so that no one may interfere in your great pleasing seclusion; and that none with beautiful face but ugly inside may spoil your mood. O Abdul Mutallib, though your child has the usual habits of children, but both this and that world have come into existence for his sake. We shall grant life to the world through him and make the sky a slave for him.

chapters.title: Where to Find the Child
chapters.subtitle: H. Abdul Mutallib’s questioning as to where Muhammed would be found; and coming of the answer from within the Ka‘abā

paras: H. Abdul Mutallib said: “But where is he now? Show me the correct way to find him O knower of the secrets!” A voice came to him from within the ka‘abā saying: “O searcher of the child who has already found out his path! Do not grieve! I shall point out to the place where he is to be found. In that valley, under a tree, he is to be found.” H. Abdul Mutallib instantly marched towards that place. Along with him went other leaders of the tribe of Quraish, as he was one among the leaders of Quraish. From him backwards up to the back of H. Ādam, his ancestors were leaders in gatherings, entertainments and battle fields. But even this ancestry was only like a rind of fruit for H. Muhammed. He is far superior to the great emperors. The pulp of his fruit is far away from ancestry and rind ancestral greatness. From the lowest level of the fish samak that carries the earth on its back, as per common people’s belief to the highest star on the sky, Samaak, there is none like him. No one searches for birth and existence in search of God’s light. There is no need for the warp and weft of God’s royal apparel. The lowliest apparel that one gets from Him as reward to one’s good deeds is greater in decoration, brightness and beauty than the sun.

chapters.title: Further Call to Bilqīs
chapters.subtitle: Left over narrative of H. Sulaimān’s message of faith to Bilqīs

paras: Get up O Bilqīs! Come over to see that kingdom of God on the shore of which you may collect pearls. Your sisters (such as Aasia, wife of Pharaoh) are settled high above upon the sky. Why get up O Bilqīs and see the everlasting kingdom of heaven and enjoy the fruit of its wealth! Do you know what that great king has given to your sisters? Get up and enter into the ocean of graces and earn profits there without investing any capital. Your sisters are everlasting joys and pleasures; and this hard sorrowful situation does not suit for you to live in. ger up and be in the company of success and good fortune and kick off this kingdom of Sabā. You may become like that poor drum beater who is beating the drum in great joy as if he is himself the king of a country, which is nothing but a furnace.

chapters.title: Search This and That World
chapters.subtitle: Example of the men engaged in the search and greed of worldly gains, ignoring the wealth of the spirit: and the latter’s telling loudly: Ah me! Would that my people knew (what I know): “Yā laita Qawmī ya‘lamūna”: (Yasīn: 36: 26)

sections.heading: Street Dog and Wild Dog
paras: That dog (referred to earlier) saw a blind beggar and pounced upon him and tore off his clothes. We have already narrated this, but we respect it now to emphasis the moral. That blind beggar told the dog: “Your friends are in the hilly tracks and hunting wild animals there. Your community is catching wild donkeys in the hill tracks, and you are pouncing upon a blind beggar in the street.”

sections.heading: Genuine and Pseudo Shaikhs
paras: In similar manner, O hateable shaiķh, give up your treachery. You are saltish water having collected a few blind fellows around you telling: “They are my disciples and I am saltish water. They drink saltish water from me and become blind. O you saltish master! First sweeten from God (Ladunn). Do not make a net of dirty water for your blind disciples.

sections.heading: Models of Great Men to Invite Others
paras: Get up like the lions of God who catch large animals like the wild donkeys. They are the shaiķhs who desire for nothing other than God. As against them, you are like the dog which treacherously catches the blind followers. Those shaiķhs are personified lions; they go after lions and are splendored with the light of God. They gave up hunting and the pleasures of hunting and got themselves annihilated in God. They have become like the dead birds, whose models the hunters display to lure the other birds to come nearer to it when they catch them. The hunters, with this display, catch the species of those modelled birds. Great men are similarly held by God, their friends and they invite other birds to Him. They are like dead bird for God and are in anxieties of both His companionship and separation. It is about their hearts that the noble Prophet said: ‘Their hearts are unstable like a ball between the two fingers of God. The bird that is hunted by the hunter through the model of the dead bird is actually the hunter which hunts the hunter. The model of dead bird is only a medium. The bird that does not come nearer to this model cannot be caught by the hunter. Consider this hunting of yours as a great fortune, as God is your hunter and the saints who attract you towards themselves as models of dead birds to take you closer to God. Do not go away from them.

sections.heading: Annihilated Saints Give Everlasting Life
paras: The saints who get annihilated in God tells: “Do not look at the state of my annihilation in God as my death. My love for God has kept me clean and away from this kind of death. Look at this fact that I am protected by God who has taken me within Himself for protection. I am not dead but I am killed by the king who has made me appear like dead. Earlier, my movements were with the support of my wings and feathers which were with my will. But now my movements are within the control that Great Controller and Judge.
