My movements were of the outer limns of my body and they were external, but now there is a lasting movement, as it is towards God and is within myself and it is by Him. Anyone showing crooked movement before my movement will be severely beaten by me, even if he as large as the Seemurgh. Do not even consider me to be dead if you are alive. And if you consider yourself as a servant of God, you should consider me to be within God’s hand.”

sections.heading: H.‘īsā’s Miracles
paras: H.‘Īsā used to give life to the dead through his grace but I am within the hand of H. ‘Īsā’s Creator. And how can I be dead while being within the hand of H.‘Īsā’s Creator, when H.‘Īsā’s hand cannot be considered to be life-giving to me. That is; when H.‘Īsā’s hand itself is life-giving, why not the hand of his Creator. I myself am H.‘Īsā. I myself can give life to others and one who gets life from me lives forever. The life that I give is spiritual life and not physical which H.‘Īsā gave. One who got life from H.‘Īsā, later died. And most highly prosperous is the One who gave life to H.‘Īsā, enabling him to give life to others. I am of that power because, I am myself annihilated in God.

sections.heading: H. Mūsā’s Staff, Wind and Mosquito
paras: I am a staff in the hand of my Mūsā. But my Mūsā is unseen and I am present before you. I become a bridge for my followers to cross the river and I also become a python for Pharoah. Therefore, be careful, not to consider this staff to be alone, as without its being in the hand of God, it cannot be like as it was. See also how the waves of flood which swallowed the loud pitch and low pitch of the drum of the worshippers of magic. So also, wind was a staff upon the enemies of H. Hūd, which smoked off his left-over enemies. even the mosquito was a staff, which smashed and blew off the brain of Nimrod.

sections.heading: Bad People Required for Hell
paras: If I go on counting the staffs of God. I can tear off the curtains behind which these Pharaohs are hiding. But let them eat this sweet poisonous grass for some more days. If there are no people of the grandeur and leadership of Pharaoh, then how in the hell to get its food. The butcher should first feed well the animal to be slaughtered, make it fat and then slaughter its as dogs of the hell are hungry and in wait for food. Had there been no opponents and enemies in the world, the feeling of anger would vanish from the people’s minds. Hell is an exposer of the wrath of God, which cannot come about without His opponents. It would not exist and would be extinguished with the light of the faithful. Hell is that wrath which needs to exist as otherwise, mercy will extinguish it.

sections.heading: Wrath to Go with Mercy
paras: If benevolence alone were to be there without wrath and viciousness, kingship would not attain perfection. Both are required to maintain the dignity of authority. If the rejectors of the noble people make fun of them, you may also do so with them, if you went, and warn them as to for how long they would live in the world when they are already spiritually dead. Therefore, my friends be happy in the understanding of and devotion to God at the door which is opened for you in this day.

sections.heading: Different Plots for Different Crops
paras: Everything that is needed for life is sown and grown in a different plot of land within one farm land itself. Garlic and onions cannot be sown and grown together in the same plot. Every vegetable grows well with the other plants of its own species, and meets its requirements in proper manner. Saffron requires to be in a different plot and it should not be mixed up with other plants. Saffron should get water as required by it, till it gets fully developed. You are also much valuable like saffron and you should make it more valuable by mixing it with sweet dishes. Do not put your face in a plot meant for beetroot, so that it may not become one like you in your tastes and appearance. You are kept in a different plot and beetroot in another. This is done, as the earth of God is very vast and large. It is so large and vast that even devils and fairies forget their paths.

sections.heading: Unseen World Larger Than Visible World
paras: That apart, the hidden world is so vast and large that the oceans, forests and mountains of this apparent world are altogether so tiny as a hair in the oceans and continents. Water of the lakes of the hearts of the friends of God is still, as its speed of flow is unmeasurable, but it is faster, sweeter and fresher than the fresh water of the fast-moving rivers and streams. This has hidden movements just like the soul and life, which are in all the bodies but move all over in it without being-seen. The searcher of God puts his steps and secretly roams about on them. The hearer failed to understand what all I said and went into sleep; and therefore, there is no need to speak of all this anymore. Therefore, O speaker, do not write your marks and words upon water and put an end to it.

chapters.title: Achievement of the Other World
chapters.subtitle: H. Sulaimān offer to Bilqīs. This time is quite suitable

paras: Get up O Bilqīs! The bazaar is going on in full speed. Run away from these mean fellows involved in losses. Get up, when you are in full control of yourself, well before death starts to catch you up. Get up and come froward before the arrival of death and look at the kingdom and country, where there are no mischiefs and turmoil. Get up and give up your sense of pride upon your status, and offer your devotion, and not your styles and poise in this abode of grandeur. Get up and do not contest with the fate appointed by God, as otherwise death will come and punch your ears. Therefore, death will pull your ears in such a harsh way as the police do with the thief. How long do you steal the shoes from the legs of the donkeys. If at all you want to steal, come over and steal rubies. Your sisters have taken over the rule of the everlasting kingdom, but you are yet holding on to the kingdom of lightless and dark country. That soul is prosperous which has given up this kind of dark kingdom, which is sure to be overtaken and ruined by death.

sections.heading: Uncomparable Joy and Life
paras: Get up, O Bilqīs and look at the kings and nobles of the kingdom of religion. They are sitting in a pleasant garden, though to look at, they appear as thorns among their friends. Gardens follow them to every place, they go, but those gardens are hidden from the people. Fruits of the garden flatter them and pray to them to eat also saying: “the water of life has come in us and have a drink of it through us”. You may go around the heaven without wings and feathers like the sun, the crescent and the full moon. O Bilqīs! You will march forward like the soul without feet. You will eat hundreds of types of foods that never become deficient. No crocodiles of sorrows will attack your boat, nor a bad name would come to you after your death. You alone shall be the fortunate and fortune itself. Even if you are a great fortune and a fortunate king in this world, it is not sure to be with you for long. Anytime, it may go away and you will lose all possessions and become like a beggar. Therefore, do not think of getting wealth, but become a wealth itself. If you understand all these things, you will become a fortunate itself and, in that situation, you get lost within yourself. O the one in good situations! When you get lost within yourself, you get into a situation of existence itself and become personified wealth and kingdom.

chapters.title: Construction of the Masjid
chapters.subtitle: Continuation of the narrative of H. Sulaimān’s construction of masjid-e-Aqsā under the instruction, inspiration of God and the help offered by the angels, devils and fairies

paras: After H. Sulaimān completed his instructions to Queen Balqīs, a voice came to him from front of his throne: ‘O Sulaimān, the fortunate prophet! Build the Masjid-e-Aqsa, as the army of Bilqīs has become habituated to perform salāt”.

sections.heading: Men: Chained to Greed, Love, Fear
paras: When H. Sulaimān laid the foundation of the masjid, men and jinns gathered and took up construction work. Some of them with full voluntary enthusiasm and some without such interest, just as some persons worship with enthusiasm and also some without it. People are like devils caught in the chains of their desires which drag them to their shops and professions for making money. This chain is made up of greed and fear for livelihood. They are always chained to it. This chain keeps them in fear, which is within them and not externally visible. No one is free of this chain of love or fear. This chain drags them towards different professions and searching. It drags them towards the oceans and deep mines to meet their greed. It drags them towards both good and bad things, as God has said about Abu Lahab’s wife, which is a case for all others: “A twisted rope of palm-leaf fiber round her

sections.heading: Neck”: “Fī Jīdiha Hablun Min Masad”: (Lahab: 111: 5) Greed Shows Things as Beautiful
paras: Certainly, we have made ropes around their necks and these ropes are made up of their own character and conduct. There is no good or bad man, without carrying a record of his actions hanging down from his neck. Greed for bad acts is like fire, which appears beautiful because of its fast color. Black colour of coal is hidden, but fire burns and makes it a beautiful lump of fire. When fire stops burning, its black colour comes back. Black coal was a lump of fire because of your greed. When your greed came to an end. It lost its fire and regained its state of black coal. While burning, it appeared like a lump of fire. This burning was the work of the beauty of the fire of your greed. Your greed presented your acts to you as well decorated beautiful objects. And when greed ended, your beautiful observation turned into ugliness. Devil (of greed) makes the bunch of raw fruits appear as ripe, and one who considers them as really ripe is a fool. When trials are conducted by his soul, and he tastes the raw fruits, his teeth become sensitive. It was his greed that made the raw fruit as a trap for him. So also, reflections of the ghost of his own greed. But consider the jobs of religion and of goodness. They are generally not looked at with greed to take them. Yet they are beautiful, of their own. They are good in their own nature, and not as reflections of others. Whether there is an impact of greed upon them or not. They are ever brilliant with their inherent goodness.

sections.heading: Without Greed, Things Appear Normal
paras: When the brightness of greed goes away from the deeds of the world, there is no beauty in them. Coal continues to be black without becoming a lump of fire. It is greed only that makes it bright even children get cheated by greed. They hold on to lapel of their shirts as bridles of the horse and run as though riding a horse. When one such a child matures and gets rid of this foolish greed, he laughs at other children doing such acts, thinking as to what a fool he was. The impact of greed presents vinegar as honey to him. How foolish he was to see things and act upon them.

sections.heading: Great Acts Done Without Greed
paras: Construction made by the prophets were not due to greed. That is why their impacts and grandeur increase as time passes. Many noble people have built many masjids, but none got a name and fame as Masjid-e-Aqsā got. The honour of Ka‘abā increases with every passage of time. This is due to the purity of the thoughts and feelings of H. Ibrāhīm, who built it. The excellence of this masjid is not due to its bricks and stones, but because of the absence of greed and competition on the part of its builder. Their records and books are not like those of others, nor the masjids built by them, not their houses and profession. Not even their discipline, anger, wrath, drowsiness, imaginations and talks. To each of them, God has granted different types of lakhs of graces, honours and statuses. Each one of them has a different kind of grandeur and dignity. The birds of their souls have different kinds of feathers and wings. My heart shivers while speaking about their affairs. Their acts are as honorable for aur acts as Ka‘abā is for us. Their birds lay eggs of gold. Their souls see the darkness of the midnight as bright as the morning. What all I say about their good qualities is deficient. It is as though, due to my inability that what I say in their praise is actually incomplete or defective, as though, I am speaking ill of them.

sections.heading: Make Your Heart Mighty as H. Sulaimān’s Ring
paras: O noble people! You may also proceed to build a masjid-e-Aqsā, as H. Sulaimān has arrived. May peace be upon him. If the devils and fairies disobey him, they will be caught within the clutches of the angels. If the devils, try to over smart him and resort to slackness in their work, a hunter like the lightening will fall upon their head. Be like H. Sulaimān, so that you devils may carry stones for the construction of your palace. Become one like H. Sulaimān without any doubts and suspicion so that the jinns and fairies may be obedient to you. The finger-ring of H. Sulaimān was his means with the might of which, he ruled over all. It was stolen by a jinn by named Saķhķher, who started ruling in H. Sulaimān’s place. This ring had so much power as to make one mighty like H. Sulaimān. Know this that your heart is as mighty as H. Sulaimān’s finger ring. If you keep your heart well protected, it will not be caught and over taken by any devil or jinn. Your heart will have an ever-lasting rule upon you. Be careful with the devils, so that they may not steal your heart. Peace be upon you.

sections.heading: Sulaimānism Exists Even Now
paras: Know this my heart! Great acts like those of H. Sulaimān (Sulaimānism) have not ended. There is one in your head and heart to carry on Sulaimānism. At times, devil also carries on Sulaimānism. But every weaver cannot weave silk. Both weavers move their hands in like manner, but there is a great difference in their results and products. In order to understand the meaning of this statement, hear this narrative in mathnavi.

chapters.title: Enhancement of Grant
chapters.subtitle: Narrative of a poet who was granted money by the king which was doubled upon the recommendation of a vāzīr, by name Hasan

paras: A poet came before a king and recited a poem in the hope of getting reward, honour and status. The king was generous enough for payment of a sum of a thousand to him with red gold, honours and other gifts. His minister told him that this is too less as amount: “He may please be granted ten thousand so that he may go back with joy, for such a poet and from such a generous person like you, majesty, my suggestion for even ten thousand is too less.” He spoke so well of generosity in a philosophic way that one-tenth of the left-over treasure of the king was given over to the poet. He was given over ten thousand and also other grants. This made the head of the poet, a house of gratefulness, thanksgiving and praises.

sections.heading: Thanks, Need Not with Words
paras: The poet then made enquiries as to who impressed the king of my skill and persuaded him to grant him generosity like this. He was told that it was so and so vazir, whose name was Hasan, which means good, and he is one of good character and feelings. In praise of him, the poet wrote another poem and left off towards his house. The graces and grants of the kings, themselves are praises about their greatness, without shaking their lips and tongue about the kings and also the grants.

chapters.title: Reduction of the Grants
chapters.subtitle: Coming back of the poet after a few years with the hope of thousands of dinars and gifts. The king’s order for the grant of a thousand dinars as per his habit to other vazir, who, after the death of the earlier vazir had occupied the place, his name was also Hasan. He said that so much money is too much. Many expenses are ahead of us and the treasury is empty; and I shall make the poet agree to accept one-tenth of what you have ordered.

paras: A few years later, the same poet was in poverty and deprivation, and he needed to go out for an earning. He thought: “At a time when both the hands are empty, and poverty has overtaken. It is more reasonable to approach the already tested source. I shall take my fresh needs to that place, which I have already tested”.

sections.heading: One Meaning of Allah
paras: In order to explain the meaning of the word “Allāh”. The lexicographer, Saiboya has said: ‘He is the one who upon needs is approached for fulfilment’. [He says that the word “Allāh” is derived from the word “Alah”, which originally was “walah”, which means wonder struck, forlorn and showing fright. The word was Alah Ilaihi. Then the first ‘H’ and ‘aih’ were joined together to make it ‘Allāh’, to mean to one to whom the creatures’ approach when they are in need with grief and lamentation ― As explained by Qazi Sajjad husain] Saiboya in another verse says: We turn towards You to meet our needs. We search for that in many places and came before You.

sections.heading: Everyone Prays and Seeks from God
paras: Hundreds of thousands of wise men when in distress and pain cry before that Unique One. There is no such a fool or mad who stretches his hand to beg before a helpless miser. If all these thousands of wisemen, had not seen Him earlier as an answer of needs, they would not have presented their lives before Him. Rather all fishes in the waves of water, all birds flying high in the sky, all waves playing about in the oceans and rivers are expressing their enthusiasm and taste for Him in every manner. Elephants, wolves, lions and their victims, hefty pythons, snakes and ants and even mud, air, water and sparks of fire ger their capital and means of existence from Him. Springs and autumns and these heavens always is His praises praying to Him: “O God! Do not leave us even for a moment. You are the pillar of our support, protection and refuge”.

sections.heading: All Things Rolled Up with Him
paras: All things are rolled up in His two right hands as the Qurān says: “And the heavens will be rolled up in his right hand”: “wa alsamāwātu mutuwwiyātun biyamīnihi”: (Zumar: 39: 67). [ His two hands mean: His attributes (names) of Dominance and Beauty (Jalālia and Jamālia) which organize and maintain all these things. The Prophet has said: ‘The two hands of my Lord are right hands. That is; as in men, right hand is stronger than the left; but Lord’s both hands are as strong as the right hand. Both are strong like the right hand’ ― Qazi Sajjad Husain]

sections.heading: Prayer of the Earth for Stability
paras: The earth says: ‘Keep me stable as you have made me ride upon water (liquid)’. [The continents and the oceans of which the outer earth is made rest upon huge slabs called tectonic rocks, which float upon the hot, molten, magma which is in liquid condition. It is this magma, which comes out from inside in the form of liquid dust and gas, from miles below the surface. The liquid upon coming out is called lave through openings resulting in volcanoes. The movements of tectonic rocks to separate, join or slip away from each other cause earth quakes, both in the sea bed and on land. The earth suffers a million tiny quakes every year including at least 100 serious ones and 10 disastrous ones. The rest occur in uninhabited areas and ignored. Earth quake in the ocean causes of monstrous tides called Tsunami and cause terrible havoc by waves rising upto 50 to 100 feet in height and sweep away areas on the coast line ― Translator’s note]

sections.heading: Everyone: a Beggar Before Him
paras: All have learnt to stitch their begging bags from Him alone and also to meet their needs. All prophets have got the commanding orders from Him alone, and sought His help through patience and prayer, as He has said: “Seek God’s help with patient perseverance and prayer”: “wa asta‘īnu bis sabri wa al salāt” (Baqara: 2: 45). Be careful to seek only from Him and never from others. Search for water in the ocean and not in the dried-up stream. If you ask someone’s help to meet your needs, and if he gives, be sure that it is God only who has given you and kept what is to be given on your palm. When He has given so much to a rejector like Qārūn, how can He remain without giving to the one who turns to Him in obedience?

sections.heading: Rich Waits for Seekers of Help
paras: The poet with the expectation of grant from the generous king, once again turned toward him. What else can the offer of a poet be other than a fresh ode? He places that before the benevolent grantor and pledges himself to him. The benefactors with hundreds of grants, graces and goodness keep gold with them and wait upon poets to come and receive from them. One verse in their view is more precious than a hundred bales of silk fabrics; in particular that verse that brings out the pearls of meanings from the depths of oceans.

sections.heading: Men Desire Praises: so Also, God
paras: At first a man in greedy of bread, as bread is the pillar upon which life rests. He resorts to professions snatching from others and hundreds of designs to earn this, and keeps his life upon his own palm and takes great risks. And later, when he is contented and satisfied with his earnings and bread, he loves to earn good name and flattery from the poets, so that his root and progeny may bloom like flowers, and lectures are made in praises of his excellences from the elevated platforms. So that, they may spread the fragrance of the ambergris through words, of his grandeur, glory and generosity. Out creation is made by God upon His own model and our attributes and qualities learn lessons from His attributes and qualities. As that Great Creator of all searches for His praise and thanksgiving, man also searches for praises for himself. In particular those great men of Truth who are very smart in great matters. Their goatskin becomes full of air of praises and blows up in size. This is their attainment. As against this, if they are not worthy, and they are given false praises. Their goatskin is a torn one and any air of praises blown into it goes out, and it remains flat. Do not take this example given by me as a cursory one if you are wise enough. I have not myself given this example. This was told by the prophet when he heard the objectionable statement as to why he was elated when praised.

sections.heading: Man Dies but Not His Acts
paras: Anyway, the poet left and went towards that king and carried with him the verses of thanks for the rewards he had obtained earlier, which he had not forgotten. Graceful people die but their gracious acts continue to live. They are such fortunate people who ride upon the vehicle of graces. similarly, the cruel people die, but their cruelties remain alive; and it is a pity upon such souls which perform treacherous and deceitful acts. The prophet has said that, that person requires to be appreciated, who left this world, but his good acts remain here itself [ The Prophet has said: When a man dies, all his acts also die except three: continuing grants, profitable knowledge and a good child who prays for him]. The generous man died but not his generosity. Faith and generosity are not of little valve before God. Good name comes out of good acts, and as his good acts continue to remain even after his death, he is not dead but lines in his good deeds. But regretful it is for him who died but not his sins. Therefore, do not ever think that the sinner would save himself from pains after his death.

sections.heading: Transfer from Generosity to Miserliness
paras: Now, you may keep this matter aside and think of the poet as he was in debts and in need of money. He took his verses to the king in the hope of earlier grants and rewards. His verses were on very subtle and intricate matters as though full of fine pearls; and he expected similar honour as earlier, full of desires and great hopes. The king as per his habit, passed an order for the grant of a thousand coins. He has been accustomed to gracefulness from a longtime. But on this occasion, there was no generous vazir as earlier, as he had ridden the burraq of honour and left the world. In his place there was a new vazir, who was merciless and mean of character. He said: “O king! We have many expenses to meet; and grant of so much to a poet is not proper. I shall bring him to agree to one-fortieth of this much, with his own pleasure and contentment.” Others in the court said: “Earlier, he has received ten thousand from this generous king. Who will chew dry grass after chewing sugarcane? Who will agree to beggary after having seen kingship.” The vazir said: “I shall press him so much and make him wait for so long, that he would go weak and cry in pain. Thereafter, if I give him the dust of my road, he will carry that like the soft petals of the flowers of the garden. Leave this matter to me as I am a master of such affairs. I can even deal with a claimant of very hot temperament. Even one who flies from the high enough Pleiades to the lower of the low under the earth, becomes soft when he looks at me”. The king said to him: “Alright: do as you feel good, but make him pleased as he is a speaker of our goodness.” The vazir said: “leave two hundred beggars like him at my disposal and you may rest aside.”

sections.heading: Crushing by False Promises
paras: Then the vazir made him wait for long; so much that winter passed off, autumn came to an end and the spring season arrived. Whatever need that the poet spoke of, the vazir ignored and gave promises and excuses upon promises and excuses. In the waiting period the poet became old and got tired of the difficulties, anxieties and pains. He told the vazir: “If you do not want to give me gold, do not give; at least give me some abusive words so that my life may be rid of you, upon which I shall become your obedient slave. My worship has killed me. Now, atleast, tell me to go away so that this poor man may be released from the prison of false and promises.” Thereafter, the vazir gave him one-fortieth of the reward and the poet fell into great worries. “Earlier, what I received was so grand and so much. And now, what I got after so much of delay is like a bundle of thorns”. People told him; that earlier vazir was wise and principled. He left the world. May God reward him for his good acts. With his hands, grants used to be doubled. He never committed wrongs in the matter of grants. Now, he has left, and took along with him acts of graciousness. He has certainly died but not his acts of grace. A wise and good-natured vazir has gone away from us, and now has come a vazir who peels out the skin of beggars. Now, you may remain satisfied with whatever he has given and go away from here in the darkness of night, so that he may not catch you again and snatch from you whatever you have, by making false allegations against you. You do not know as to how we made a hundred persuasions even to get so much paid to you.”

sections.heading: Good Name with Bad Conduct
paras: Then, the poet turned his face towards them and said: “O benevolent kind people, please tell me from where this cruel soldier has come. What is the name of this fellow who pulls out even the clothes from the body of the people.” People told him: “His name is Hasan (meaning good).” The poet said: “O God! What is this? Hasan was that generous vazir’s name and so also of this cruel fellow? How is it that one name is of two fellows of opposite nature? He was so good and this fellow is so bad; O lord of the faith! This is highly regrettable. There was that Hasan upon a little movement of whose pen, hundred vazirs and men were hopeful of grants. And now there is a Hasan with the hair of whose ugly beard a hundred ropes can be made? A king who offers his ears to hear from such a vazir will make the names of kings and kingdoms disgraceful forever.

chapters.title: Comparison of Vazir with Hāmān
chapters.subtitle: Comparison between this mischievous and anti-human vazir and his destruction of the king’s goodness and Hāmān, the vazir of Pharoah, whose potentiality to mischief resulted in the rejection of H. Mūsā’s advice

paras: Many a times, upon hearing the words of H. Mūsā, Pharaoh used to become soft and amenable, as H. Mūsā’s words were such as to make a stone provide milk. Upon consultation with his Minister Hāmān, who was very mean, ill natured and hard-hearted, he was prevented from being reasonable. He used to say: “Till now you were the ruler of Egypt and by hearing that ill clad treacherous fellow, you have become his slave! His words, as though thrown as stones from a large sling would fall on the grass palace of Pharaoh. Whatever H. Mūsā used to say in hundred days used to destroy by him in a moment.

sections.heading: Minister Makes and Unmasks the Kings
paras: In similar manner, your wisdom has become a victim of your passions. There is a dacoit of the God’s path in your existence. Some godly man gives advice to you and that dacoit treacherously chases it away from you, telling: “Be warned! This advice is unsuitable for you. Do not ever go away from your place. This is not such a thing to be followed. Be careful: do not go mad.” How regrettable it is for a king to have such a minister. He makes the wrathful hell as a place of choice for both of them. That king is very fortunate who has a helping hand in his good deeds like Āsif, H. Sulaimān’s minister. When the just king has such a minister, his name goes like light upon light. A king like H. Sulaimān and a minister like Āsif are like two great perfumes: ambergris upon Abir. But for a king like Pharaoh and a minister like Hāmān, there is nothing but misfortune. They have darknesses upon darknesses during their life time and on the doomsday neither their wisdom not wealth will be any use. I have not seen anything other than hard-heartedness in the mean fellows. And, if you happen to see good in them, tell my salutation to them.

sections.heading: Wisdom of Self and Others Is Useful
paras: A king is like the life and soul, and the minister is like wisdom; and mischievous wisdom chases the soul out. When the angel of wisdom goes wrong like Hārūt, one becomes a master to teach mischief to two hundred devils; Do now make your immature wisdom as your guide, as common people do but become a king by making perfect wisdom as your minister. Do not make your desires as your minister, as your clean soul will go away from the worship of God. Desire full of greed looks only as the present things, but wisdom thinks and looks at the happenings of the trials of the last days. Both the eyes of wisdom look at the ultimate effects and results of matters and they prepare themselves to receive the pricks of thorns for the sake of flower, as the thorne does not break or fall down in autumn. May it happen that every nose not go after the fragrance of short-term flowers, which fall down and decay soon. Though you too have your own wisdom, be advised my father, to consult others and decorate your wisdom all the more. With yours and the wisdom of another, you will be away from many calamities and keep your feet upon the heights of the heavens.

chapters.title: Devils Become Mighty at Times
chapters.subtitle: Seating himself of the jinn upon the seat of H. Sulaimān and carrying on of his functions, calling himself as Sulaimān b. Dawood and appearance of the difference between both

paras: The jinn by name Saķhķhar called himself as Sulaimān and occupied his throne and took control of the kingdom. He had seen the external acts of H.Sulaimān which he adopted, while his inside was devilish. People said: “This Sulaimān is without a clean inside. There is a great difference between this Sulaimān and that. That Sulaimān, just as that Hasan and another Hasan” (about which there was narration earlier). This devil said: “God has created another Sulaimān like me by giving that devil a face like mine. He has given my face to devil so that he may catch you in his loop. If he comes about before you, you should never believe him on his face value.”

sections.heading: Wise People Cannot Be Fooled
paras: This devil used to say treacherously like this, but there used to no impression upon the clean-hearted people. Tricks and designs are not possible with people who have the sense of discrimination, particularly those, whose wisdom and sense are guided by forces unseeable by others. No magic, treachery and tricks can put curtains upon the people with this wealth. They used to tell themselves in reply to him: “O the one with wrong words, you are giving in the reverse side. You will again go in the reverse side towards the lowliest of the lowly stage of hell. Though H. Sulaimān is deposed of kingdom and become poor, his forehead is bright like the full moon. You have stolen the finger ring of H. Sulaimān, you are a personified hell, not of heat but of excessive cold, with which you have become frigid and forlorn. But we, with our grandeur glory, army, grave and dignity, will never even keep our feet in it. If by inadvertence we keep our forehead before you, a hand will come from under the soil and lift up in head, telling: “Do not keep your head before this perverted fellow. Be warned! Do not ever prostrate to this deficient fellow!

sections.heading: Why Mean Fellow Assumes Great Status
paras: I could explain to you the mystery behind this fact as to why such mean fellows assume great positions, but the great dignity and superiority of God comes in the way and prevents me. Greatness of the Great God is unmatchable. A part of it is given to man which is a great gift. God gives this even to the mean and lowly with a purpose. I dare not think over that purpose. Be satisfied with what little I have said now, and wait until some other time, when I may explain. Devils keep the names of great people, such as Sulaimān and tey to put curtains upon the faces of the innocent people so that they may not know of their devilish character. Therefore, ignore the name and face and look at the inside of the people, and not at the name and status. Make enquiries about them acts and character; and in between their acts and character only, they have to be understood, not in their name, fame and status. But be careful! This kind of study is not for every this and that man (only those with great enthusiasm, taste and enquiring nature can do this). Now, hold on to your proceedings and finish the jobs of construction of masjid-e- Aqsa. To be precise, its construction is over. It became a place of pilgrimage and H. Sulaimān was its pilgrim.

chapters.title: H. Sulaimān’s Visits to Masjid to Teach
chapters.subtitle: Entrance of H. Sulaimān into the masjid every day for worship and offering guidance to the worshippers and dwellers; and growth of medicinal plants in the masjid and H. Sulaimān’s talking with him

paras: when H. Sulaimān, Prophet of God, and king of the people, finished the construction of the masjid, it became his routine to visit the masjid every morning and remain there for some time. He used to see a new plant grown in the masjid. He used to ask it to tell its name and the benefit within it: “you are of benefit for whom and of loss for whom”? Each plant used to speak of its name and say: “I am a cause of life for so and so and of death for so and so. I am sugar for such and such men and poison for such others. My name is so and so as written on the protected tablet (Lawh-e-Mahfooz) with authority.

sections.heading: Lawh-E-Mahfooz Explained
paras: [ Lawh-e-Mahfooz, Protected Tablet is a large sheet or tablet of unimaginable infinite size upon which are written all laws of nature, causes of creation and destruction of everything, properties of all things: chemical, physical, botanical, zoological etc. all senses and their creation, psychic functions, actions of every man great and low, all laws of history, evolution of all sciences, of everything to occur every where in the universe and beyond space and time – from the beginning to the final end of all physical and psychic things, wisdom and thinking of every creature, and their fate, individually and collectively. All things that we study through all subjects of study from the unknown beginning and prior to beginning and the final end and subsequence, are all written down, not in letters and winds but as powers and properties, whatever we see in anything is written without words and letters in everything, peculiar and particular to it. Each thing with its own peculiarity and particularity exhibits the matters relating to itself, a model of which is in the Protected Tablet. Whatever is known to man about anything is known through the study of that thing. Properties of oxygen became known by study of oxygen itself. Thousands of pages written about the structure, activities, deceases and treatment of the eye or nose and anything part of man are written in words by different authors from the early days to this day by studying those very parts. All written down knowledge came from them only by observing them, which is not written in words but by their appearance and functions. Similarly, in respect of everything in the universe. Their functioning, properties etc. are written down in the protected tablet, which they possess and unreservedly obey. These things can be considered to possess a bit of the protected tablet directly related to them. There are billions of things and their actions, comprising of elements and the combined forms as chemicals, from elementary matter and energy particles, to the cosmos. Microcosmic to macrocosmic. Billions of living things from viruses and bacteria to large sized elephants, unicellular to huge multi cellular animals and the extinct dinosaur and plants, billions of stars, planets and other objects in the heavens, various forces of nature like gravity, electro magnetic force, weak force and strong force with their energies and so on. Every thing about each and every thing in the universe ad their laws and also of spiritual non-physical powers beyond the universe (lamakan) as stated in the Qurān: “We ordained laws for him in the tablets in all matters both commanding and explaining all things”: “Wa

sections.heading: Katabnā Lahu Fil Alwāhi Min Kulli Shai‘in Wa Maw‘izatan Wa Tafsīlan Likulli Shai‘in”:
paras: (A‘raaf: 7: 145). Each creative (living, non-living) has its own tablet with everything written about it within it. And the lawh-e-mahfooz is the compendium of all these writings ― Translator]

sections.heading: Knowledge of Medicinal Plants
paras: Thereafter, H. Sulaimān used to explain the profit and loss causable by the plants to the medicine men and physicians. These medicine men and physicians became wise. Leaders and explainers of the qualities of these plants, such an extent that they wrote books on diseases and their treatments and relieved to bodies of pains and sicknesses. This knowledge of astronomy and medicine came to the prophets through godly inspiration (wahī). The noble Prophet Muhammed said: One among the prophets drew a line. Any line that went along with the prophet’s line is right and any other one not in accordance with it, is wrong (Hadiţh). There is no other way for wisdom and senses to tread the path of lamakan (world of non-physical existence)

sections.heading: All Knowledge Is Initially by Inspiration
paras: Deficient wisdom of men relating to one particular study is not creative. It is capable only of meeting its further needs and accepting fresh information. It is capable of learning more from others; and the inspired man becomes his teacher. All crafts and professions came about from inspiration in the beginning and wisdom improved and developed them. Every artisanship and craftsmanship cannot be learnt other than through a teacher. And our wisdom alone cannot give us artisanship and craftsmanship. Though your wisdom became so capable of splitting of the hair through words, but no profession can come to you without a teacher. If the learning of professions was from wisdom only, you would have learnt it without a teacher.

chapters.title: Profession of Grave Digging
chapters.subtitle: Cain’s (Qābīl) learning of grave digging from the crow as there was no profession of grave digging before him

paras: Grave digging which is a lowly profession now, could not come about by thinking, planning and wisdom. If Qābīl (Cain) had the sense for it, he would not have carried the dead body of his brother, Hābīl, upon his head, worrying as to where I should hide it. The body was smeared with blood and dust. He saw a crow carrying the dead body of a crow in its back and flying fast towards him. It came down from the air and started the art of grave digging to teach him the art. Then it dug up mud with its claws and made a grave; and kept the dead crow in it and put over mud upon it and hid the dead body. The crow learned this art under the inspiration from God. Cain said to himself: “Ah! Fie upon my wisdom. The crow has gone ahead of me in an art.”

sections.heading: Perfect Wisdom and Partial Wisdom
paras: God said of the wisdom of the Prophet as perfect wisdom and said: “His eye did not turn aside nor yet he was over bold”: “Mā zāghal basaru wa mā taghā”: (Najm: 53: 7). That is: his perfect wisdom saw everything in clarity. But the partial wisdom of man turns towards different directions to ascertain. The perfect wisdom is the light of God for the special servants of God. Wisdom of the crow is the master of those who put the dead bodies inside the graves. The soul that flies behind the crow, will be taken over by it to the graveyard, as it is only partial wisdom some of specific things. Your self is also like a crow. Do not go after it, as it will take you to the graveyard and not to the garden. If at all you want to follow a bird, you should follow the ‘Unqā of your heart, as it will take you toward the Caucasus Mountain and the masjid-e-Aqsā. Fresh grass needed for your life and soul will be available to you, which grows in the masjid-e-Aqsā of your heart. Your heart is like masjid-e-Aqsā for this purpose. You may value this place as H. Sulaimān did and search for the grass for your soul through him and do not keep your feet of rejection and refuse to enter into it. This speaking of heart, masjid-e-Aqsā and the plants therein only is to tell you about the fertility of the soil of your heart and the varieties of plants as though that grow there.

sections.heading: Invisible Forces Drag You
paras: Whatever grown in one soil speaks of the quality of the soil: sugarcane of its quality and dry cane of its quality. The soil of the soul of which thoughts are the plants speak of the secrets of the heart. If I say to one capable of understanding hidden truths and apparent truths and how to differentiate between them, I can grow lakhs of flowers in the garden. And when I find other than him, that is, incapable fellows, my thoughts run away from my heart like thieves. Where there are no audiences to hear, it is better to keep quiet, and hiding high- level talks from them is still better. Everyone moves towards the one who drags him. Real attraction is not false attraction. Sometimes you walk in misguidance and sometimes in guidance by what that drags you; but neither the rope is visible nor the dragger.

sections.heading: Ignorance Leads
paras: You are like a blind camel and your rope is pledged to others; and therefore, you should think of the dragging itself and not the one who drags. If the rope-puller were to be visible, this world would not be a place of confusions. The infidel would see that he is going after the dog and becoming obedient to the black-faced devil. He would not follow behind him like a prisoner. This old fellow with the wisdom of a boy would drag his feet away from him. He would not follow him like a eunuch. Even an infidel would refuse to follow him. If a cow were to be aware of the butcher, it would not follow him to his shop. It would not eat husk from his hand or give milk to him with love to please him. If it were to know of the object of its feeding, it would not have digested the fodder given to it. Thus, this world itself is stationed on a pillar of ignorance. There is no need to mention about wealth. It is connected with great struggles and mutual quarrels. Its beginning is running about here and there and its end is getting kicks. This is a ruin in which, there is nothing but donkey’s death in the form of man’s death.

sections.heading: Defects and Results of Jobs: Not Certain
paras: Defects of any job that you take up and work for, remain hidden from you. This is the reason that you engage yourself in it. This is because, God, the organizer of all jobs has kept them hidden from you. Similarly, I all the thoughts and ideals you engage yourself in, keep their defects hidden from you. Were you to know of the defects and failings in them you would run away from them on the distances between the east and west, which never meet. Were you to know of the situations and actions that ultimately put you to shame, you would never go after them. That is why, God under his grand scheme keeps the results hidden from us so that we may go for what is predestined for us, putting us to shame. This becoming ashamed is another predestination. Therefore, do not give too much importance to the shameful situation, and pray to God. If you do not do like this, you will become personified shame, that will make you all the more ashamed: half of your life goes in these anxieties and the other half will go into shamefulness. Give up these thoughts of shame and search for a good friend, situation and job. When you do not have any good job to do, upon the loss of which thing will you feel ashamed?

sections.heading: Guilty Conscience May Be Mistaken Notion
paras: Engage yourself in a job which you feel to be a good job, because if you do not know of a good job you cannot know of a bad job, because it is from an opposite that its opposite can be found out. A good thing can be known only by its comparison with a bad thing. Therefore, our advice to you is to give up the thought of your shame, and that you are helpless. If you say you cannot give up these thoughts of shame, you should know that, while committing sins also you had thought that you were helpless to prevent yourself from them. When you feel of helplessness in giving up the sense of shame, search for the cause of your helplessness. Therefore, be sure to know that even the sense of helplessness has not been felt in this world without its comparison with power. Nobody is aware of it nor anyone would know it later. In similar manner you are behind the curtain to see the defects of everything that you desire. If you were to know the defects of the desires, your life would run away from the search for it. If God were to reveal the defects to you, nobody could take you towards it by any number of efforts. The other jobs you hate to do are due to your knowing of their defects.

sections.heading: Clean Heart: a Proper Guide
paras: O God! You are the One with sweet words. Do not hide from us the defects of bad acts. And do not show us defects in good acts, so that we may not go cold in our approach to them and as such become worthless. The elderly H. Sulaimān, as per his habit entered into the masjid in the brightness of the morning. It was his routine to search for new plants in the masjid. Just as H. Sulaimān used to know of the secrets of the plants, a man of clean heart also sees the things that are hidden from the common people.

chapters.title: Materials Are Reflections the Heart:
chapters.subtitle: Narrative of a sufi, who had kept his head down upon his knees in meditation; and peoples’ telling him to raise his head and see the garden, flowers and birds

paras: A sufi, in connection with his spiritual observation was sitting in a garden as is the sufi practice, with his head upon his folded knees. He sank deep into himself and was lost to himself. A senseless fellow got disturbed at this type of sleeping and said: “Why do you sleep in such a beautiful garden? Wake up and look at the grapes, trees and greenery as the Queen has said: “contemplate the memorials of God’s mercy! ― He gives life to the earth after

sections.heading: Death”: “Fanzur Ilaā Āţhāri Rahmatillaahi Kaifa Yuhil Arda Ba‘ada Mawtihā”: (Rum: 30:
paras: 50). Obey the command of God to look toward the symbols of His benefit.”

sections.heading: All Things Are Reflections of Heart
paras: The sufi said: “O the one involved in these material signs! Know that, heart is His sign. It is the real sign and all things outside it are signs of the heart. Gardens and their signs are in the heart. Gardens and their signs are in the heart. What is outside is only signs are in the heart. What is outside is only its reflections as is seen in flowing water. Water contains the reflection of the heart which appears to be shaking because of water’s cleanliness. Gardens and fruits are in the heart and it is its subtlety, which falls on mud and water. If it were not be due to the pleasure of the heart, there would not have been the reflection of the cypress tree. It is for this reason that God has called material world as a place of frauds. This fraud is the reflection of the hearts and souls of men, which is considered by many as real. All are the victims of this frauds and who consider the world as a paradise.

sections.heading: Spiritual Death Before Physical Death
paras: They run away from the truth to the base of the gardens and go on blabbering about this reflection. When they come out of their sleep, they will see things in reality. But this seeing will not of any benefit for them. That is why, there are great sighs and cries in graveyards which will last till the doomsday. That man is very fortunate who dies well before physical death. That is, he is well aware of the reality of the grave yard which is a place of grief and sighs and turmoil, before this death.

chapters.title: Growth of Ķharrūb Plant
chapters.subtitle: Growth of the Ķharrūb plant in a corner of the masjid and H. Sulaimān’s grief upon this, when the plant spoke of its name and qualities

paras: As was his routine, one day, H. Sulaimān entered into the masjid and found a new kind of plant in a corner with ears of grains upon it. It was a rare, strange, green plant. Its greenery was so fine and pleasing that the eyes would not turn away from it. The plant saluted H. Sulaimān and he responded well which further increased its beauty, H. Sulaimān asked its name, and it said: “O king of the world, my name is “Ķharrūb”. H. Sulaimān asked: “what property do you have in you?” And it replied: “In whichever home I grow, destruction comes upon it. As I am Ķharrūb as my name itself is derived from the word Ķharāb which means bad. Therefore, I am a cause of bad results. I am the one to destroy whatever is built with mud and water.” Upon this H. Sulaimān thought within himself: “My death is approaching and I have to go on the final journey. So long as I am alive, this masjid will remain protected from calamities of the earth. This masjid will not meet destruction during my life time. Therefore, the destruction of this masjid will come about only after my death.”

sections.heading: Ķharrūb of the Heart
paras: The heart, the body of which performs worshipful acts itself (salāt) is a masjid. And whosoever’s heart becomes a masjid like this, and a bad man becoming his friend is like Ķharrūb. When the love for a bad friend grows in you, be very careful do not talk to him, but run away from him. Pluck out his love from its very roots, as, if it grows, it will destroy you and the masjid of your heart. Ķharrūb also grows in the heart of a disciple like cripple, when he crawls like a child. Call yourself as ignorant and criminal, and fear these qualities, so that your guide may not be reluctant to teach you. Saying that I am ignorant and teach me, is a kind of justice to the self and a greatness.

sections.heading: Admit Wrong; Offer No Excuses
paras: Learn this from your grandfather, H. Ādam, the one with a bright forehead. When he realized this wrong, he instantly admitted and said: “O lord! We have wronged our own souls”: “Rabbanā zhalmanā anfusinā”: (A‘raaf: 7: 23). Neither he offered excused not resorted to raising the flags of cheating. On the contraty, Iblis started arguments, saying: “I was red faced with pride but you made me pale faced with shame. You are the provider of colours. You are the one to give me colour by turning me from red to pale. You alone are the root of sin, my troubles and disgrace. Read what he said to God as stated in the Qurān: “O my Lord! Because, you have put me in the wrong”: “Rabbī bimā aghwaitanī”: (Al-Hijr: 15: 39). That is: “I did what I did, because of Your own act of putting me on that line through predestination,”

sections.heading: Predestination Is an Excuse for Faults
paras: Read this well and reflect so that you may not fall into the darkness of predestination and go wrong. How long do you want to jump upon the branches of the tree of predestination and keep aside your free will to act which is a power given to you by God. That is: you can do what you want to do. How long do you want to quarrel and argue with God on predestination like Iblis and his progeny? Man commits sins with his own pleasure and choice. If the commission of your sins is under the impact of predestination, why does he feel pleased and run after them. How can anyone dance with pleasure while committing sins instead of feeling sorry for sins. You quarrel with advisers with a might and force of not yours alone but of twenty persons. You tell them in a rough manner: “what I am doing is perfectly correct and my way is the best. None can find fault with me other than the incompetent.”

sections.heading: Only Helpless Plead Predestination
paras: One under the impacts of predestination is a helpless fellow. His vociferous arguments say that he is not helpless. How can he engage in such quarrels, when he is on the wrong under the force of predestination? You adopt for yourself whatever is of your choice and pleasure, but when your wisdom tells you not to de that, you plead: ‘I am predestined to do that.’

sections.heading: Love Should Be Above Wisdom
paras: One who is shrewd and fortunate knows that pleading of excuses is an act of Satan and H. Ādam’s act is a product of love. Swimming in the sea is cleverness, which cannot be for long: one has to come out of it. If he persists in swimming alone, his ultimate end is drowning. Shrewdness cannot be resorted to in the affairs of God. They are not so simple. Stop swimming and eliminate pride and jealousy God’s affairs are not a stream or river, but a fathomless ocean. This is very deep and coastless and so large that it can sweep away all the seven oceans like a scrap of grass. On the contrary, love is a boat for those in love with God, which has very few risks but assured deliverance. Wisdom is of no use in the place, but madness of love is! sell away your wisdom and purchase estrangement. wisdom is full of suspicions but estrangement is real observation.

sections.heading: Arrogance Destroys One’s Wisdom
paras: Surrender your wisdom before H. Muhammed Mustafā and think of the advice given to him by God and follow it. The advice is: “Say: Sufficient to me: There is not God but He: On Him

sections.heading: Is My Trust”: “Faqul: Hasbiyallāhu, Lā Ilāha Illā Huwa; ‘Alaihi Tawakkaltu”: (Tauba: 9:
paras: 129). Unlike Kan‘án, son of H. Noah, do not discard the baot as he was led astray by the cunning, misguided wisdom of the self. He had said: “I shall climb upon a strong hill to save myself. Why should I be under the obligation of H. Noah?” O misguided fellow, how can you protect yourself other than through his support when God also feels to oblige and grave him. O arrogant jealous fellow! Even God admits of his obligation in His way.

sections.heading: Inspired Knowledge Is Preferable
paras: How good it would have been for him, if Kan‘án had not learnt swimming in which case he would have connected himself with H. Noah and his boat. How good it would have been, if he was ignorant like a child, in which case he would not have used his imperfect wisdom to plead for him, but taken the support of H. Noah, just as a child seeks the support of his mother. Or, he had been not in possession of formal teaching (misteaching) and received some teaching from a saint who receives inspirations upon his heart from God. When this kind of light of knowledge is before you, you should not bring before it the knowledge learnt from books. In such a case, your soul familiar with inspired knowledge gets disgusted of you.

sections.heading: When Ignorance Is Bliss
paras: This acquired formal knowledge as against ablution with flowing water (wuzu). Tayammum is not permissible when water is available. Formal acquired knowledge has no worth before the statement of those with inspired knowledge. Pose yourself as ignorant and ill-witted before them and follow them from behind, in which case you will get rid of your ignorance and misguidance. Know this: many dwellers of paradise are ignorant and simpletons as stated by the noble Prophet: (Dwellers of paradise are simpletons ― Hadith) to explain this point.

sections.heading: Forlornness Better Than Shrewdness
paras: Your shrewdness, like arrogance bloats you with the air of false pride. Become forlorn to keep your faith intact. Forlornness does not mean foolishness which gives rise to jokes and laugher. Not even the foolishness of collection of wealth by hard-heartedness. Forlorn is of a man in love, who ignores everything and remains devoted to the beloved. He remains wonderstruck at the sighting of the beloved and gets lost in the beloved. He puts a yoke of friendship and love around his neck and feels its tightness as a great relief. Those women of Egypt were forlorn and deeply absorbed who remained unaware of their own hands and remained wonderstruck at the extraordinary beauty of H. Yūsuf. They forgot themselves and peeled off their fingers instead of peeling apples.

sections.heading: Surrender Wisdom to Love
paras: Sacrifice your wisdom for the love of the friend (God) because wisdom also comes from the same place where the friend (God) is. Men of greater wisdom sent their wisdom to that place itself from where it came. That is, to understand the action and attributes of God and through them, God Himself. But the senseless and foolish use their wisdom in the affair of the materials of this world. Like the earlier men of greater wisdom, if your wisdom gets lost in estrangement and wonder of God, your head, and every hair of your head becomes, not possessor of wisdom but wisdom itself. On this side, there is no tension of worries and thinking and searching wisdom, as it creates gardens and forests of its own choice. These are such gardens and forests from which your date palms are provided with water, and your dates get refreshed. Also, they provide you with such information’s which you cannot get anywhere else. Give up your sense of pride in this path of love so that your leader may not be disturbed with the movements and arrangements of the possessions of pride remain motionless to avoid disturbance to your master. One who shakes his head without any purpose, has his head not as head but as tail and its movement is like the movement of the tail of scorpion, which has its venomous sting in the tail. Such a fellow walks in a crooked manner, being blind of eyes, vicious and poisonous. His profession is to spoil clean, healthy bodies and souls. Crush the heads of the fellows of the nature as they always have bad conduct and character. Crushing of the head of such a fellow is in his own interest, so that his soul may get out as pieces of the crushed head and rid him of his vicious body. Take away the weapons from the hands of a mad fellow, so that goodness and justice may remain pleased and obliged to you. When his hands have weapons, and wisdom is not in him, it is better that he and his hand are kept bound, as otherwise he will cause a hundred injuries.

chapters.title: Rule by Incompetent Fellows
chapters.subtitle: To explain that acquisition of learning, wealth and honour by the ill-natured is disgraceful for him and is like giving sword in the hands of dacoits

sections.heading: Havoc Caused by Incompetent Rulers
paras: Giving knowledge and act to an ill-natured fellow is like giving sword in the hand of a dacoit. It is better to give a sword in the hand of a drunken Zangi (inhabitant of zang/negro) than to give knowledge to an incompetent. Knowledge, wealth, honour, high status, and connections will prove to be a calamity in the hands of a man of baser qualities. It is for this reason that jihād is duteous upon the faithful so that they may snatch weapons from such hands. His soul is mad and his body is a sword; and therefore, snatch the sword from this ill- natured fellow. An elevated status of one ignorant fellow brings about calamity to humanity which even a hundred lions would not bring about. His inherent defects remain hidden, but get exposed upon his attaining the status. His snake-like qualities come out from the snake pits and run about in the forest. The entire forest becomes full of snakes and scorpions, when an incompetent fellow becomes a king issuing bitter commands. An incompetent fellow upon getting wealth and status goes in search of disgrace for himself. Either he behaves in a miserly manner and avoids giving of grants; or if he shows generosity, it is on wrong occasions and upon undeserving persons. He dishonors the noble people putting them in tight corners. These are the types of the grants from an ill-witted fellow. When political power goes into the hands of such misguided fellow. He considers it only as a place of honour, but it becomes a deep well for him. He knows no way to lead but becomes a guide for viciousness and sets fire to the world.

sections.heading: Leadership of False Guides
paras: Similarly, when a childish fellow resorts to teaching and guidance, his disciples are caught hold of by the devils of misfortune and immorality. He tells them: “come with me so that I may show you the truth of God like a bright moon of spiritual world, when he has not even seen the moon of this world in a proper manner. When you have not seen the clear worldly moon itself in your whole life, how can you as an unripe fool show the moon to others, when even its reflection is not seen by you in water. When fools become leaders, wise men, out of fear hide their heads under blankets.

chapters.title: The Wrapped Up to Get Up
chapters.subtitle: Explanation and exegesis of: O the wrapped up! ‘Ya-ayyuhal muzzammilu’: (Muzzammil: 73: 1)

sections.heading: Come Out to Guide the Unguided
paras: The prophet was addressed as “The wrapped up” to tell him: you have distanced yourself from the people and wrapped up yourself in seclusion. Get out of it. Do not keep your head under the blanket hiding your face from the people, because the world is a body full of confusions and only you are in clear mind. Do not hide yourself out of the fear of the disgrace that the enemy would cause, as you have got the bright-light-spreading-lamp of inspiration. You are to stand up for prayer at night (Qumillaila), O competent one like the lamp, which stands erect and lit for the whole night. Without your light, even the day is like dark night, without your support even a lion is a prisoner of the rabbit. Become a shipmaster in this large ocean, as you are like another Noah. A wise knower of the ways is required for the people to guide on all the ways and particularly in water ways.

sections.heading: Prophet to Avoid Seclusion
paras: “Get up and look at the looted and misled caravan. Every devil has become a shipmaster everywhere. You are the Khizr of the time and you are the support for every ship. Like Jesus Christ, do not resort to seclusion in this world, and also go away to the heaven alone. You are like a lamp in this gathering and therefore do not resort to separation and seclusion. This is not a time to remain aloof, O guide! Come into the gathering. You are like the huma from the Caucasus Mountain. The full moon moves upon the chest of the sky at night and it never cares at the barking of dogs. You may also do so and do not stay put and stop moving. Your opponents are like barking dogs while passing unpalatable remarks upon you because of your high grade. These dogs are deaf of the command of “keep quiet” of the Qurān which says: “When the Qurān is read, listen to it with attention and hold your peace”: “Wa izā Qurī al Qurānu fastami‘ū lahu wa anșitūn”: (A‘raf: 7: 204). That is why, with their foolishness they bark at you. But you should not leave the sickman without treatment. Do not deprive these deaf and blind of the walking stick. Have you not said: “One who puts the blind on the way gets a hundred rewards from God.” And also, that: “one who takes a blind man for forty steps gets his sins pardoned and gets proper guidance.” Therefore, you may take the men, blinded by the destructible world, away from it in ranks after ranks. This is the job of the guides and you are a guide. You are a cause of joy for the people of the last of the periods.

sections.heading: God Helps the Prophets Against Enemies
paras: “O leader of the pious! Take these men full of suspicious toward certainty. I shall hit upon the neck of the one who put efforts to play tricks with you. Therefore, go forward with confidence. I shall add further blindness upon the blind so as to make them consider poison as sugar, which they will receive from me. They have brightened their wisdom with my wisdom. So also, they have learnt tricks from the tricks that I pray. But these cannot be greater than mine. What is the worth of a tent of blankets erected by the Turkmans before the male elephants of the world? (Turkmans were a tribe of desert dacoits). How can their lamp burn against the waves of my fast winds? In view of all this, what do you, my great messenger, think of yourself?

sections.heading: Doomsday Arrives
paras: “Get up and blow air into the frightening bulge so that thousands of dead bodies may come from underneath the mud. As you are the Isrāfīl of the present time, get up and bring up a doomsday well before the arrival of the great real doomsday. Show yourself to anyone who asks as to where is the doomsday, and tell them: “Look here, I am the doomsday.” [The noble Prophet has said: ‘Myself and the doomsday have been sent together”. That is to say just as the doomsday separates the truth from falsehood so also. I do ―Qazi Sajjad Hussain]. Tell the questioner: Lok here! That is: Hundreds of new worlds will about because of me. Dead persons will receive new souls from me and come to life.”

sections.heading: Greatness of the Prophet Cannot Be Explained
paras: If he is not capable of understanding and accepting this, them O king! The answer to a foolish question is silence. When a fellow supplicates for a foolish thing which cannot be accepted by God, the answer that comes from the sky is silence. What a tragedy! The time for harvest came; but to our misfortune, it passed off. That is: the opportunity for the speaking of the greatness of the Prophet has come now, but the time to speak is so short that I cannot do. Time available is too little to speak of it. Even an everlasting life is too less for it. An expert spearman cannot show his skill from the depth of a pit. If he tries, he fails and is put to shame. Time is too short and the taste and wisdom of the common people is also so limited as a hundred times lesser than the available time. This being the case of deficiency and your own saying that the answer for the foolish question is silence, why did you speak of all this in such a lengthy manner. I submit: I am compelled by the circumstance provided by God. He has made me to say so through the wave of His mercy and grant. Because, he fells rain on both fertile and rocky land and wettens them.

chapters.title: Not Answering Is Answer
chapters.subtitle: Explanation of the statement: not answering itself is an answer and the answer to a foolish question is silence. Both as the same can be seen in the following narrative

paras: A king had a servant, whose wisdom was dead, but his passions were alive. He did not perform even small jobs for him and used to speak ill of the king and considered this as a good act. The king ordered for the reduction of his salary; and if he were to make hue and cry, he may be dismissed and his name may be struck off from the register of employees. That servant’s wisdom was deficient but his greed was more. When his salary was reduced, he became all the more wild and rebellious. Had he been wise, he would have taken note of his own defects and sought pardon, upon which his status restored.

sections.heading: No Self-Introspection
paras: Leg of the donkey is tied upon its misbehavior, and upon further instilling, the other leg is also tied. Then, the donkey says: “Do not tie the other leg. One leg’s tying is enough.” It should know that the other leg is also tied for its meanness of not giving up its first wrong. If it had known the cause of first tying, and got rid of the first wrong, the second leg’s tying would not have been done. Rather, the tied first leg would have been released. Instead of looking at the ties, had it known the reason for tying, it would have behaved better and got rid of the first tying also. There is another aspect: had it not committed the wrongs, it would not have been a foolish donkey but a male lion.

chapters.title: Difference Between Angels, Animals and Man
chapters.subtitle: In the exegesis of the Hadith: God created the angels and kept wisdom in them; and the animals, and kept passions in them; and the children Ādam, and kept in them both wisdom and passion. One who increases wisdom over passion becomes an angle. One who increases passion upon wisdom, will be lowlier than the animals. What the Prophet said is true

paras: It has come in a Hadith that great god created three types of creatures of the world: one group has knowledge, wisdom and perfectness in generous acts. They are the angels. They do not know about anything excepting complete obedience. They do nto have any element of greed and desires. They are perfect light and exists only in this love of God. There is another group of creatures which have not wisdom at all. They are just living beings interested only in food and fattening. They do not look at anything other than food and a place to live. They are totally ignorant of the nobility of heart, and know nothing. They are animals.

sections.heading: Man Has Both Qualities
paras: Then, there is the third group of humans, as children of Ādam. They are half from angels and half from donkeys. Their one part, half of donkish instinct is inclined only towards the lowly material world (Nasoot) and the other angelic half toward the upper world (Lāhūt). Both these halves are at loggerheads with each other. It has to be seen as to which half defects the other half and dominates. If the wisdom dominates, he gets highly elevated and becomes more worthy than angels. On the contrary, if passions dominate, he becomes lowly and worse than animals and wretched.

sections.heading: Angelic Men
paras: Both these halves ― groups of angels and animals are engaged in mutual fights in man and man in these quarrels is in a calamity. All these men put together are divided into three groups and are always under trial. They are all men to look at, but in character they are different. One group is totally sunk in goodness and joined with the group of angels like Jesus Christ. They are like men in physical appearance, but deep inside, they are like the angel Jibra‘īl. They are free from anger, passion and quarrels. They have crushed their viciousness though austerities to such and extent that they do not need them after getting purified, like angels, as though they were not born out of man.

sections.heading: Man of Animal Character
paras: The others joined the group of donkeys, and are perfect animals, getting involved always in wrath and are personified passions. The angelic qualities that they had totally vanished. It had a narrow place of residence in the body as it was fat, and finding no place to reside it left. Such a person is like a dead body. He has no life as that of the angel. He becomes a donkey with the less of angelic qualities. He also becomes meanly like the crows and follows their nature. His life becomes a material body after losing its manly qualities. As, such a life does not possess its original manly qualities. It becomes lowly. Thus, he is what the Sufis, who remain at the higher level of angels, also say. He gets into more troubles than animals and performs every intricate acts in the world.

sections.heading: Sciences and Arts of Worldly Man
paras: The acts of treachery and designs that he does are so intricate that other animals cannot do. He weaves fabrics of gold and brings out pearls from the sea. Intricate points of mathematics are brought out by him and of astronomy, medicine and philosophy. Thus, he gets involved in such sciences which bring about betterment of this worldly life as he is upto the seventh heaven from where he can learn other sciences of the other world; the next life of spirits and angels. All his sciences are for the construction and making of the comforts of life such as stables and pillars for the comforts of horses, cows and camels, for the life of a few days of this world. These ill-witted fellows name these sciences as the learning of secrets of nature and creatures (both living and non-living).

sections.heading: Sciences of Human Soul and Heart
paras: The knowledge of the science of the next life or the stages of life of the path of God, the Asolute Truth, are known to men of hearts and their hearts. These relate to the affairs of the human soul as against the animal soul of man. Man as the only possessor of human soul as against all other creatures along with the instinct of ferocious beasts and other soft animals is a special combination of all. God has also granted wisdom to man which He has not given to others. Some humans are deprived of it and they contain only animal instincts. They are stated by Him to be like cattle, rather worse than them. That is: “They are like cattle, − nay more misguided”: “Kal an‘āmu bal hum adhallu”: (A‘raf: 7: 179). Their opposing instinct is like the opposing of sleep and wakefulness.

sections.heading: Qualities of Animal Soul
paras: Animal soul does not possess anything other than sleep in its mental capacities. Even in wakefulness it is as though asleep. Only their bodies work, but the animal soul always sleeps. They possess perverse senses. Even when they are awake, their animal soul continues to sleep. They see the perverse reflection of the writings of their own deeds. Like in the dreams. But when the real wakefulness comes, they will see that what they had seen was perverse. Then they realize that they are lowly among all other lowly ones. That is what God has said: “We have indeed created man in the best of the moulds; then do We abase him to be the

sections.heading: Lowest of the Low”: “Laqad Khalaqnal Insāna Fī Ahsani Taqwīm; Thumma Ra Dad Nāhu
paras: asfala al sāfilīn”: (Tin: 95: 4, 5). Get rid of this and give up the love for destructibles or setting stars and sun as H. Ibráhīm had said after the setting of stars, moon and sun: “I love not those that set”: “Innī lá uhibbul áfilīna”: (An‘aam: 6: 76)

sections.heading: Cursing Self-Satisfied Self, Commanding Self (Lawwamā, Mutma ‘Innā, Ammarā)
paras: Man went into the lowest of the low as he did not use the capacity to alter his animal instinct into higher human or angelic instincts, though he had preferred to live in the lowly physical comforts and achievements of the material world, which destroyed him and prevented him from going to higher levels. When he spoils these abilities in him, whatever him go more and more toward physical comforts. What all he consumes is like what the donkey consumes. If he eats baladar which acts as a medicine for mental shock, it becomes opium for him and increases his stupefying effect and lack of wisdom. Yet, there is another group of men which is half animal and half as guided one. This of those who are victims of the nafs-e-lawwāmā, (the cursing self). The first category of those who are fully satisfied with what they are doing either of this worldly or that worldly affairs have nafs-e-Mutma’innā (the satisfied self). The other one is of those who are in the struggle between animal instinct (vicious self) and human instinct (wisdom) who have nafs-e- ammārā (the commanding self). They are in a situation of pulling and pushing during both day and night. There is a pull from this side and a push from the other continuously.

chapters.title: Tussle Between Wisdom and Desire
chapters.subtitle: Tussle between wisdom and self is like the tussle between Majnūn and the she camel. Majnūn wanted to go forward towards Lailā and the she camel backward toward its calf which was left behind; And Majnūn’s telling: My camel’s inclination is on the backside and mine on the front side, both are in a different direction

paras: Tussle between the self of man and wisdom is like the tussle that Majūn had with his she- camel, in which at one time the she-camel dominated and at another time Manjūn. His self- drags him forward and wisdom drags backward. Majūn’s inclination was to go forward to meet Lailā, but the camel’s was towards its calf that was left behind.

sections.heading: Both Dominated by Love
paras: People are certainly like Majnún and the camel. Their self and wisdom drag them in opposite directions. Majnún wanted to go forward but the she-camel backward. When Majnún wanted to go forward but she-camel backward. When Majnún became careless about himself for a little time, the camel turned backward. As his body was dominated by love and infatuation, becoming tired and going unconscious for some time was inevitable. The thing to control him was his wisdom and through it to control his body, but love for Lailā had snatched away his wisdom. But the she-camel was very smart and waterful. Whenever she found the rein loose, she used to understand that the rider is careless and disengaged, she turned back towards its calf. Upon getting consciousness, Majnún would know that she has gone in the opposite direction for miles together. A journey of three days kept him engaged for years. He said: “O my camel, we are both in love. We are having opposing destinations and therefore are not fit to travel together. Your love and my rein do not co-ordinate. It is better that I remain away from you. We as companions are dacoits for eachother.”

sections.heading: Man’s Body and Soul Have Opposite Destinations
paras: Similarly, a man totally engaged in the affairs of the body is also in misguidance. Desires of the soul and body are different. Soul, because of its separation from ‘arsh (imperium, the abode of souls from which it comes into the world and gets imprisoned in man’s body), is anxious to go back to the place of its origin, but the body is hungry of the pleasures of the world like the camel, hungry for thorny branches of trees. The soul opens its wings to go high to its abode, but the body has entangled itself with earthly materials.
