So, thinking, Majnún said to the camel: “O lover of your country, so long as you are with me, my soul will remain away from my Lailá. My life is getting spent in this struggle, just as the followers of H. Músá, who were lost in the desert of Tia. Every morning they would move to go out of it and struggle for the entire day and come back to the starting point in the same place in the evening. The distance of my destination was just steps, but because of your treachery I was held up for sixty yeats (whole life). The way was very closeby, but it took a long time. I got disgusted to the fullest extent with this riding.” He felled himself down from the camel saying: “How long am I to burn myself in the fire of sorrows?” The vast expanse of the forest appeared very narrow for him. He dropped himself upon rocky land. He dropped himself in such a way that with bad luck, his leg also broke. He bandaged his leg with a strip of cloth and said: “not being able to walk anymore, I shall round up myself and roll like a ball and move towards my destination, like the ball batted by the player. This is how sweet-tongued-philosopher, Sanaai says: ‘I curse upon the rider who does not get down from the body that carried the soul.”

sections.heading: Strange Journey Towards God
paras: Love for God cannot be lesser than the love for Lailá, it is better to get rounded up like a ball to roll on, than to walk on legs. Become a ball and roll on the path of truth and reach the destination of God. As you move towards God in this manner, you will be dragged by the curved end of the stick (hockey stick) towards God. This will be a journey which starts with your side with difficulty but gets pulled forward later by God without efforts from your side, as against a journey on the camel which has to be with your efforts till the end. This journey is different from other journey as it is without the company of those of the same species and support of men and jinns. This is not a normal type of journey. This is a special journey which is organized by the excellence and blessing of Prophet Muhammed. This much is enough for the present. Salutations to you. This has kept me away from the narrative of the king’s servant who had sent a message to the king.

chapters.title: Reading of Letters
chapters.subtitle: The servant’s letter to the king regarding reduction of his salary

paras: The king’s servant sent a letter, expressing his haughtiness, self-appraisal and contempt to the sophisticated king. A written letter is a body and look at but it has to be keenly seen whether it is worthy of being sent to the king. If you find that it is improper, tear it off and write down another with appropriate words.

sections.heading: Reading of Topic Heads Is Misleading
paras: It is easy to open a letter and read it, but opening the body of man which is an envelope containing the letter is not easy. It is very difficult to read a man’s inside, as otherwise, everyone would be capable of knowing everyone’s secrets. Opening the man’s letter is very difficult to see his inside as it is the job of very capable persons, and not of children engaged in playing. We are all so incapable that we look at the heading of writings and remain satisfied with that, as we are full of greed and desires and hesitate to read the full text. The heading of letters are misleading like nets for the common people who take the full text also to contain the same as the headlines is. Therefore, one should read the entire text without reluctance to know fully. Read the entire text though it is difficult to read and know in full, yet God alone knows best.

sections.heading: Read the Intentions and Not Words Alone
paras: Similarly, what you hear from a man by his words is only a verbal statement. This may not be the same as the speaker intended. Therefore, you should read the text of letter of his heart, and decipher it, to see whether it is in accordance with what is stated by mouth, so that there may not be any hypocrisy; and by relying upon the stated words, you may not be liable to be a hypocrite. When you are carrying a large bag, the minimum for you is to know as to what it contains. Whether it contains bitter or sweet things. If you find the contents as worthy, you may carry it, otherwise do not. Otherwise, you may empty the useless stones from the bag and protect yourself of the ensuring quarrels; and the disgrace of carrying worthless materials. Fill the bag with such things which are worthy of being taken to the ruler and kings of guidance of the other world. And it is totally wrong to carry a bag full of sand and anything of lesser value. If you cannot carry rubies to them, you may go empty handed. The best thing you can carry is good character. Which you can keep in your inside (heart) and present it in the form of good behavior through your outside (body)

chapters.title: Thief Cheated by a Fraud
chapters.subtitle: Story of a jurist who wore a big headdress and a thief who carried it away and the jurist’s calling at him to first open it and see its content and then take it away

paras: A jurist collected torne pieces of clothes and patched them in his headdress, so that it may appear fat and large, when he would go into gatherings and give lectures. He had patched it with torne pieces of various colours to make it beautiful to look at. Its external appearance was like the beautiful dress of paradise but its inside was ugly, disgraceful and rough like the hypocrite. Pieces of old clothes, cotton and leather were buried in it. Early in the twilight of morning he left for a school, so that with the grand looks of the headdress he may receive good offerings. In an empty street, a thief of such perfection in theft as to steal the apparels from the bodies of men was waiting to exhibit his skill. He took away the headdress from the jurist’s head and ran away to meet his next object. The jurist shouted at him: “O young man open the headdress first, look inside and then take it. You are flying in the air with four feathers. Open up what you carry as a prize and see it well. Open it up and test it with your head and then take it away. I have pardoned you. While on the run the thief opened it and thousands of torne pieces of clothes spread over on the street. Everything came out of this fat dress and what left in his hand was one yard of old cloth band. He got wild and threw that piece of cloth and said to the jurist: “O unworthy fellow! With this trick of yours, you caused obstacle in my job. What kind of treachery, trick and fraud is this, that you got me caught in the net of bird which had caught? Are you not ashamed of these torne pieces? You are a fraud. You have treacherously caught me in your fraud.” The jurist said: “I have cheated the people. But I am sincere to you that I told you the entire truth.” This is how the world appears beautiful at first and later shows its ugliness

chapters.title: World Is a Great Adviser
chapters.subtitle: World’s advice to the worldly men with its, appearance itself; and exposure of its faithlessness to the searchers of truth

paras: In similar manner, the world appears fresh and pleasing, yet it speaks of its defects in aloud manner. Know this wise man! Deep inside this decoration, there is destruction. Its beauty is a treachery and its destruction is a lesson for you. Its beauty says: “Come to me I am a prosperous step;” and the destruction says: “go away from me as I am nothing in worth.”

sections.heading: Fading of Beauties, Fouling of Delicious Dishes
paras: O the who gapes at the beauty of the spring! Look at its winter and paleness. Everyday you see a bright beautiful face of the morning sun. consider its deathly state at the time of setting in the evenings. You see the full moon as a grand beauty spreading light in the four directions: and from next day onwards, look at the reduction of beauty and light. A beautiful boy is a darling of everyday, loved and respected by all as a master. As he entered into old age, he became ugly and honourless among fools. If silvery beauties have trapped you in their love as a hundred animal, you may look at them in old age when they become like a cotton crop in the field. O the one searching and looking for tasty, fatty dishes! Get up and go to the latrine and see them as ugly, foul-smelling shit. Ask that dirty shit as to what happened to its greatness, beauty, appreciable state and its capacity to invite each and all? You were floating in the dish in style with softness and attractiveness, and with your grand appearance wonderfulness and five fragrances on the dining sheet! It will say: “I was a grain and the net to catch the birds, when you were trapped, I went out to your sight.”

sections.heading: Everything Deteriorates and Turns Useless
paras: Fingers of great artisans and craftsmen were so active and decorating that, other great masters looked them with awe, but in the end, in old age they shiver. Beautiful-narcissus like life inspiring-eyes become watery losing all charm. That brave fellow who rushes into the ranks of lions becomes so weak as to fear a rat. Far sighted expert professionals, lose all talent and become dull like old donkeys. Pleasant, fragrant intoxicating curly hair lose all their value and become ugly like the donkey’s tail. Look at the pleasant beauty of anything the world in the early stage and its ugliness and uselessness in the later stage. It has only shown a net to please you, so that you may enter into it with pride. It is your own folly that you did not see its treachery. You say that it has caught you by pleasing you, as otherwise your wisdom was not one to be defected by it. Look at the golden necklaces, and shoulder strips to hang your sword, which later became yokes, chains and handcrafts for you. Consider everything of the world as such, and consider both its beginning and end. One who looks at the end of anything is fortunate; and one who is pleased with the seeing of the grazing horses is far away from sense. Look at the proud moon-like face in the beginning and also at the end. So that, you may not be one like the one-eyes Iblīs, which looked at the apparent outside of Ādam and not at his inner greatness. He looked at the mud of which he was made but not at his inner wisdom. He looked at this world and not at the other.

sections.heading: Why Men Are Superior to Women
paras: Men are superior to women not for the reason of their strength, earning and property. Lions and elephants as stronger than man. They are superior because they look at the end of things in a better way. A man who is not perfect in seeing the end of things is lesser than women who looks at the end.

sections.heading: Man: Caught in Opposite Pleadings
paras: Two types of opposite voices come from the world. One sound wakes up the good and cultured people, the other sound is a treachery for the heard-hearted. Hear the sound of the flower and the throne, and think over both, and incline towards the voice of the thorn, which is a sound of warnings. It says: “I am a thorn and the other one is a flower on the same twig. The flower falls down, but I continue to remain.” The flower says: “The thorn is a seller of flowers and come to me.” But the thorn says: “Do not try to come near me.” You get puzzled. You go toward one voice and ignore the other. Flower and thorn are opposed to each other, just like the lover who is deaf to the refusals of the beloved. He persists in his love how much ever the beloved avoids.

sections.heading: See the Future End
paras: There is another voice which says: “this is my present and look at it.” And the other voice says: “look at my end. My present is tricky and treacherous. Therefore, do not get cheated but look at my future in the mirror of your wisdom.” If you choose one of these, you become inimical to the other and unfit for it. That man is fortunate who hears that later voice first, which the ears and wisdom of men have heard (as against women’s). He looks at the distant results. When he finds a vacant house, he occupies it without bothering about its being fit or otherwise. He does not care to find any fault in it. Freshly made earthen pot which has absorbed urine first cannot get cleansed of it with water.

sections.heading: Attraction Between Things
paras: Everything in the world attracts another. Infidelity attracts the infidel and guidance attracts the guided. There is the grass kahruba that attracts other scraps of grass and so also magnet that attracts iron. These are the nets to attracts others. If you are iron, you are taken away by magnet; and if you a scrap of grass, kahruba moves around you. If you are not a friend of the good people. Certainly, you go close to the vicious. One who befriended the thorn, becomes disgraced as a companion of thorns.

sections.heading: Good for One Is Bad for Another
paras: H. Mūsā was vicious in the eyes of Copts of the race of Pharaoh and Hāmān wa a hatable fellow in the view of bani-Israīl of H. Mūsā’s community. Hāmān’s soul attracts the Copts and H. Mūsā’s soul attracts the sabtis (bani-Israīl). Stomach of the donkey drags grass and man’s stomach drags the contents of wheat. If you cannot understand all this with the darkness of your mind. You may search for the one who is made as a leader by God. Every body of animal goes behind its mother which exhibits its species. Man gets milk from the breasts on the upper part of the body and donkey gets from the lower part of the body.

chapters.title: God: Provider for All
chapters.subtitle: To explain that the Gnostics of God get their food from the Light of God as the Hadith says: “I spend my night with God. He provides food and drink to me.” And also, his statement: “Hunger itself is a food from God, with which He keeps alive the bodies of the Truthful by providing food Himself, the Honorable and Dominant” (Hadith)

paras: Making of provision by God the provider is just and equitable. It is a strange fact that there is no oppression and compulsion in it. Every provision is just and equitable. Everybody believes in it. If it were predestined and fateful, why would any body feel ashamed of failure and deprivation. If it were oppression, why everyone seeks God’s protection.

sections.heading: Nature Provides Food to All
paras: [Everyone is quite contented with what one is provided with. Herbivores animals go after leaves, herbs and grass; and the carnivores after flesh. Flies and insects go after filth and so on. Even among humans, people of poor countries are contented with what they get without any regret. So also, the people of earlier periods. In the rich countries also, vast majority of the people are poor and contented with what little they get. Whether rich or poor, their food to eat is from the same baser products; grains, lintels, vegetables, milk, meat and so on; which both the rich and poor eat and drink. The difference is only in providing taste and delicious and in the manner of serving, which are products of sophistication, show, pomp and superiority. If they are kept without food for some longer time than their usual, they pounce on any kind of food forgetting all their taste, sophistication and pomp. This is the natural requirement to keep body and soul together irrespective of the statuses and cultures. So many principles of economics go after, not about these basic requirements but about excesses than necessities. These are the mental aberration of high-level thinkers, and not of the vast majority of the humans in villages, forests and shabby localities of the poor and slums in the rich cities. They do not know or bother to know about the mental aberration of the over-rich, over-wise and over-fed few everywhere in the world. Supplies of non-basic things, if not provided to the village and forest dwellers and nomads in desert, humanity does not starve and vanish and manages itself in frugal ways for the time being till nature provides in abundance later. Because, God is the provider of all and everywhere as per needs. All the people donot eat the same food. Rice eaters have no value for wheat, miller etc and vice versa just to tell in one sentence. This can be elaborated in all or any manner as one chooses ― Translator] I have said a little in a nutshell and there is no scope to elaborate as evening has arrived. There is no day time to elaborate anymore now. The substance is: think over all that is happening, coming and going in the world. You will know yourself; and God knows everything best.

chapters.title: Know the True, False and Absolute
chapters.subtitle: Address to the misguided of the world and the victims of the self

paras: O the one who has reposed full confidence upon the treachery and flattery of a sinner! What you have made is like a round tent of a bubble supported with very weak ropes. Treachery is like lighting, in the light of which a traveller cannot find this path. This world and its possessors are without results and both of them have a single opinion in the matter of dishonesty. This world and its products are unfaithful even though they fact you, but their faces are really on your back.

sections.heading: Think of the Other World Also
paras: Those belongings to the other world, because of goodness, always maintain their promises and agreement. Two prophets cannot be opposite of each other. They do not snatch each other’s miracles. The fruits of that world never go bad and its pleasures do not ever turn into sorrows. Passionate self in this world is unreliable and needs to be beheaded. It is so mean and ignoble, and so also are its objects. This gathering is fit for those with vicious self. Shrouds and graves are the only fit thing for the dead bodies. Though the passionate self is very clever and well assimilating to the points of wisdom, but as its object is this world, it requires to be taken as dead. When the water of God’s inspiration reaches this dead body. It gets into life from the mud. Until the inspiration of God on to it, do not believe in it, as it goes on telling every time that life is long; and good acts can be performed in later stages of life and one should have a pleasureful life now.

sections.heading: True, False and Absolute
paras: You should go after that calling which should never mislead you; and after that sun, which never sets. These things can be had from the men of Truth. Those engaged in acts, arguments and interpretations belong to the community of Pharaoh and they are destined to sink and die in the water of river of Nile. Their beautiful appearance, greatness, grandeur and magical expertise drag people toward great pomp. But you should be careful enough with them and with the magic spells of magicians, and consider the staff of H. Mūsā as a python and causer of their death. It swallowed in a single morsel all those things that they demonstrated the night, and when morning came there was nothing to see; everything was swallowed. With this swallowing, all the darkness vanished and there was light everywhere which increased moment by moment, and took it back to the same level at which it was before that dark night. This was a light of God which is Absolute. The increase was not of the light because it is Absolute. The increase was its impacts. Absolute light neither decreases nor increases. It remains the same.

sections.heading: God, Difficult to Comprehend
paras: God’s status did not increase because of the creations. What He was prior to creation continues to be so even after creations. Increased His impacts and provided scope for understanding Him. There is a great difference in the state and impacts. A Qudsi hadith says: “I was a hidden treasure. I desired that I should be recognized, and so I created the creations.” Increase in the expositions of His greatness provided better scope to understand Him by the understanding of His acts and attributes. If we say that His state or essence increased, it means that it was lesser or deficient earlier. The eternal essence is Absolute and devoid of occurrence and deficiency. This increase in the essence is to be found in the creatures and not in the Creator, as creatures come about as accidents and are deficient due to so many causes. But that is not so with the Absolute, Eternal Essence. My dear friend there are many subtle and five points of understanding here which are difficult to comprehend. Yet be hearing these subtle points.

chapters.title: Effects of Magic and Miracles
chapters.subtitle: Exergies of the ayat: H. Mūsā feared in his heart and We told him: do not fear as you are high above: Fa awjasa fī nafsihi khīfatan Mūsā, qulnā lā taķhaf innaka anta al a‘alā

paras: H. Mūsā said: “Magic also causes confusion. What am I to do? People have no capacity to distinguish between magic and miracle.” God said: “I shall imbibe that capacity in them. I shall brighten the discriminating wisdom. When I expose the miracles. I shall make wisdom to be proud of seeing the difference [H. Mūsā’s fear was not of the magicians and their snakes but of the incapacity of the onlookers to differentiate between magic and miracle ― Qazi Sajjad Hussain]. I shall grant brightness to the discriminating wisdom. I shall make a worthless ignorant fello ws blind even if they are extracting surf from the ocean. O Mūsā! Be not afraid. You will be victorious.” Magic in those days was a qualification of pride. When H. Mūsā’s staff became a python and swallowed the products of magic, it lost its worth. [Different arts were matters of pride during different periods, but lost their worth before miracles. Medicine was a great art during the days of Jesus Christ, but lost its value before the miracles of Jesus Christ. During the days of H. Muhammad verbalism was considered as great, but before the superb qualities of the Qurān with words with indepth meanings and expressions lost their worth ― Qazi Sajjad Hussain]

sections.heading: Genuine and Counterfeit Gold
paras: Magic of the magician vanished from the scene before the miracles of H. Mūsā. Both magic and magicians do not exist anymore but became famous for their worth before the world. The fame of magic remained as a defeated and accursed art, but the fame the greatness of the religion remained everlasting high. At a time when touchstone is not available to the people to test genuine gold and imitation gold, a counterfeiter may come forward and speak of its high value. This is the only time for him to carry on his boasting. He will be highly honoured by the people. When the touchstone becomes available, it loses all its worth and his counterfeit becomes black. The imitation gold tells the genuine gold with contempt and pride: “I am not less than you in gold, O pure gold.” The genuine gold says: “Yes my friend, you are right. But wait for some times; the touchstone is arriving and be ready for the test.”

sections.heading: End of False Claimants
paras: Death of the body is a great gift to those who know the secrets of life. Just like pure gold, they do not fear being cut into piece by the goldsmith’s cutter. If the pretender of greatness like imitation gold were to know that he is going to be blackened in the end, he would have preferred to remain humble in this life instead of pretending greatness, and remained honorable at the time of meeting death. He would not have resorted to hypocrisy and falsity. He would have been a seeker of greatness. His wisdom would have dominated over his false pretentions.

sections.heading: Set Right Bad Qualities for Proper Sight
paras: When a man recognizes his wrongs and remains broken at heart, he would see the patcher of heart right before him. God’s grace would be right before him to heal the wounds of his heart. He becomes instantly connected with the patcher of broken heart. His grace sends copper towards alchemy to become worthy like gold. The one who persists in the commission of wrongs remains deprived of the graces of God. This is the example of the non-genuine shaikhs. Therefore, O pretending shaikh! Do not persist on your showy business longer. Your disciples will not remain blind always. Some day they will find out your hollowness. Light of the doomsday will brighten their eyes. Your magical spells will no longer keep their eyes overlapped with your blind folding, and you will be put to disgrace. Look at those who have seen the end to meet which they anxiously wait and desires to look at with pleasure. Do not look at those who see only the present. They have cut and snatched a few secrets of God from out of the whole secret, with which they cheat the innocent people. Such fellows are always under misguidance and doubts and consider false dawn and true dawn as the same. They cannot differentiate between dim and bright appearances. Those caravans that marched forward in the dim light of false dawn were put to loss and destruction. Therefore, my dear, wait and search for the true dawn, so that with its clarity you may find out the proper way. By attaching yourself with the true dawn of the real guide, you will see things clearly and learn to differentiate between good and bad. Every genuine thing in the world has a non-genuine pretender to put men in mistakes. He gets into difficulties who does not possess the touchstone of wisdom to find out the genuine. Now let us go to the narrative of that servant who wrote a strange letter to the king.

chapters.title: Pseudo Scholars Destroy Communities
chapters.subtitle: Warning to the pretending guides to follow the Prophets and saints

paras: [Musailama Kazzāb had proclaimed himself as prophet in the region of Yamama in Arabia and some people became his followers. During the khilafat of H. Abu Bakr, his place was raided and he was killed by H. Wahshi]

sections.heading: Mimicry Cannot Misguide Always
paras: Musailama declared that he was a prophet, and he could upset the religion of H. Muhammad with his efforts. Tell Musailama not to be arrogant. Do not look at the crescent (first night moon) and look at the end. Do not be a leader with followers to collect money from them. Keep the torch before you, make it your guide and follow it. The torch takes you towards destination with its light just as the moon does and points out the places as to where is the grain and where is the net. Whether you want or not, a lamp shows the face of the falcon and of the crow. Many crows of the religion have lit their own lamps and mimicked the sounds of the white falcons.

sections.heading: Expert in One Not in Another
paras: The bird Qata also called as Sangkhwar (stone-eater) with its sounds is helpful in indicating the source of water in the forest. But that alone is its usefulness and that travellers go in the direction of its sound for water. Becoming proud of this followership, it may learn to mimic the sound of hoopoe, but from where can it possess the secret message of H. Sulaimān that hoopoe carried to Bilqīs, the queen of Sabā.

sections.heading: Psuedo Scholars Destroy Communities
paras: Sounds of the open feathers and tied up feathers are different. Hoopoe wears a crown on its head which puts it in an elevated position among other birds, but it has no worth at all before the crown of the king. Words and points of wisdom stated by the dervishes and gnostics of God are learnt by heart by shameless fellows and repeated before innocent people to foot them and make followers. It is because of such fellows that earlier communities of prophets were destroyed who were made to misbelieve a stone as a lump of ambergris. Though such fellows had the capacity to differentiate between good and bad, which they could have used, but greed and wealth and reputation made them deaf and blind. Blindness of the really blind does not keep them away from the mercy of God, but blindness of greed is no excuse for the receipt of mercy.

sections.heading: Self-Inflicted Punishment
paras: The criminal who is ordered to be punished with the nailing of his hands and feet on the board called charmaikh punishment, can still be not far away from mercy. The king may yet pardon him. But the punishment of charmaikh of self-generated jealousy is unpardonable. O fish in the water! Look at the hook with bait carefully. The vileness of your throat will shut your eyes which prevent you from seeing the end and you will be caught. Man should look at both the beginning and end with his two eyes. Be accursed, not to be one-eyed like Iblis, the accursed, who looked at only the outside of H. Ādam, but not at his great inner abilities.

sections.heading: Law of Damages on Loss of Eyes
paras: One-eyed is the one who looks at only what is present before him like animals, which do not see what is behind them. Punching of both the eyes of an ox carries a penalty as equal to punching a single eye of man. This discrepancy is maintained in law in view of the nobility of man’s eye. That is to say: both eyes of the animals are worth half of the man’s eyes (i.e., one eye if man), because both their eyes cannot see on their own but need to be supported by the eyes of man [Left to its own eyes an ox does not see and be of use] If you punch and gouge out one eye of a man, you have to pay half of the damages payable for gouging both eyes, because man’s single eye can perform the acts that can be done by both eyes. As the beginning of the functioning of the donkeys eyes continues to be the same as at the end, though they are two, yet both perform a single job. That is: they can see only what is present before them and not what is behind. Therefore, they come under the list of one-eyed. There is no end to this discussion. Let us go to that foolish servant, who out of the greed for bread wrote the letter to the king.

chapters.title: Good Words with Bad Meanings
chapters.subtitle: The servant’s letter to claim his salary

paras: Before writing the letter, he went to the incharge officer of the royal kitchen and said: “You are the one to resort to miserliness in the kitchen of the generous king. It is far away from the kings grace to think about my meals to be reduced.” He said: “The king has issued the order in view of some reasonable object, and not out of miserliness or deficiency.” He said: “I swear upon God. It is too trivial a matter for the king to bother. Even pure old tested gold is just like mud for the king.” The incharge of the kitchen made many points, but they were all rejected by the servant’s greed. When he was provided less food at the time of breakfast, he made many remarks and blabbering, but it was of no use. He told the incharge: “You are doing all this deliberately.” But he said: “No no. I am an obedient servant. Do not consider this to have come from the branch of the tree, but from the root. Do not speak ill of the bow. The arrow is shot by the hand. See, it has been said, you did not throw when you threw but it was Allah who threw (Surah Anfaal: 8: 17). This also means that the Prophet was so close to God as to be He. Do not put this upon the Prophet but God. Look at this fact, water is polluted at its source itself.”

sections.heading: False Praises Are Effectless
paras: The servant in extreme sorrow and anger went to his house and wrote a letter to the king with full of anger. In it, he praised the king and strung the pearls of his generosity and gracefulness saying: “O the one the palm of your hand is larger than the ocean and clouds. You are the one to search for the needy to fulfill their needs. This is because, whatever the cloud gives, gives in the form of tears and cries. You palm smiles and gives dishes upon dishes of food.” In appearance, the letter contained praises, but the smell of resentment emanated from words. The letter continued: “Therefore, your jobs are rough and without charm as you are far away from inherent light. The appearance of the works of the mean fellows of showy, just as a fresh fruit rot sooner. Sooner. So also, the charm of the world exhibits is defects soon, as it belongs to the world of making and unmaking. Merely by spoken words, hearts of the hearers do not get pleased, when the praiser’s heart is full of ill will. Therefore, my heart first get cleansed of hate and ill-will and then go to praise and smartness. Praises from the mouth but hate deep inside, means treachery of tongue or treachery, pure and simple. That is why God has said: I do not see what is apparent and see what is inside as the Hadith says: Allah does not see your faces and materials but sees your hearts and actions.

chapters.title: Self-Praise by Praising Others
chapters.subtitle: Narrative of a praiser who was thankful for his own honour, but the hidden sorrows were apparent from his old clothes to say that he was a lier and self-praiser

paras: A man came from Iraq in his old torne clothes. His friends enquired about his separation from them for so long. He said: “Of course, there was along separation from you, but my journey was very prosperous and pleasant for me. The Calif granted me ten royal apparels. May there be hundreds of persons to praise and bless him.” He went on praising and thanking so much that they went beyond limits. Then, they told him: “Your wretched conditions are speaking otherwise. They speak of your lies. You do not wear anything worthy on your head and body. You appear to be burnt with troubles. You have only learnt it to be thankful, or use stolen words of thanks learnt from others. Where is the leader of your thanksgiving and praises who ought to be the sign of your claims upon your head and feet? You appear to be without any honour. Your tongue is praising the king but all the seven limbs of your body are grumbling. There are not even a pain of shoes and trousers received from the generosity and gracefulness of the king.” He said: “I have distributed in charity what all he gave me; he was never deficient in keeping me pleased. I took all his grants from him and gave them over to the orphans and poor. By giving away my materials I have purchased a long life, because I am very clean- hearted.”

sections.heading: Good Acts Leave Signs on the Face
paras: But they told him: “May prosperity be upon you that you got rid of worldly materials. But there are no impacts of these acts visible from you. There appears to be fore and smoke from your inside. There are hundreds of resentments like pricking thorns within you. Sorrows cannot be the result of generous acts. If what you say is true and correct, there ought to be some signs of love, sacrifice and consonance from you. Agreed that you have distributed your materials but where is the impact of it upon you. Floods pass off, but they leave their marks on the ground. If your eyes are black and soul-inspiring, they ought not to be blue in colour. You are sour-faced. There are no signs of cleanliness of heart in you. We feel the smell of false self-praising from your words. Generousness gives rise to hundreds of marks on the inside, and good acts always leave their impressions.

sections.heading: One Grain Creates Seven Hundred Grains
paras: If wealth gets exhausted by distribution in charity, hundreds of inner lives came about as its rewards. Carrying on cultivation on the land of God with good seeds will certainly bring about good crop. Heart of a man is a special land of God. If one grain in this land does not give a hundred grains, it cannot be considered as a large land. It is a lamakan (beyond space). It has no low level and elevation. Its base is in the heart of the gnostic (knower of God). If it does not give plenty of bunches of fruits, how can it be called as a large land. When this land of this destructible world is so fertile and does not remain without giving good yield, imagine the yield from that land of God, which is so large. There is no counting and limit of its yield. One grain produces seven hundred grains. The Qurān says: “The likeness of those who spend their wealth in Allah’s way is as the likeness of a grain which groweth seven ears, in each ear has a hundred grains”: “Mathalul lazīna yunfiquuna

sections.heading: Amwaalahum Fee Sabeelil Laahi Kamathali Habbatin Ambatat Sab‘a Sanaabila Fee Kulli Sumbulatin Mi‘atu Habbatin”: (Baqara: 2: 261) Righteous Sit with Nearly Angels
paras: You have, of course praised the king, but there is no sign of praising. Neither there is any sign on the outer nor on the inner side. The praise of the knower of God (‘aarif) is alright for God, because, it is not his mouth alone, but his hands and feet are the witness to that effect. It takes him out of a deep, dark well and releases him from the prison of the world. Silken fabric of devotion and familiar light settle upon his shoulders as the signs of his praises. He gets delivered from this world of a few days and gets in to the garden with flowing springs. He settles upon the elevated throne of unknown secrets. That becomes the place of gathering of similar persons of high level, status, grade and elevation. The Qurān says: “The righteous will dwell among gardens and rivers, firmly established in the favour of Mighty

sections.heading: King”: “Innal Muttaqeena Fee Jannaatinw Wa Nahar Fee Maq‘adi Sidqin ‘Inda Maleekin
paras: Muqtadir”: (Qamar: 54: 54, 55). This is such a dwelling of the truthful ones, in which all are happy, fresh and well off. Their praise is like the garden in spring season with hundreds of sings of greatness full of glory and grandeur. These are evidenced by the springs, date-palms and grass in the garden and beauteous surroundings. There are thousands of witnesses for them all around, who are such great witnesses as pearls in the oyster.

sections.heading: Satans Watch Men from Hidden Places
paras: But in your case, there comes the foul smell of garlic from your mouth. O boastful fellow! Your head and face are shining with your griefs. Brave fighters in the battle field identify their enemies with their smell. You may not make cries of the brave men in a boastful manner. Do not boast of the fragrance of musk from you, as the smell of onion is so glaring from you. Your breaths are revealing your secrets. You say that you have eaten the compound of rose and sugar but the fragrance of garlic is spread out around you. Do not blabber anymore! Heart is like a large housing quarter; and there are many neighbors dwelling in it. They become aware of the secrets through the windows and the heart about which no one will even suspect, and the house owner feels fully protected. Read from the Qurān that Satan and his progeny smell the conditions of man in a secret manner: It says: “He and his tribe watch you from a position where you cannot see them. We made the evil

sections.heading: Ones Friends to Those Without Faith”: “Innahu Yaraakum Huwa Wa Qabeeluhu Min Haithu Laa Tarawnahum; Innaa Ja‘alnash Shayaateena Awliyaa’a Lilazeena La Ayu‘minoon”:
paras: (A‘raaf: 7: 27) They become aware of man by such means about which man is not aware, because they are not of tangible and sensible nature and shapes. Do not try to cheat those who can test and find out. Do not be mean enough to cheat the touchstone. Touchstone has the ability to find out the genuine and the counterfeit, as God has made it a commander of the body and soul of gold. The devils with all their dirt and filth can find out the secrets of out thoughts and faith. They have secret passages in our hearts and because of their stealing capacity, we are always fallen down. Every moment we are in losses and misunderstandings because of them, which cause pain to out body and soul. Because of their stealthy ways we fall flat on our faces. They are the masters of the openings of our windows and wall breaches.

sections.heading: Saints Also Know Hearts
paras: When the devils can know so much about our affairs, how the bright-hearted saints and godly men remain unaware of our situations. Can they be at lesser level than the devils, when their souls have pitched their tents upon the heavens. Theirs are the places on the heavens towards which the devil goes stealthy, but the fire causing meteors strike him with their fiery spears. He falls down flat from the sky in such a manner as an unfortunate soldier falls after receiving a wound from the spear in the battle field. Out of their love and regard from their beloved souls, they throw away the devils down from the sky. If you are handicapped lame, blind and deaf, you are so; but not consider those great souls also to be like you. Do not give up your sense of shame, and do not boast and spoil yourself, as there are many spies on the other side of your body.

chapters.title: Saints Know Your Inside
chapters.subtitle: Diagnosis by the physicians of God of the diseases of the heart and faith by looking at the foreheads of disciples and strangers; also, from the tone of their talk, colour of the eyes; and also, without these, through the passages of their hearts as they are spies of the heart. Sit down with them with true heart

paras: Physicians of the bodies of humans are very learned men. They are aware of the sickness of your body better than you. They are so capable that with just a look at your urine they can know if your sickness. You cannot do likewise for your own self. They can diagnose all your sickness with your pulse, colour and breath. When that is so with these physicians of the world, how can the physicians of the other world remain without knowing about your sickness. The physicians of the body without any doubt understand about your sickness with the touch of your pulse, by looking into your eyes and at your colour. They are well-read people. Yet they need these signs to know your sicknesses. But the perfect godly men hear of your name from a distance and with this itself they enter into the depths of the wrap and weft of the fabric of your body and soul. Rather, they have been observing you from much earlier time, even before your birth. They are aware of all your situations. They know of each hair of your body, because they are full with the secrets of the essence of God.

chapters.title: Great Men Know of Future Great Men
chapters.subtitle: Giving of happy news of the birth of Adul Hasan Kharraqāni by H. Baayazīd (May his secrets remain pure), many years before birth and pointing out of his physical appearance and of character; and the writing down of the news by historians for verification later.

paras: [Baayazīd Bistami’s (d. 874) real name was Taifur and his followers are called Taifuris. He was a saint of very great status. H. Junaid Baghdādi said about him: Amongst us, he has a position, that H. Jibra‘il has among the angels. Abul Hasan Kharraqānī was a contemporary of Sultan Mahmud of Ghazni (971 – 1030). His connection with H. Baayazīd were purely spiritual, just as those of the noble Prophet with H. Owaise Qarni, who had not physically seen each other. H. Owaise learnt everything from the Prophet by spiritual means ―Qazi Sajjad Hussaid] Have you heard about the narrative of H. Baayazīd that he had seen the affairs of H. Abul Hasan Kharraqānī even before he was born. One day that great devout of God was going along with his disciples in the forest. Suddenly he felt a fragrance from kharqān in the surroundings of Rey. He made a loveful sound of great pleasure upon the feeling of this fragrance in the air. He took long breaths to smell the pleasant air, as though his soul was drinking wine. Air became a pleasant liquid, as it happens when due to drop in temperature vapours of air becomes liquid. This is like the pieces of ice that accumulate on a vessel containing ice which do not come out from the vessel but are formed in its outside due to the fall in temperature. Air bringing fragrance became water for him; and water became like pure wine, and he felt as though intoxicated. Looking at the strange matter, one of the disciples came nearer to him and said: “You seem to be in the finest of the states, which is beyond the five senses of man (seeing, hearing etc), beyond all the six dimensions (back-front, up-down and right- left). Your face is appearing in different colours ― red, pale and white, moment by moment. What is it due to and what pleasant news have you heard? You seem to be smelling flowers, when there are no flowers in the surroundings. Certainly, it must be from an invisible source and from the garden of the essence of everything (God).

sections.heading: Heavenly Wine of Bliss
paras: “You are the object of everything in need! Every moment a new message comes to you. Every moment you feel the smell of H. Yūsuf, just as H. Yākoob felt. Your brain receives new pleasures every moment. Please put a drop from the contents of your vessel and speak out a little of that pleasant garden. O greatness in beauty! It is not the custom that our lips should be dry and your lips alone should drink. O smart-high-flying-accurate-measurer-of-the- heaven; please give us also a gulp of what you drank. There is no chief of the gathering in the world other than you, O king! Please cast a look at your friends. The wine that you drank cannot keep itself hidden. Wine certainly brings disgrace to man. One who drank wine may hide its smell, but what can he do with his eyes? And the wine you drank is not of this type. Its fragrance is that which cannot remain unfelt even from behind lakhs of curtains. It is a wine of the gnosis of God. The forest and deserts are filled with its impacts. Nay, it is not forests and deserts! It has passed even beyond the heavens. Do not try to shut the mouth of its container with a lid. This is not that can be dressed up from outside. O knower of the secrets and revealer of the secrets! Be graceful to us and tell us about the falcon that you have caught.”

sections.heading: Impacts of Intense Love
paras: H. Baayazīd said: “I felt a strange fragrance just as the Prophet left from the direction of Yemen. He said: “The wind brings to me the fragrance of God from Yemen: Inni la-ajidu nafsar Rahmani min qibalil yemen. I feel the breath of God from Yemen (Hadith). The fragrance of Rāmīn is coming from Wis. [Rāmīn was a well known lover of Wis in the Arab tradition, just as Laila and Majnūn. The impact of Rāmīn’s love on Wīs was such as against, the general trend, where the beloved tries to go away from the lover, Wīs fell in greater love for Rāmīn. That is to say: when a lover devotes himself to the beloved so much as to get lost in her, he merges in her, so that the beloved becomes the lover. The feeling of love gets exchanged ― Qazi Sajjad Hussain] The fragrance of Rāmīn was coming from Wīs. In similar manner, the fragrance of God was coming from Owaise Qarni. The strange fragrance of Owaise Qarni had pleased and intoxicated the Prophet. As H. Owaise had lost himself and annihilated, he lost his earthly connections and became heavenly. When bitter myrobalan is preserved in sugar syrup, it loses its bitterness. It loses its own independent existence, maintains its shape, but loses its taste. In like manner, one who has totally gone away from oneself, wraps up one’s self and ego and casts them away, and become totally devoid of them. There is no end to this discussion. Let us go to that great man as to what he said about the unseeable inspiration.

chapters.title: Fragrance from Yemen
chapters.subtitle: Answer of the kingly H. Baayazīd to explain the meaning of the prophet’s statement: I feel godly breaths from the Yemen’s side

paras: H. Baayazīd said: “The smell of a friend is coming to me from this direction, as to a village there, a great king (of gnosis of God) is about to come. A few years later this king is about to be born, who would pitch his tent upon the heavens. His face will be like the flowers from the God’s Garden and in his grade, he will be above me.” The disciple enquired about his name. He said: “His name is Abul Hasan.” Then he explained the features if his face from his forehead to the chin. He explained about his cheeks, colour and shape and about his hair and face, one after one. He also said about the soul and the types of its qualities, paths of entry and place of occupation. [Man is made up of three things: body, animal soul and human soul. The first two: Body and animal soul are destructible and so also their shapes. One should not give importance to them. The third one, the human soul is connected with the upper world and is not destructible. One’s connection should be developed with it ― Qazi Sajjad Hussain]

sections.heading: Forecast of H. Abul Hasan’s Birth
paras: “Body of that great king to be born is like a bright lamp upon the earth, the light of which searches upto the seventh heaven. This is like the tablet of the sun, which is in the sky but its light reaches every home. Flowers are kept under the nose in location, but their smell is above the palace and the roof of the brain. A man is asleep in his house but sees something frightening from the everlasting, non-material world out of fear. H. Yūsuf’s shirt was in the possession of a greedy fellow in Egypt, but its smell filled the air of Kan‘aan,” His disciples wrote down the date of this forecast and waited for its occurrence just as roasting of meat chops is waited anxiously. When that particular time arrived, that great king took his birth and got up.

chapters.title: Birth of H. Abul Hasan Kharraqāni
chapters.subtitle: Birth of shaikh Abul Hasan Kharraqāni (May his secrets remain pure) after the death of H. Baayazīd Bistami (May god grant comfort to his soul) at the specified time

paras: That foretold king took birth and came into this world from the world of non-material existence (‘adan), as a king and played his game of dice in the kingdom of the spiritual world and drove fast his horse. He was born many years after the death of H. Baayazīd. What all, he had said about him in the matter of telling that requirement to be told; and with holding what required to be withheld (as per the capacity of the receiver), came to be established in the same manner as already foretold.

sections.heading: Forecast Was Inspirational
paras: The Protected Tablet was his guide, as exactly as per which, he had spoken, as it is fully protected and totally devoid of any mistake [see the earlier pages about the explanation of Protected Tablet]. It is neither astrology not dream, nor ramal [an ancient science of forecasting of events by inserting fingers in sand. The knowledge about it is now extinct ― Translator]. This was an inspired information from God. Yet its exactness is known to God alone. This is a very special source of knowledge which the prophets and saints get, which cannot be told to all, as it is not understandable by the common masses. Sufis call it as the inspiration to heart. You may consider this simply as the inspiration to heart, as against what you come to know through your fine senses, and learn from others and from your own experience, with the aid of wisdom and intellect. Because, heart is another observer, apart from those mentioned above, which does not go wrong. This is an inspiration to that heart which is totally engrossed and lost in God. If you are a man of faith, you will become one who sees with the light of God, and remain protected from the commission of wrongs and forgetfulness.

chapters.title: See the Causes and Not Effects
chapters.subtitle: Return to the story of the slave who complained of the deficiency of food: and to explain that the sufi’s food of heart and soul is from God

paras: When a sufi becomes distressed with poverty his poverty itself becomes one to feed and provide the needs to him. Because paradise is built upon the foundation of difficulties and deprivation; and mercy, humility and grieved hearts are its parts. The fellow who crushes the heads of the people with his pride and haughtiness does not get the mercy of God and the people. There is no end to this talk. Let us consider that servant of the king who had become weak due to the deficiency of food.

sections.heading: Food and Provision of Sufi’s
paras: That sufi is fortunate whose food and provision are reduced. He will become from the level of a bead and proceed to that of a pearl and grow as large as the ocean. One who comes to know of this special reward, becomes entitled to the nearness of God making himself as a source of provisions, because of the elevation to higher levels of his soul. But when the provisions of the soul are reduced, his life starts shivering at this loss. He realizes that some sin has come about by him as the garden of the consonance with God and his own satisfaction has not bloomed. This is like the case of person whose farm land has gone under loss and instead of looking for the reason, he remains satisfied with just writing a letter about it to the land owners, as was the case of that servant of the king.

sections.heading: Think of the Reason of Deprivation
paras: The wise master received the letter of grievances, read it and did not give any reply. He said to himself: “This fellow is worried only about the reduction of his provision and not about the reasons for this. In such a case, remaining silent is better than answering to a fool. He is not bothered about his separation, or closeness with me. He is only worried about the awards from me. He is bothered about the branch and not of the root of the tree. He is foolish and dead due to his own self indulgence and selfishness. He is much bothered about the branch of the tree that he has no time to think of the roots.” Consider the heavens and the earth as an apple, which is created from a tree with the creative power if God. You are like a worm in that apple being unaware of the tree and the garden: There is another worm in the apple which is aware if what is happening outside. Its movement in the apple is so powerful that it tears off the apple; as the apple is not capable of bearing its force. Its movements tear off the curtains of the apple. Though it is just a small worm to look at but it is a powerful as a python.

sections.heading: Great Power of Fire
paras: The spark that comes out of the red-hot iron at first is very tiny and slow in movement. It meets with cotton like a baby meeting the wet nurse at first, but later creates such flames which reach upto the sky. Similarly, man, at first, is bound to food and sleep, but later becomes greater and higher than the angels. With the support of cotton and Sulphur, he creates such flames and light that reach upto the farthest star. He brightens the dark world and pulls down steel girders with a needle. Though fire is also a physical substance not a soul and has no connections, with soul, but its power is so great that generally physical bodies do not have a share in it (though some physical bodies contain it inside). Fire is a phenomenon and not matter existing in the form of energy in energy particles. Heat and light which can overlap, overtake and over power those very matters from which it originated. If we take the origin of the universe itself as with the Bigbang, it is clear that it was energy and not matter. The energy had billions of degrees of temperature. It exploded and just one second after big bang the temperature fell down to about the thousand million degrees when there were only photons, electrons and neutrons and their anti-particles and few protons. After hundred seconds, the temperature further came down to one thousand million degrees, contributing as atoms forming heavy hydrogen (deuterium) with one proton and one neutron in the atom. And from here with further loss of heat atoms of other elements were formed. (Theory of everything: Stephen Hawking: page: 74-75). Thus, the first thing in the universe was heat energy as per our present-day terminology but at the earlier times it was termed as ‘fire’ ― Translator

sections.heading: Human Body: a Drop in the Ocean
paras: Body of everything is just like a drop in the ocean. Body, left to itself, has no share in the matter of pride. Body grows in size everyday because of the soul, and when the soul gets out of it, you may see what happens to the body. Though your body grows in size, yet its overall size does not go beyond one or two yards, but your soul can roam about in the sky. Know this wiseman: that the long distance from Baghdad to Samarkand is just as short as half a step for the soul. Your eyes contain seven grams of fat in it, but the light of its soul reaches upto the farthest regions of the sky. Its light even with closed eyes sees so many things in the dream. But it is its light that is everything, otherwise without its light, it is worthless. Soul does not need the beard and moustaches of your body, but body without soul is dead and disgraceful. What all that is now said is about the grandeur and greatness of the animal soul, which is there in the animals also. Do not remain satisfied with this alone. Proceed further and consider the human soul, which is far greater than the animal soul. [Human soul and its connections with animal soul are explained in earlier pages]

sections.heading: Human Soul, More Powerful Than Jibra’iil
paras: But, donot remain contended with the words and explanations of the human soul also. Proceed further upto the shore of the soul of H. Jibra’iil. Upon your reaching this stage, the soul of H. Muhammed will feel surprised at you and H. Jibra’iil will be so frightened with you as to go away from you. He will say: “If I come one more step toward you, I shall be burnt.” This was told by him to H. Muhammed on the occasion of Ascension (Mi‘raaj) that he cannot go one step beyond the fourth heaven. This is a forest of spiritual world which has no head and feet to discuss about. The servant of the king is in sorrows for he has not received a reply from the king to his letter. Let us go to him.

chapters.title: Imputing Wrong upon Others
chapters.subtitle: The slave’s anxiety for not receiving reply from the king

paras: When the slave did not get a reply from the king, he was very much upset. Because of this, his clean water got polluted. It caused a kind of madness in him and he lost his peace of mind and sleep at night. Throughout the day and night, he kept his head down in anxiety thinking: “It is strange that the king has not given a reply to me. It is possible that the carrier of the latter, out of his contempt for me has not delivered the letter. He might have hidden the letter and not shown to the king. He might have been a hypocrite like water hidden under grass. Let me write another letter to the king and search for another efficient carrier of the letter.” In this manner that ignorant fellow attributed defects upon the king, the chief of the royal kitchen and the latter carrier. He did not take stock of his own follies and went astray just as an idol worshipper does in the path of religion.

chapters.title: Improper Thinking of H. Sulaimān
chapters.subtitle: Devotion of the wind from the throne of H. Sulaimān because of his improper thinking

paras: Wind took a devotion from the throne of H. Sulaimān. He told the wind not to deviate and go wrong. The wind said: “You may also not deviate! And, if you deviate from the way, do not be angry with me. God has created this reciprocation of one with another as a balance, so that there may be proper equity between us. If you creat imbalance in your weighing machine, I shall also do the same to you. So long as you shed light on me, I shall also do so.” [As God has said: “The recompose for an injury is an injury there to”: “Jazaa’uu sayyi’atin

sections.heading: Sayyi’atun Mithlaiha”: (Shura: 42: 40) Impacts of Bad and Good Thoughts
paras: In this manner, H. Sulaimān’s crown also took a tilt, and converted his bright day into a dark night. He said: “O my crown, do not remain tilted on my head. O sun, do not get lost from my east.” He used to replace his crown in a proper manner on his head with his hand, but again it used to tilt to the other side. He set it right in this manner for eight times and every time it tilted. Then he said: “What has happened to you my crown? Do not go wrong in your actions.” Then the crown said: “Even if you set me right for a hundred times, I shall tilt so long as you are on the wrong ways. Then, H. Sulaimān set right his wrong thoughts that had occupied his mind. The desire that he had in his heart lost its. Weight and slackened. Then his crown straightened itself and settled on his head in the same manner as he desired. After this, H. Sulaimān deliberately used to keep the crown in a tilted way, but it used to set itself right upon his head. He did like this for eight times and every time, the crown used to go right. Then he enquired with the crown: “What has happened to you now? I deliberately keep you tilted but you became right.” The crown said: “O king! Now you may be proud of yourself as you have cleansed your feathers of dust. You may fly high now.”

sections.heading: Your Troubles Are Your Makings
paras: I am not permitted to proceed further to explain this in greater detail by tearing of the curtains of the hidden world. Keep your hand on my mouth, shut it up, so that unpalatable words do not come about from it. This, it is required that whether troubles came to you, should not be attributed to others. On the contrary enquiries should be made about your own follies. Do not have suspicions upon your friends for your troubles just as that slave did that, he suspected the carrier of letter, the chief of the royal kitchen and the generous king, one after the other,” This, he did like Pharoah, who did not think about H. Mūsā who was very much being taken care of in his place, while he was engaged in beheading children of others outside. His enemy was very much in his house itself, but he went on killing others beyond you, without at all caring for the hatable self of yours and consonance with it. Your self is your enemy which is within yourself and pleasing it with sweet meats; and blaming all others who are away from you. Like Pharaoh, your eyes go blind as well as your heart. You are pleased with your enemy but engaged in blaming others. Like Pharaoh, how long do you want to kill the innocent while feeding your already filled up belly with grains. The Qurān says: “Whatever misfortune happens to you, is because of the things of your hands”: “Wa maa asaabakum min musiibatin fabimaa kasabat aidiyakum”: (Shura: 42: 30). Pharoah was much wiser than other kings, but Allah’s seal struck upon his eyes, ears and wisdom. This seal makes even a wiseman like Plato, a fool. God’s command appears on the tablet of the heart just as the command of the unseen world appeared on the heart of H. Baayazīd.

chapters.title: Shaikh Abul Hasan Kharraqāni’s Hearing of the Forecast Made by H
chapters.subtitle: Baayazīd about him, well before his birth

paras: Whatever H. Baayazīd had forecast came about, and H. Abul Hasan came to know of it that: “He would be my disciple and follower. He would take lessons from me every morning, from my grave, and become a God knowing shaikh at my grave. H. Abul Hasan also said: “I also saw in a dream and heard from his soul all that you had heard from him.”

sections.heading: Teaching in Absentia
paras: Every morning he used to go fast to his grave, and sit by it with full conviction; and also stand there till the forenoon, facing toward it, until the shaikh would appear before him like a real person. And sometimes, without such appearances clear his doubts and difficulties of understanding. One day when he came with the usual devotion, he found all the graves having been covered with freshly fallen snow. He saw layers upon layers of ice like mounds and he felt very much grieved. He heard the living voice of the shaikh from the boundary wall of the grave yard: “See! I am calling you. Come fast before me. Come fast upon my calling. The entire world is like ice, but do not turn your face away from me.” From that day onwards H. Abul Hasan was completely changed and he saw and heard such things which he had not till then. Now, it is time to return to the slave and complete his affairs.

chapters.title: Slave’s Another Letter
chapters.subtitle: The slave’s writing of another letter to the kings as he had not received the reply

paras: That suspicious fellow wrote another letter to the king, full of disgust, grumbling and haughtiness saying: “I had earlier written a letter to the king and it is strange that inspite of receipt, it was not replied to. I had sent another letter to see your beautiful face and no reply was given even to that.” The king did not show any interest in his letters. He wrote altogether five letters but the king did not care to reply. His private secretary told the king: “Anyway, your lordship! He is your slave. It would be better if you send a reply to him. This will not bring any deficiency to your kingly status. Please have a little grace for your slave and servant.”

sections.heading: Teaching Fools’ Recoils upon Teachers
paras: The king said: “It is very easy to write to him. But he is a fool. A foolish fellow is vicious and rejected by God. If I forgive him for his wrongs and derelictions. I shall also get infested with his sickness. Hundred fellows get infested with a fellow suffering from rabies. And in particular from a foolish patient of rabies. May god not give the rabies of foolishness even to an infidel. He is such an unfortunate fellow that he would make the clouds waterless. Because of his misfortune, clouds fail to fell water. His owlish nature destroys well established cities. It is because of the fools suffering from rabies that the floods were caused during the time of H. Noah, which destroyed and disgraced the world.

chapters.title: Wise Are Praise Worthy
chapters.subtitle: Praise of the wise and condemnation of fools by the Noble Prophet (A.S)

paras: The noble Prophet said: “Every fool is out enemy and a misguide on the way of like a ghost. Every wise man is our life. His soul and the wind from him are a fine fragrance for us. I shall be pleased even if wisdom abuses me, as it has received my blessings. Its abuses will not be useless. Its hosting will not be devoid of delicious dishes.” On the contrary, even if a fool keeps sweet up on my lips, I get feverish because of it. Be sure, that lack of cleanliness of heat and brightness of wisdom is not a reason to seek pleasure of any kind in kissing the back of an ass. It will only pollute your moustaches, and the dinning sheet of such fellows will keep a cauldron on it which would blacken your clothes. By dining sheet is meant wisdom and not bread and meaty dishes. The wine of the soul is nothing but the light of wisdom.

sections.heading: Light of Wisdom Is Man’s Food
paras: Man’s food is nothing but light, and life does not develop other than with it. Keep yourself slowly away from eatable dishes as edible food is of worth only for the donkeys. These are not the possessions of the noble people. In order to become one for the real food, you should go after the morsels of light. It is because of the reflection of this light that bread has come about. It is because of its grants that the soul of man has become a real soul. If you eat the food of light once, you will throw dust on the bread prepared in the clay oven pot (tandoor). If you eat this food of light of wisdom, you will tell the bread of the body to go away: “I do not need your fatty, tasty, food anymore. I have found only the true path. I do not need you strength for my feet.

sections.heading: Acquired Wisdom
paras: There are two types of wisdom. One is acquired which is learnt from others just as children learn in the school. You acquire it from the book, teacher, thinking and remembering the meanings and good and refreshing informations. As you proceed, this increases and you go ahead of others. But you get tired and overburdened with their weight and their remembering from being lost. You will be like carrier of a paper sheet containing all this and roaming about here and there. This is not like the Protected Tablet (Loah-e-Mahfooz) which contain real, original wisdom and information. There is difference between acquired and remembered wisdom and original inherent wisdom.

sections.heading: Inherent Wisdom: Godly Gift
paras: The other wisdom is a grant from God. Its source springs from the soul. When the water of this springs of wisdom sprouts from the heart, it is pure, totally unpolluted, not taken from old sources and uninfluenced by others. There is no scope to stop its sprouting forth with force as it originates and survives in the heart itself and is always in force. Acquired wisdom is like a stream which starts from the water pools, moves in the streams and reaches the heart. If the water-pool which is its source dries up, it becomes destitute. As against this, the wisdom that sprouts from the stream of the heart never dried up. Therefore, search for the springs within yourself, so that you may be rid of the influence and obligation of the incompetent teachers.

chapters.title: Consultation with Others
chapters.subtitle: Story of a person who consulted with another and other ones telling him to consult another, himself being his enemy

paras: A person consulting another so as to go out of doubts and seek clarity of the affair to attend to. That man said: “O the one with a good name, search for someone else for advice as I am inimical to you. Do not entangle yourself with me. No one has enemy. Go and search of someone who is friendly with you. Without any doubt, a friend will be a well-wisher. I am your enemy and certainly out of my own concern for myself. I shall go on the wrong path and show enmity to you. It is not proper to seek the protection of the wolf. Searching for someone at a place where he is not available is no searching. I am your enemy without any doubt. I can never guide you properly. I am like a dacoit for you. One in the company of friends finds himself as in a garden, even if he is in a furnace. One who sits with an enemy will find himself to be in a furnace even while sitting in a garden.

sections.heading: Consult a Friend
paras: Do not harm a friend by differentiating between yourself and him, so that your friend may not become your enemy. Do good to others for the sake of God and for your own peace of mind. So that, you may consider everyone as your friend and may not have ill-feeling for others as it makes you unhappy. And if you have enmity for anyone, be careful not to consult him but consult a loving friend.”

sections.heading: Wisdom Controls in and Out
paras: The first, seeker of advice said: “O grateful one, I know you and also that you are an old enemy of mine. But you are a wiseman and of high knowledge. Your wisdom will not allow you to go on the wrong way. Your personal desire will tell you to take revenge of the enemy, but your wisdom will act like an iron chain for your desire. Wisdom will come forward, advises it and prevents it from desiring as such. Wisdom is like a police officer to distinguish between good and bad. Wisdom coming out of faith is like a just police officer and it is a guard of the city of heart and its controller. It remains smart like a cat, and because of it, the thief remains hidden in the hole like a rat. There is no scope for its to come to play mischief. And if it comes out, it means there is no cat for it to frighten. I am sorry! I am wrong in considering wisdom as a cat. No! it is a lion, and that too a lion which can chase another lion away. This is the case of the wisdom coming out of faith. Its roar is a commander for other carnivorous beasts. Its roar is also a preventer of herbivorous animals too. These beasts are like the might of wrathful tendencies of man, which are kept under control by wisdom.

sections.heading: Man’s Body Is Like a City
paras: The city of the body is full of thieves and tricksters who can pull out the clothes from the bodies of others. The mere presence of the police officer of wisdom keeps them under control, whether he is on the spot or not. Wisdom is also the controller of the faith in the body, out of the fear of which the thieves of the vicious self-feel themselves to be prison. O my soul! You alone are the wisdom of my wisdom and the soul of my soul! You alone are the wisdom of all creatures and the kings of life. Perfect and absolute wisdom is interested and anxious about your becoming perfect and absolute, upon which all creatures will be under your control, just as H. Jibra’iil was estranged upon the perfect wisdom of the noble Prophet.

chapters.title: Young Man Made to Lead Veterans
chapters.subtitle: The Prophet’s appointment of a young man of the tribe of Bani Huzīl as commander of the army consisting of elderly, battle trained and experienced veterans

sections.heading: No Security Without Leader
paras: The noble Prophet was dispatching a small army to fight against the infidels and elimination of absurdities. He selected a young man from the tribe of Bani Huzīl and made him a leader and commander of the army. It should be known that the leader of the army is certainly its base. A group without a leader is like a body without head. See yourself as virtually dead and devoid of hope, if you have given up a leader. It is with laziness, miserliness, egotism and self-proclamation that you turn your head aside and become rebellious and make yourself as a leader. This is like a donkey which, to avoid the burden of carrying a load, runs away towards the hill track, his master running behind it saying: “O rebellious fellow! All around there are wolves in search of donkeys. If you go out of my sight now, from all sides, some wolf of the other will come before you. It will chew your bones like sugar and you will never see life again. Do not run away. You will even lose your grass to eat and you will be like fire which goes cold when fuel is not required. Be warned! Do not run away from the job of carrying burden that I am giving you. Know this, your life is secure with me as I am its protector.”

sections.heading: Donkeys Addressed as Horses
paras: In similar manner, my dear reader, you are also like the donkey as your arrogant self is dominant upon you, and your dominant donkish nature decides your status upon which you will be called as a donkey. But Graceful God has called you as a horse instead as a donkey. He has used the word “ta‘aal” which means “Arabian horse”, for the donkey like you and used the derivatives of “ta‘aal” while referring to you. The noble Prophet is the stableman of the stable where you are lodged, to train and moderate your cruel self. God has used the derivative of “ta‘aal” to call you to mean “come over”, so that He may modify you as He is a modifier. In this manner. He has directed the Prophet to call you towards him through the phrase “Ta‘aala”. This He has done in order to elevate and grace you from the level of the donkey to that of the horse.

sections.heading: Sufferings of Trainers
paras: The stateman and trainer of horses gets kicks from the horses while training and modifying them. So also, the prophets get many troubles from people. Getting troubled by the people is an inevitable consequence for the prophets. Prophets undergo many trials and tribulations from the people, because training up the untrained, crude fellows is a very tough job.

sections.heading: Different Means to Train the Different
paras: You are very slow-going-horses like the Trukic ponies. Take lessons from me so that you may become a fast runner so as to be fit for the king. God has said: ‘Ta‘aalau’ (come over) many times to you as you are weak horses unfit for racing. He has told you ‘Ta‘aalau’ to call you back as you have run away from training. So also, He again said ‘Ta‘aalau’, considering you to be lazy with weak nerves and muscles. Through these callings He wants to rid you of your defects. At the same time, He said to the Prophet: ‘Do not grieve, O Prophet if they do not come. Do not get disgusted at the lack of response of these two-four worthless fellows. Some people are deaf to these calls of Ta‘aalau. Every kind of horse has to be kept in a different stable. Some people ran away upon this call. Donkeys and horses have different places to be kept. Some people got disheartened upon your calls and narratives they are of different tastes, and live away from you and others, just as every bird has a different nest. So also, the angels are not alike. That is why they are in different ranks upon ranks in the heavens. All children learn the same lessons in a class, but they are at different levels from each other. People from the Eastern and Western countries have different senses and emotions. Sense of seeing in the property of the eyes. Only they can see. Even if lakhs of ears stand in rank upon rank, to see, they cannot see, but a single eye sees, because they donot possess that light that makes the eyes see. So also, the state of the ranks of ears is different. Eyes have no share in their hearing capacity.

sections.heading: Five Outer and Five Inner Senses
paras: The soul of the Qurān and the narratives mentioned in it cannot be accessed by all the lakhs of eyes just as an eye is incapable of hearing, consider all the five senses in similar manner. The job of each sense organ is different. It can do those which other organs cannot do. Five external senses (hearing, seeing, smelling, tasting and touching) and the five internal senses (imagination (khayal), ratiocination (tafakkur), memory (hafiza), perception (tawahhum) and reasoning (‘aql) are engaged in the respective allotted functions like the angels in ranks. One who rebels against the principles and ranks of faith joins the ranks of the vicious. Therefore, O Prophet donot deviate from giving the call of ‘Ta‘aalau’. This is word full of wonderful effects like those of alchemy to bring about a great change for the good. Even if a lowly fellow like great change for good. Even if a lowly fellow like copper refuses to hear this call, this alchemy, you should not draw back from him. At the present moment his magical self may be deaf, but later on, he will have its impacts and get benefitted.

sections.heading: Seek a Lender, Not Leadership
paras: This is the lesson for you, O youngman! Go on repeating ‘come over’ again and again as it is a call of God; and God calls towards the house of security and peace whomsoever He wishes, stated in the Qurān: “God doth call to the Home of peace and guides whom He pleases to a

sections.heading: Way That Is Straight”: “Wallaahu Yad‘uu Ilaa Darissalaami Wa Yahdii Man Yashaa’u Ilaa Siratin mustaqiimin”:(Yunus: 10: 15)
paras: Therefore, O master of your own arrogance and superiority complex! Do not be so anymore! Search for a leader and guide and do not be a claimant of leadership.

chapters.title: Greatness of the Elderly
chapters.subtitle: Objection raised by one before the noble Prophet upon the appointment of a Huzīlī as commander of the contingent

paras: When the Prophet appointed a Huzīlī as the commander of the victorious army, one dull- witted person, out of jealousy could not bear with this, and raised an objection and declared: “We donot agree with this appointment.”

sections.heading: Pride Causes Disunity
paras: Look at the people in how much darkness they are! How they are getting destroyed for this destructible world. Because of pride they are all disunited. They are dead from the spiritual point of view but are alive for the fire-causing-world. It is strange that their life is held up in a prison, even though its key is in their hand. That objecting young man was sunk head to foot in dung, even though a flowing stream was hitting upon him, with which he could clean himself. At every point he was in lasing mental disturbance, even though he was closeby to a place of rest and comfort.

sections.heading: Benefit of Distress
