paras: God’s light is hidden but its existence is proved by the searching for it by the searchers. Heart does not search without a purpose. It has an object to search for God’s light and that is why, it is in search of it. Had there been no scope of escape from the troubles of the world, there would have been total distress and the heart would not have put efforts to get rid of them. Distress drags you as a policeman drags, and tells you to search for the correct path, and to give up the wrong path on which you are proceeding. The right path is there, but it is hidden from you. Distress of the world compels you to find out the route of escape not only from the troubles of the world, but also from the world itself to seek relief of the next world.

sections.heading: Disunity Compels to Unite
paras: Disunity of the people actually puts them in anxiety and compels them to search for unity. You can see the face of unity in disunity itself. This is not only between man and man but also between man and God, because God is not away from you but is with you wherever you may be. As He says: “And He is with you wheresoever you may be”: “Wa huwa ma‘akum aina maa kuntim”: (Hadid: 57: 4). Dead seeds when put in the soil and watered come into life with their roots in order to make you know of the giver of life; As He says: “Then contemplate (O man!) upon the memorials of God’s mercy! How He gives life to the earth

sections.heading: After Its Death”: “Fanzur Ilaa Aathaari Rahmatallaahi Kaifa Yuhyil Arda Ba’ada
paras: mawtihaa”: (Rum: 30: 50). Why are these prisoners constantly looking at the door of the prison? Because they know that someone would bring the good news of their release from the troublesome situation in this life itself and from this world itself. This release is also by way of guidance in the matter of escape.

sections.heading: Deprivation Leads to Searching
paras: Lakhs of people go in search of water, only because, somewhere it is available and they can find it. So also, those who go in search of the water of mercy from God. They hope for it and search for it. You donot get comfort while you are lain on the ground; and think of going to the house, where bed and blanket are available. Had there been no bed and blanket at home, you would not have felt the uneasiness of being lain on the ground. People search for comfort because of their discomfort. Intoxication of the wine is of no pleasure if there is no scope of something that would put an end to it. That is: no one likes unending intoxication. Time is also a factor to end the intoxication. Remaining intoxicated without break gives no pleasure of intoxication. Similarly, where there is no intoxication in wine at all, no one would go after it.

sections.heading: Virtues of Old Age
paras: The objector to the appointment of a young commander said to the Prophet: “O Prophet! Do not appoint one as commander other than an elderly man. O Prophet! a young man may be the child of a lion in bravery, but none other than an elderly person should not be a commander. You have already told us that a leader should be an elderly man. You have said: ‘An elderly person among his people is like a prophet among his followers: Alshaikhu fii ahlihii kal anbiyyu fii ummati (Hadith). O Prophet! Look at this army! There are many elderly persons who are better than the appointee. Please donot look at this tree with its yellow leaves. Please pick up the ripe apples from it. Even its yellow leaves are not useless. They speak of maturity and perfection. Yellow leaves of the tree like the white hair of beard announce about the maturity of wisdom. Freshly grown green leaves of the tree declare that the fruit is still raw. Non-possession of the virtues of youthfulness is a proof of their possession of other greater virtues. Yellowness of gold is a sign of success of a goldsmith.

sections.heading: Wisdom, Experience Above Physical Strength
paras: One with a plumply cheeks like flowers and the emerging fresh beard thereon gives the information that he is still a learner in the school. The writings of his hand are crooked and ill shaped. He is handicapped of wisdom, though his body runs fast. Legs of the old man are incapable of moving fast, but he has two wings of wisdom that fly high above in the sky. If you want to have an example of the fact that wings of feathers develop in place of the Tayyaar. He lost his hands and legs, but God provided him with wings. If you are capable of understanding the eloquence of language, I can speak of the Ja‘afai gold, which was considered to be the purest and most shining and called as such because it was introduced into the market by Ja‘afar Barmakkī during his prime ministership at Baghdad. Let me stop at this about the greatness of gold, as my heart is disturbed and wavery like mercury. Hundreds of silences are keeping their fingers on my lips to make me remain quite and to stop further talk.

sections.heading: Wisdom of Silence
paras: Silence is like ocean and talking is like a stream. An ocean of silence is searching for you and you may stop searching for the stream of talks. Donot turn your face away from the silent directions of the ocean. Put an end to your talk and know that God alone knows best. In this manner that indisciplined fellow went on talking to the Prophet with cold lips. Word will be of use to one who is without any information. But for a person who has seen the realities with his own eyes, any amount of information is of no use. These informations come about only after the observation of events. These are not for those who leave actually seen them, but for those who were away from the scene and seeing. It is a useless exercise to give information to the one who has already seen. There is no need for middle-women to pass on the lover’s letter to the beloved, when the lover is already sitting with the beloved. So also, for a boy who has grown older or a middle-women to pass on the letter, as his robust youth itself is a firm informer of his affairs.

sections.heading: Knowers Need Not Be Told
paras: Reading of the letter is needed to learn about the unknown matters. Words are spoken to clarify the matters. It is wrong to speak before those who have already seen matters; and if we do that, it speaks of our ignorance and deficiency of knowledge about those well aware persons. So also, is the case of persons who see things through their inner eyes and intuition and about the affairs of God. It is better for you to remain silent before them. It is for this reason that the command of ‘keep quite’ (Ansitu) or hold your peace has come in the Qurān which says: “When the Qurān is recited, then listen to it with attention, and hold your

sections.heading: Peace: That You May Receive Mercy”: “Wa Izaa Qurii’al Quraanu Fastami’uu Lahu Wa Ansitu La‘allakum turhamuuna”:(A‘raaf: 7: 204). Where Speaking Is Necessary
paras: And if the order comes to speak, speak well and a little and do not speak too much. And if the order comes to elucidate it well, then also speak well convincingly. This is like what I do in respect of these beautiful statements. Now, I am with Zia ul Haq Husāmuddīn. When I speak a little in good articulation, he compels me to say in hundreds of ways. O Husāmuddīn! You are the light of God. You have already seen the beloved (God). Why do you still insist upon speaking about Him? Perhaps, this is the answer to my question. This is due to the love of the beloved. Love demands that all senses are engaged with it. What the eyes have already seen is sought to be heard by the ears. A drinker of wine tells the cup bearer; give me the wine to please me and also speak of it so that the ears also may be pleased. Now, at this moment the cup has touched your mouth and the ear says: “Where is my share of it.” It is said to the ear: “Your share is the warmth of love, which enters into you with the seeing of the beloved by the eyes.” The ear says: “My greed is not satisfied with this warmth alone; and that comes by the narration of the affairs of love. That is why, be talking about the beloved.

chapters.title: Objector Replied
chapters.subtitle: The Prophet’s reply to the objector

sections.heading: Prophet’s Extraordinary Level
paras: When that Arab went beyond limits in his talk before the sweet tempered, Mustafa, the king of ‘walannjm’ and ‘‘Abasa’, he kept his finger on the lips to prevent him from further speech and said in a cool way: “Enough! How much do you talk before the one who is aware of the mysteries of life.” [Walannjm is surah 53 of the Qurān which declares about H. Muhammed’s specialty among all humans before and after him: that he is neither astray nor misled; he does not talk as per his desire, but only at inspiration of the Mighty in Power (God), endued with wisdom from the One from the highest part of the horizon who came closer to him as though both were within a circle form by two semi-circular bones, his heart being in no way falsified. The other is a surah in ‘Abasa (He frowned) surah no. 80, in which such a special person, Muhammed was reproved by God for having frowned and turned away from a blind man, Abdullah b. Umme Makhtum, who interrupted him while he was engaged in trying to explain the holy Qurān to Pagan Quraish leaders. These two surahs refer to the highest level of teaching to the noble Prophet by way of contradictory ways ― one by speaking of his highest elevation, and praise and the other by its extreme opposite; reprimand ― Translator]

sections.heading: Silence: Not Lack of Knowledge
paras: The Prophet continued: “You are taking dried dung before the master of intuition and inner inspiration to buy it in place of musk gland. You keep the dry dung under your nose and take long breaths to pose it as a fine fragrant. You, as a foolish squint-eyed fellow, yell out long breaths so that your worthless commodity may be sold out. You have a dry brain and yell out this sound, to project a worthless dry dung as a grant musk. How long can you cheat a man who is an expert perfume who roams about in the gardens of heavens. Though his composed and tolerant nature has made him pose himself as innocent and layman, yet you should also look a little at your own self.

sections.heading: Maintain Dignity of Great Men
paras: If the mouth of the cauldron is kept open on the night, the cat also should have some concern and maintain its dignity and not lick its contents. Great men project themselves as ignorant and sleeping to overlook some undencies, but as you are fully awake, you should not try to degrade them. How long do you want to blabber in a quarrelsome manner and recite these devilish spells before the Prophet. They have lakhs of composures, each of which is like that of a hundred mountains. Their composures make a fool of a smart fellow and a blind of one with the brightness of a hundred eyes. It is like an excellent wine of such quality that its impacts go beyond one’s brain. One intoxicated with this strange wine starts walking in a crisscross manner like the queen in chess. Its fast-intoxicating capacity makes a young man fall down on the way like an old man. Particularly, the intoxication of which lasts not for one night but for the whole life. Which is the wine of the love of God.

sections.heading: Impacts of Prophetic Wine
paras: The companions of the cave (Ashaab-e-kahaf) were so much intoxicated with this wine that they could not think of their food and journey. They lost their sense for three hundred and nine years. The women of Egypt had sipped a cup of this wine while looking at the beautiful face of H. Yūsuf. They lost all senses and cut their own hands with their own knives. The magicians of Egypt got intoxicated and considered the scaffold as a more lovely thing than life. When H. Ja‘far Tayyār got so much intoxicated with this wine that he sacrificed his hand and legs.

chapters.title: Meaning of Subhanii Maa A‘zam Shaanii
chapters.subtitle: Explaination of the meaning of the statement of H. Baayazīd Bistāmī: How holy I am. How great is my state: Subhaani maa a‘zam shaani. Raising of objections on this by his disciples. His clarification: not by words but by demonstration

paras: That honourable dervish, H. Baayazīd Bistāmī told his desciples: “I am your God.” This he said in such an open way in a state of intoxication (of love of God) that there is no God but me and you may worship me. When this state was over in the morning, his disciples told him that he said such and such, and that it was not proper. He told them; if I say any such thing again, you may stab me with knives. God does not have a physical body and I am a body. When I say so, I am worthy of being killed.” As per the clear advice of that free man, everyone of his disciples kept a dagger with him. On another occasion he was once again in a state of deep immersion, and those instructions went out of his mind. When love dominated his senses, his wisdom was lost. This was like the loss of importance of the lamp when morning arrived.

sections.heading: Wisdom Dominated by Others
paras: Wisdom is like a police officer appointed by the king to control but when the king himself came to take charge, the police officer kept himself away. Wisdom is like the shadow of God; and God is like sun. what is the worth of the shadow before the sun to face it. When the fairy (or jinn) dominates over man, man ceases to be man. Whatever he says is not what he says, but it is the saying of that fairy, be it this way or that. When such is the power and domination of the fairy, what will be the power of the fairy’s God. Man loses his state and himself and becomes a fairy. A Turk who does not know Arabic starts talking in Arabic under such domination. When he comes back to his senses, he does not say anything in Arabic. This shows that it was the fairy that had become his essence and quality.

sections.heading: Domination by God
paras: Thus, God of that fairy and of man cannot be lesser than the fairy. Consider that a semi- intoxicated fellow does not fear a lion. This fearlessness is not his quality but is an impact of the wine. No one seeks to know the direction of a way from a blind man. A semi-intoxicated fellow may try to drink the blood of lion and you will say: ‘this is not done by him but by the wine.’ While talking, he may speak of an old hidden secret. You will say that this is said by the wine. When these good and bad are the impacts of wine, then, does not the light of God have such power and capacity that it would not empty you completely of yourself, dominate and overpower you and make you speak of very high-level things?

sections.heading: Strange Words, Strange Impacts
paras: The Qurān is from the lips of the Prophet, but everyone says it is not he, but God said. And one who denies this, is an infidel. In a similar way, what Baayazīd said was not what he said but what God said. When this bird, Huma of supernatural qualities started flying by losing its senses such a statement came from the mouth of H. Baayazīd Bistāmi. His wisdom was swept away by the flood of strangeness. At another time he said something stranger than what he had said earlier. He said: “There is none other than God within my garment. How long do you want to search for Him in heavens and earth?” Hearing this, all his disciples were maddened and started stabbing his clean body with their daggers. Everyone was attacking him like the infidels of Gardkoh upon his body (a mountain in the region of Rey whose inhabitants were massacring Muslims). Everyone pierced his dagger into him, but it used to cause injury upon his own body and there was not a single would upon H. Baayazīd’s body. The disciple himself injured and sunk in blood. One who attempted to cut off his throat, got his own throat cut and died. One who stabbed him in the chest got his own chest pierced and he too died. One who was informed of H. Baayazīd’s grand state was not permitted by his heart to stab him. A little wisdom of his, tied up his hands, saved his life but got a little injured. All this happened during the night.

sections.heading: State of Annihilation
paras: When morning arrived, his half-dead disciples were crying in pain. Thousands of men and women came to him saying: “O shaikh, you have both the worlds in your garment. If this body of yours were to be of a man, it would have been lost with the attacks of the daggers.” When a person interested only in himself attacks one who is lost to himself, it is he only who suffers. It is like pricking a thorn into his own eyes. You have used a sword as good as Zulfiqār (the Prophet’s sword, which was later taken over by H. Alī). Upon those who are lost to themselves, you have actually used it upon yourself. Because anyone who is lost to himself and reached the state of annihilation in God is dead for himself but alive for God. He is as protected as God Himself is. He is in peace forever.

sections.heading: Saints Are Like Mirrors
paras: His physical appearance has died and he became a mirror for others to see themselves in him. The mirror does not see itself and all others see themselves in it. It can see only others. If you spit on the mirror, you spit upon yourself. If you attack the mirror, you attack yourself. The mirror shows you what you are. If you have an ugly face, you see an ugly face. You see yourself only. And if you see H. Īsā bin Maryam in the mirror, you may conclude that you are H. Īsā bin Maryam. The mirror is neither this nor that. It is just clean and clear of everything and it is simply as it is. It has kept your own face before you.

sections.heading: A Very Dangerous Level
paras: When the discussion has come to this level, my lips have shut the door. When the pen reached at this stage, it broke off. Therefore, stop the movement of your lips, how much ever eloquence you may have in speech. Do not breath further and be sure that God alone knows of all the guidance. However, I shall tell you further this much that one who is intoxicated with wine of God, sits on the edge of the terrace in a very risky place. Either sit at a lower level; and if you are at higher level, better come down for safety. Every moment of success attained at this level, should be considered as a risky place like the edge of the terrace. Be very frightened and careful whenever you reach this level and keep it hidden. Do not ever reveal it, so that my calamity may not fall upon your elevated friendship with God. Be very careful to walk on this dangerous path.

sections.heading: Disaster upon Reaching Highest Level
paras: Nearness with God is very pleasurable but there is always a fear of it getting lost. Therefore, you should keep yourself away from the edge of the terrace of this hidden world. A little carelessness makes you fall and cause great disaster. You may not see the edge of the terrace, but your soul sees that, because, it is the soul that enjoys that pleasure of nearness to God. All calamities that have fallen upon others, have fallen upon their reaching the edge of the terrace of pleasures. A fall is always from a high pedestal and edge of the terrace. Therefore, learn lessons from the calamities faced by the people of Noah and Lot. The calamities came upon them upon their reaching the highest level of pleasure. Therefore, take lesson from the hidden cleanliness to protect yourself; and this can be learnt from the inner cleanliness of the hearts of the prophets and saints.

chapters.title: Pleasures and Deficiencies of Intoxication
chapters.subtitle: Reasons for the blabbering and talking too much of that dull-witted fellow before the Prophet

paras: When the reflection of the excessive impacts of the knowledge of the Prophet fell upon that dull-witted fellow, he became very euphoric and pleasureful. Inevitably he was very joyous, pleased and talkative. His euphoria made him give up his discipline and enter into madness.

sections.heading: Intoxication of the Good and Uncultured
paras: Intoxication does not create mischief everywhere and in everyone. It makes the uncultured more uncultured. It makes a wise and cultured man wiser and grand; and if he is of bad temperament and misconduct, he becomes all the more so. A cup of wine for a sensible person is like a tonic and makes him more sensible; and a senseless fellow becomes more senseless. One who has annihilated himself in God becomes one of perfect discipline with the wine of the love of God. And all egotist becomes more indecent. But as most of the people are bad and ignoble. Wine is declared as unlawful for all. Laws are made for the majority of the people to follow and to control them. The law maker has taken away the sword from the hand of the dacoit.

chapters.title: Selection of Young Man as Commander
chapters.subtitle: Explanation of the reasons by the Prophet for the appointment of the Huzili as the leader and commander of the army and preferring him to other veterans

sections.heading: Scale of Wisdom
paras: The Prophet: “O the observer of the appearances! Donot consider that young man to be immature and incompetent. There are many with black beards but old in nature; and there are many white bearded who have black hearts. I have tested his wisdom on many occasions. That young man has shown qualities of old age though he is young. You should know that an old man is wise in the scale of wisdom and not in the basis of whiteness of his head and beard. How can anyone be older than Iblis. He is the oldest. But because he has no wisdom, he is worthless. When a child attains perfectness in his wisdom and acts well, he may be considered as a well-natured, mature old man.

sections.heading: Researchers and Blind Followers
paras: Consider him also as old, who has the qualities of H. Īsā, who talked so wisely, and was totally cleansed of pride, arrogance and greed. Whiteness of the hair is also a sign of maturity, but that is for the mild thinking, slow moving fellows with closed eyes. The common man, who can only follow in generality (muqallid) has to rely upon this scale of age for wisdom as he has no capacity to search for evidence and interpret. He can find his way on the basis of some well-established signs and symbols. This is the advice for such simple fellows. That is why we have given this instruction to such fellows to chose an elderly man for guidance and leadership. We mean one who is old in the matter of wisdom and not on age; and not the one who cannot find the difference between an examiner and the examinee. One who jumps away from the curtain of blind followership (taqlid), sees everything with the aid of the light of God. His clear light without any argument and evidences tears up his skin and penetrates deep inside. But, for the one who only looks at the appearances there is no yardstick to find out the truth and untruth. He cannot know as to what is there in the basket. Sometimes gold looks black due to the impact of smoke for protection from the thieves and the jealous. There are many pieces of copper with gold plating for being sold out to those with lesser wisdom. We being among those who see the inner qualities of everything in the world, look at the heart inside and not the apparent outside.

sections.heading: Appearance for Common Men
paras: A judge considers only the apparent and passes judgement on the basis of what apparent facts are provided to him. Once a fellow recites the first article of faith (No God but Allah) with his mouth, he passes a judgement that he is a Muslim, even though there is nothing of that sort in his heart. It is through this apparent show that many hypocrites have taken protection but they secretly shed the blood of hundreds of faithful Muslims. Therefore, put efforts to become an oldman of wisdom and faith, so that you may be able to see the inner things just as perfect wisdom does.

sections.heading: Wisdom Wears Many Apparels
paras: When wisdom exhibited its beautiful face from the world of non-existence (‘adam), nature granted it many apparels and gave hundreds of designations. The cheapest (lowest) designation it gave to it was that it is independent and does not need anybody’s support. If wisdom becomes a physical face in the world, a day will become dark before it. And if foolishness assumes a physical body, darkness of the night will become bright before it, because, foolishness is darker and blacker than night. A fool, possessing foolishness is like a bat which eats and survives upon darkness. Therefore, it is required that the one in the darkness like the bat should cultivate the habit of developing consonance with the light of the day in a slow manner, as otherwise one will remain like the bat for the whole life. One with a dark inside will love only darkness like the horse or camel tied with the ropes and confined to one place. He will be inimical to any place in which there is a bright lamp. He is tied up with the rope of darkness and is always crazy for it for the reason that, he may get more money in the worldly life, so that money may further entangle him with ropes, and to keep him unaware of his bad qualities.

chapters.title: Signs of Wise, Perfect and Arrogant Men
chapters.subtitle: Signs of the perfect and the imperfect in wisdom; and of the perfect and imperfect men, and of the unfortunate, arrogant and worthless

paras: He is wise person who has a torch in his hand. He becomes a leader and guide to the caravan. He is a follower of his own light. He is not under anybody’s control and guidance but marches forward with his own light. He has faith upon himself and develops further faith on the light upon which he grazes and seeks the food for this soul. The other one is semi-wise, who finds out a wiseman to make him see the world through his eyes. He keeps his hand upon the shoulder of the wise man just as a blind man keeps on his guide’s shoulder, to such an extent that he becomes bright-eyed, smart and great with his guidance.

sections.heading: Fools Hate Wise Men
paras: Then, there is ass who does not possess wisdom even of the millets size. While he himself does not have wisdom, he even refuses to be with a wise man. He does not know of the path to a little or large extent and does not even search for a warner or guide. He keeps himself engaged in dullness, arguments and silly talks. He feels ashamed of following a leader. He goes along a large forest: sometimes with desperate steps and sometimes runs fast. He has no lamp, which he can take as a guide. Not even a semi-light from which he can borrow some light. He has no wisdom at all upon which he can lead his life. He does not have even half wisdom with which he can make himself like a dead body which is bathed by other living persons. If he makes himself, at least like a dead body, he has the scope to rise from low level to higher level. Therefore, one should make himself like a dead body to be cleaned by others when he has no wisdom of his own. A living breath is a refuge for the wise fellows. He is not alive, in which case he could be like H. Īsā, a living man (as H. Īsā did not die). And also, he is not dead upon which H. Īsā would blow his breath to give him life. He is neither alive nor dead and is like a raw grape which is neither a full-grown sweet grape to eat nor worthy of getting converted into wine. He is a raw grape, and cannot go beyond its rawness. He gets hardened, remains raw, sour and dead. His blind soul moves on all sides and gets trapped in superstition and doubts. He never struggles to get good results and always remains disturbed till death when there is no peace available to him as at the time when calamity has already arrived from the sky.

chapters.title: Three Fishes in a Pond
chapters.subtitle: Narrative of a lake pond and fishermen and three fishes of which one was wise, the other semi-wise and the third foolish, arrogant, careless and worthless; and their end

paras: Donot behave like an arrogant fool! Hear the narrative of the lake in which there were three large sized fishes. You might have heard this story in the book, Kaleela wa Dumna; but that was a rind of the fruit and what I am now to say is about its pulp and soul. Some fishermen came near that lake and found out about the fishes. They went back to fetch the net to catch them and the fishes came to know of their design.

sections.heading: Consult the Ambitious and Lively
paras: The one which was wise decided that it should go away from the spot, though going away from there was not by choice but to avoid difficulties. It said to itself: I shall not consult the other fishes as they will certainly make me dull of mind and power. The place of birth and the love for the country will have their impacts upon their minds; and their dullness and lack of wisdom will impact upon me. Consultation should be made with those who have a desire to live so that they may give a new life and vigor to you. Consult about a journey with one who is also in journey. If you consult a woman about going on a journey, she will make you lame. Go away from the bond of the love and treachery of the love of the country. Know this well, your country (world) is not the one where you have taken birth, but the one where you have to go. That is the (next world). If you want to go to your real country go to the other side of the lake and do not read wrongly this hadith.

chapters.title: Improper Supplications
chapters.subtitle: Meaning of the hadith: love of the country is a part of faith: Hubbul watani minal Īmān: improper recitation of the supplication: O God provide to me the fragrance of paradise: Allahumma Arihnii raa’ihata al jannata: while cleaning the nose; and supplication after cleaning the bowel after defecation: O God make me one among the repenters and among the cleansed one’s: Allahumma ja‘alnii minal tawwabiina waj‘alni minal mutatahhiriina: And a friends hearing of these losing patience and chastising him for improper recitation

sections.heading: Mysteries of Supplication Explained
paras: There are different supplications in performing of ablution. Different, while washing different parts as has been enunciated in Hadith. Thus, when you clean your nose, you should pray to God to provide you with the fragrance of paradise, fragrance of the flower guides one towards the garden. And when you clean your bowel after defection, what you should recite is: “O God cleanse me of this dirt. I cleaned myself upto the extent my hand reached, but my hand is very short in the cleaning of the soul. O God, you have made the incompetents, incompetents. The hand of your grace reaches upto the souls. The extent of this mean fellow like me was only upto this which I have done. And. O generous One! You may clean me of what is beyond my extent. O God! I have washed my skin of dirt and You may clean this friend of yours of the risks of the times.”

sections.heading: Inappropriate Recitation
paras: One fellow while cleaning the bowel after defecation was saying: “Set my connections with the fragrance of paradise.” A friend of his said: “You recited a good supplication; but you ignored the hole of the body for which it is meant. This supplication is meant for the nose but instead of that you brought down this recitation to the bowel’s hole. A free man smells the fragrance of paradise with his nose. How can the fragrance of paradise come from the hole of the bowel (anus)?” Just as this supplication is in an inappropriate manner, so also is the showing of consideration pride before the kings. Showing pride and superiority before the mean fellows is good and proper, but not before the kings, either of this or of that world. Be careful! Never to deviate from this principle as it would tie up your hands. Flowers are grown to provide fragrance to the nose. Smelling is the job of the nose. Do not be mistaken on this! Fine smell of the flower is meant for the pleasure of the brain. This lowly placed hole of the bowel is not a place of fine fragrance. How can you get the fragrance of paradise from this place? If you want to smell fine fragrance, you should search in its source.

sections.heading: Country Does Not Mean Place of Birth
paras: This is how you have to understand the meaning of the love of the country and from this angle it is good. Before considering it as a part of faith, you should first know what country means and which is that country. It is clear to every faithful man that his country is the next world and it is the love of that country that is a part of faith. Knowing the meaning of country has priority over the other aspect.

chapters.title: Wise Fish Leaves the Place
chapters.subtitle: Realization of the wise fish of the danger and leaving the place without consulting others

paras: The wise fish said to herself: “Let me go on a journey. I should not bother myself about consulting others and act upon their advice. There is no time left for consultation and therefore leave off just as H. ‘Ālī took a long sigh in a well when he was lonely. [ This is not a true narrative, but according to which, H. Ālī, under the compulsion of emotional tension wanted to take a long sigh for relief before some confidant friend. But finding none, he put his head on the mouth of a well and took a long sigh ― Qazi Sajjad Hussain]

sections.heading: Speedy Decision in Times of Danger
paras: There is no confidant at all on this way and therefore, I must alone secretly go away in the darkness of the night just as the police officers do to catch criminals. I must leave this lake and go toward the sea, search for the sea and give up this whirlpool.” The fish made her careful breast as careful steps and went away from the dangerous place towards the light of the sea. This was like that deer that was followed by a dog. It runs so long as far as its muscles and limbs allow it to run. This simile of “sleep of the rabbit” and “followed by dog” is wrong. Nobody in fear can have sleep in his eyes. Anyway, that fish left and took its way toward the sea which was a very long and very wide way. It underwent many difficulties on the way, but at last reached a place of peace and security. It put itself in a large deep sea the shore of which could not be seen by any eye. Later, when the fishermen brought their net, the semi-wise fish got worried and found difficulties ahead. She said to herself: Ah! I have lost my time. Why did I not take my friend as my guide? She has abruptly left, but anyway, she has gone away. I also should have gone along with her. Now my feeling sorry and anxious is of no use. What can I do now, when I have lost the chance? It is wrong to regret upon what has already happened. The time lost will never return. It is futile to think of it.

chapters.title: Advice of a Wise Bird
chapters.subtitle: Narrative of the bird which advised: Donot worry about what has already happened, donot believe in the impossible and set aright the present time and donot waste time in worries

paras: A bird was caught by a bird catcher by tricks in a net. It told the bird-catcher: “O great master! You have caught hold of a weak bird like me. Suppose that you eat me! You get no gain. You have eaten many cows and goats. You have also sacrificed many camels. Inspite of eating all that your stomach is not full. By eating my parts also your stomach will not be full. Be generous and let me go free, O noble, young honorable person! You may let me go and in recompense I shall give you three pieces of advice so that you may know whether I am wise or foolish. I shall give the first advice when you keep me on your hand. Be sure that my heart and soul have high regard for you. I shall give the second advice when I sit upon the wall, so that this advice may please you, make you good and make you proud of yourself. The third advice I shall give when I reach upon the tree, so that you may become very fortunate with them.

sections.heading: Do Not Believe in the Impossible
paras: While sitting upon his hand, it said that you should never believe in what is impossible. After saying this first advice, it flew off, became free and sat upon the wall. Then it gave the second advice: “Donot regret upon what has already happened.” Then it continued and said: “There is hidden in me a wonderful pearl weighing ten dirhams. It was your wealth and a fortune for your children. It was such a precious thing! I swear upon you. You lost that pearl as it was not in your luck to have it. A pearl the like of which is not to be found anywhere.” Hearing this, the bird-catcher started wailing and crying as a woman does in labour pain. He became mournful and started telling: “How regrettable! what a self-destruction I have done for myself. Why did I set you free with those tricks you have put me on the wrong path.” The bird said: “Did I not advise you that you should not regret upon what has already happened on the earlier occasion. When this has happened and gone, why do you feel sorry for it. Either you have not understood my advice, or you are deaf and not heard me. I had also given another advice: not be misguided and donot believe in what is impossible. O man like a lion! Think over! I am not even three dirhams in weight. How can a thing of ten dirhams find a place within me?” The bird-catcher came to his senses and said: “You are right, my beautiful one. Now, you may give me the third advice.” The bird said: “What good you have done upon my earlier advice that I should give you the third one, which will be a waste.” It said this and flew off joyously, fully euphoric, towards the forest.

sections.heading: Advice to Fools Is Effectless
paras: Giving advice to a foolish, ignorant fellow is like putting seeds in a barren land. What is torne by foolishness and ignorance cannot be darned. Therefore, O wiseman, donot put seeds in a barren land, because the ignorant fellow is a slave of ignorance. He will never-ever hear your advice.

chapters.title: Semi-Wise and the Foolish Fish
chapters.subtitle: The semi-wise fish’s designing a trick of showing itself as dead

paras: The semi-wise fish at a time of trial, when it had got away from the shadow of the wise, said: “My friend has gone toward the sea and freed itself from sorrows. I lost such a good friend. But I should not involve myself in these thoughts now and prepare myself to undergo troubles. Now I shall make myself as dead. I should make myself upside down like a dead fish with my belly upside and the back downside and start floating on the surface of water. I should float on the surface just as scraps, not swimming as man does. I shall make myself dead and let myself entirely at the mercy of water. Death before death is an avoidance from calamity.”

sections.heading: Death Before Death
paras: Death before death is a matter of peace, my dear young man. The noble prophet has said the same to us. All of you should die before the arrival of death and die with pain. [That is to say: you should annihilate yourself in God and be secured from all kinds of trials] In this manner it became like a dead fish with its belly upside. Water took it sometime above and sometime below. The fishermen, felt much grief that such a big fish had died and they lost it. With their talks of regrets the fish felt much happiness and said to herself: “my trick has given me victory and I got protected from the knife.” Then one of the fishermen caught hold of it, spat on with contempt and threw her on the dust. With efforts it turned this and that way and stealthily entered into water and saved itself.

sections.heading: Not Heading the Warner
paras: The third foolish fish turned and twisted herself this and that side to turn back into water and save herself. The fishermen spread their net and caught it in the net. Its foolishness led her to fire to be roasted on the frying pan and it entered into the sleep of death along with foolishness. While it was boiling with the heat, its wisdom was telling it: Did not a warner came to you? From this trap and calamity, it said like the infidels: “Yes they had!” [As has been said in the Qurān about those dumped into hell: “Did not a warner come to you?” They will say: “Yes indeed; A warner did come to us, but we rejected him”: “Alam yaatikum

sections.heading: Naziiran? Qaalu Balaa: Qad Jaa’anaa Naziirun: Fakazzabnaa”: (Mulk: 67: 8,9)]
paras: Then the fish used to say again: “If I get relieved of this neck breaking trouble, I shall not take any other place as my country other than the large sea. I shall not take a lake as my place of residence and comfort. I shall search for unlimited quantity of water and live in it in peace so that I may always be with health and security. It was making such agreements with itself which depended upon its getting released from that ordeal. “I shall ever hold on to the lapel of a wise one so that I may not be caught in such troubles and calamities.”

chapters.title: Liars Never Keep Promises
chapters.subtitle: To explain that the promises of the fools when they are caught in difficulties, and their regrets are of no use, as: if they were returned, they would certainly relapse to the things they were forbidden, for they are indeed liars: “wa law rudduu la‘aaduu limaa nuhuu ‘anhu wa innahum lakaazibuuna”: (An‘aam: 6: 28). A liar never keeps his words

paras: Wisdom told this foolish fish: “Foolishness is with you and promises of the foolish are broken. Keeping up of promises go with wisdom, but as you donot have wisdom, you are like an ass. Go away from here as you have no wisdom. Forgetfulness dominates and becomes your leader, which is your enemy and spoiler of your plans. With deficiency of wisdom, a moth does not remember the fire, its burning and pain causing effects. When it gets its wings burnt, it repents, but its desire and forgetfulness again make it hit upon fire. Self- control, thinking, memory and care are possession of the wise, as all these have been elevated to higher levels by wisdom. There cannot be any brilliance other than in a gem. And when there is none to make you remember, there is no scope for return to earlier good situations. Yet a fool desire to return to normalcy, but even this is a product of his foolishness as he fails to see that even his foolishness has become a part of his conduct. His feeling of shame upon failure is a result of pain and not as result of his wisdom. The moment that pain goes, his repentance and sense of shame remain just as worthy as dust. He regrets, because of the burden of darkness of sorrows. What was spoken at night and the decisions taken then, vanish with the oncoming of the light of the day. When that darkness ends, sorrows become joys. The products and gains of pain also vanish. He repents but his old wisdom calls him back and after returning, he does the same thing again.

chapters.title: Difference Between Wisdom and Imagination
chapters.subtitle: To explain that imagination is a counterfeit coin of wisdom and its enemy. It resembles it but it is not so in reality

paras: Wisdom is the opposite of passion. One going after passion and desires may not be called as wise. Consider that the one craving for non-existing or non-available things as an imaginer. [Both wisdom and imagination are mental faculties. Wisdom is an ability or result of ability to think and act utilizing knowledge, experience common sense and insight. It relates to real things. Imagination is a faculty or action of producing mental images of what is not present or experienced. Both are mental faculties. Wisdom has permanence, but imagination is passing and temporary ― Translator] The touchstone for wisdom and imagination is the Qurān and the conduct of the prophets. The touchstone tells the counterfeit to touch it and find out its unreality with its beatings and scratching and telling: “You are not fir to meet my lowly and higher attacks and yet subsist.” On the contrary if the coin of wisdom is cut into pieces, it still continues to smile and show itself like burning flame.

chapters.title: Dialogue Between Pharaoh and H. Mūsā
chapters.subtitle: Arguments between H. Mūsā as man of wisdom and Pharaoh as man of imagination

paras: Pharaoh has imagination, which sets fire to the world but H. Mūsā has wisdom that brightens the souls. H. Mūsā went on the path of depriving himself of his own life by annihilating himself in God. Pharaoh asked him as to who he was. H. Mūsā said: “I am wisdom and a prophet of the God of Grandeur and Majesty. I am a proof of God, a nd provider of peace from the miseries of misguidance.” Pharoah said: “Stop all these confusing statements. Keep quiet! Tell your earlier name and status!” H. Mūsā said: “My status is from His bowl of dust. My real name is His meanest slave. I am a child of a slave of God born from his back and the womb of one of His maids. My origin is from mud and water and dust to which God gave life. My return is the return of body of mud toward dust. O cruel fellow! Your return also is toward dust. Our origin and that of all rebellious fellows is from dust and there are a hundred evidences for that. “Has not your body been made of mud and has grown larger by taking food from mud? When the soul gets out of the body, you again go back to mud, in a fearful, frightening grave. Both you and me and all others similar to us, will become mud and your grand status will be no more.” Pharaoh said: “Apart from this progeny, you have another name, which suits you better. You are a slave of Pharaoh and a slave of his slaves, who in the beginning brought up your body and soul. You are a rebellious, arrogant, cruel slave, who ran away from his country for committing a shameful act. You are a murderer, traitor and denier of the rights of others. Consider your character on these lines. You were put to disgrace, deprivation and miseries away from your country, because you failed to recognize our right and graces upon you.” H. Mūsā said: “May God protect me! How can anyone be a partner to the great king? He is the only One in His kingdom and He has none to help Him in His administration. There is no leader for his servant other than Him. Nobody is a master for His creatures. None can claim partnership with Him other than the one to be destroyed. He is the maker of all shapes and He is my Maker. Anyone making claim on it is a seeker of calamity. You cannot make an eyelash of mine. How can you find out my soul? Rather, you are a traitor and rebel, as you claim participation in Him. I killed a cruel fellow by mistake and not with intention or for pleasure. I just gave a blow to him but he instantly fell down and died and gave up a life which did not belong to him I killed a dog but you killed lakhs of innocent children of a prophet (H. Yāqūb). [ The progeny of H, Yākūb is called bani Isra’īl, as Isra’īl was his another name, meaning beloved of God. In his progeny are included Prophets H. Yūsuf, H. Binyamin, H. Mūsā, H. Dāwood, H. Sulaimān, H. Zakariā, H. Yahyā, H. Maryam and H. Īsā and others. H. Mūsā himself being a bani Isra’īlī was sought to be killed Pharoah for which he had ordered for the killing of all male children of bani Isra’īl out of the fear of a male chile of bani Isra’īl to be born would because of his destruction ― Translator] “You have killed them and all this crime is upon your head. You do not know as to what punishment you will get for all these murders. You killed the progeny of H. Yāqūb, with the object of killing me. But God chose me and protected me by keeping you blind of me. What all you desired with these killing fell flat on the ground.” Pharaoh said: “Leave all these things and tell me whether, what you are doing in the fulfilment of my rights of providing you with bread and salt? Will all this, is it right on your part to insult me before the gathering of the people and connect a bright day into darkness upon my heart?” H. Mūsā said: “The insults to be faced on the doomsday are very hard, if you donot differentiate between good and bad qualities. You cannot bear the pain of a prick caused by a mosquito. How can you drink the poison of the snakes there? To look at, I am destroying your jobs, but in reality, I am cleaning the garden of thorns.”

chapters.title: Combination of Opposites
chapters.subtitle: To explain the construction is in destruction, peace of mind in anxieties, perfectness in spoilage, success in failure and existence in non-existence and all others in the opposites and alliances, in similar manner

paras: A person came and started digging the ground. A foolish fellow looked at this and shouted at him: “Why are you spoiling the ground, digging at and spreading out the mud?” The man said: “O dullard! Go away and do not pass remarks at me. First, understand the difference between construction and destruction. How can a farmland of wheat come about so long as the smooth land is not dug up and upturned? How can a garden, farmland, leaves and fruits come about, so long as the land is not dug up and its mud brought up and down? How can a body sore be caused without piercing its closed end and removing the pus from it? Until and unless the poisonous body fluids are burnt with medicines, there cannot be a regaining of health and happiness. The tailor tears the cloth into pieces; but nobody condemns his expertise, questioning him as to why he tears it off and what can be done with the pieces? Whenever new buildings have to be constructed, earlier older foundations have to be up and removed. Similarly, all professionals like carpenters, blacksmiths and butchers start with the cutting and upsetting of earlier conditions. It is hammering and powdering of bitter myrobalan that results in the health of the people. So long as you donot grind and make flour of wheat, our dining sheet cannot be organized.”

chapters.title: H. Mūsā’s Answer
chapters.subtitle: H. Mūsā’s answer to Pharoah on his warning

paras: H. Mūsā said: “You have said about providing bread and salt to me. It is incumbent upon me that I should repay it and save you from the hook of the fishermen, O great fish. If you follow the advice of Mūsā, you will be saved from this never-ending pricking of the hook. You have made yourself a slave of greed and converted a worm into a python. Your python is the python of your arrogant self. I have brough another python to fight against your python to use it for your betterment moment by moment, by making it hiss upon your python’s hisses and finally destroy it. If you agree with me. You will get rid of both of these snakes or otherwise, both will take away your life.”

chapters.title: Pharaoh’s Threats
chapters.subtitle: Pharaoh’s answer to H. Mūsā, with threats

paras: Pharaoh said: “Certainly you are a great magician, that you have created divisions with your treachery in people who had a single heart. You divided them into two groups. Your magical power is such that, it can create a split in rocks and mountains.”

chapters.title: Not Magical Powers
chapters.subtitle: H. Mūsā’s denial of magic and sorcery

paras: H. Mūsā said: “I am sunk in the message of God. Who has seen magic with the name of God? Magic is a product of infidelity and ignorance. But the religion of Mūsā is a torch of guidance. How can I be like the magicians, O unclean fellow, when experts in sorceries wait upon my breath for life? How can I be like the unclean magicians, when my name has granted light to heavenly scriptures? How can I be like the magicians as I am one upon whom the words of God fall from heavens? As you fly upon the air with the feathers of greed, you think me also to be similar to you.

sections.heading: Lowly Look as Others as Lowly
paras: Such of the people who deal with animals think lowly of the good people also to be like themselves. As you are one belonging to the lowly world, you think of all others as of your baser level and misguided ones. When you suffer from vertigo, your eyes see the house to be moving around. While moving in a boat across a river you feel the river bank also to be moving. If you have a narrow mind, you feel the entire world to be like you. If you are in the company of joyous friends, you will find the world as a beautiful garden. Many hypocrites go to Syria and Iraq and find only hypocrisy and dishonesty in the people there. Many people have gone to India and Herat and found nothing but commercial activities there. Many went to Turkistan and China and saw nothing but treachery and meanness there. Know this, O seeker of goodness, people see the same thing in every place what they want to see.

sections.heading: Search for What Is Needed
paras: One who cannot recognize anything other than matters of color and smell, may be told to see the same everywhere in the world. A cow suddenly entered into Baghdad, and went from one side to the other side. Inspite of there being great pleasures, entertainments and joys, it found nothing but the rinds of water-melon that were found fallen on the road, or grass, as these only are of its search and taste. They are like the meat hung upon the hook left for drying. It can only be affected by the surrounding circumstances and its other qualities do not improve. It only gets reduced in weight every day.

sections.heading: Progress of the Soul
paras: God’s earth is a victim of the world of cause and effect. But the impression of the soul changes every moment. It sees a new and fresh world every moment, whether it be the streams of paradise. But a heart that remains cold, remains at a single level, which is the quality of a vicious soul. O the one, who is caught in the field of causes and effects, you are not aware of the Causer of the causes. You keep yourself as an ass attached to petty causes. This inevitable results in the blindness of heart and madness, keeping you in distress and chains. Open your eyes and look at the Causer the causes, so that you may get rid of the causes of loss.”

chapters.title: Perceptions Are Different and Exclusive
chapters.subtitle: Perception of one sense organ of man is different from that of another organ; and one sense organ is not aware of the perception of another organ, just as an expert in a job of one country is ignorant of the expertise of another job of the same country; and this ignorance is due to the fact that, that is not his job. And because of this ignorance, perceptions do not cease to be perceptions

sections.heading: Sense Organs Do Only Allotted Jobs
paras: The point from which you see the world is your own perception. Good people remain behind their curtains for protection from your unclean perceptions. For a long time, you will have to wash your perception with the water of inner observation. This is what the Sufis do by washing their clothing, through which they cleanse their inside. When you clean up yourself, the curtain between you and the clan Sufis will be lifted and their clean souls will exhibit themselves to you. If the world of non-material things also were to be bright and physical, your eyes would have seen them. This alone is what you would see with your eyes. As against this, if you shut your eyes and bring forward ears to see the cheeks and tufts of a beauty, your ears will say: “I do not get inclined toward the face, because, seeing is not my job. My job is hearing alone. If that beautiful face calls me, I can hear and respond. Looking at physical objects is the job of the eye and not mine. Eye can see but I am not capable of seeing. I am an expert only of my job and art, and my job and art are related only to words and souls.” So also, if you call the nose and say to it to see that beauty, you will find that it is also not capable of seeing. It will say: “If there is the fragrance of musk and rose, I can take stock of it. This alone is my art, job and expertise. How can I see the face of that beauty with silvery feet? Be careful, not to trouble me to use that power which I donot possess.”

sections.heading: Defective Eyes See Good Things as Defective
paras: Even seeing which is the job of the eyes cannot be done perfectly by the cross-eyed. They will see not in perfectness, but twisted, whether you walk before it in a straight or topsy turvy manner. So also, a squint, who cannot see one thing as one but as two. It goes after duality and not oneness.” H. Mūsā continued to speak to Pharoah: “You are a personified treachery and fraud. You cannot see the difference between you and me. O performer of crooked acts! Do not try to see me within yourself, so that you may not see one as two. Look at me from my own angle for a little time, so that you may see a vast land ahead of your world. You will get rid of the sense of honour and dishonour and see love only in love. Peace be upon you!”

sections.heading: When Ear and Nose Also See
paras: When you get rid of the body, you will know that, your ear and nose do the job of the eyes. That sweet tongued king, H. Baayazīd Bistāmī has said that every hair of the gnostic of God becomes an eye, and sees. Certainly, there was no eye in the body when it was just there was no eye in the body when it was just a muscular flesh in the mother’s womb. It came only later. Even the capacity of seeing by the eye is not a property of the fat in it, which is done when the eye is open. If that were its property, then how does the eye see things when it is closed as it happens when one is in sleep. Capacity to see is not of the eye but of something else. Non-physical creatures like devils and fairies see things even though they have no eyes or fat in the eyes. There is no connection between light and fat. God, the Grantor and Creator has established a rapport between them. Man is made up of mud, but has no similarity with it. So also, the jinns are made of fire but there is no similarity between them and fire. The fairy is not like fire, even though it is made of fire as its base. Birds’s existence is with air but they are not similar to air. God has granted relationship between unrelated things. There are many such connections between the branches and bases of things. They are entirely different from each other, but God has established relationships between them.

sections.heading: Seeing Without Eyes
paras: Man was created from the particles of clay. That is to say: clay is the father and man is its son. But there is no similarity between them. And if there is a connection, it is beyond the comprehension of wisdom. Wisdom has no physical body; and it is very difficult to comprehend a non-physical substance. There are things which can see and differentiate without eyes. If God had not given sight to the wind which has no eyes, then how did it differentiate between the people of ‘Aad? How did it differentiate between a faithful and infidel, and found them to as different from each other as wine and the pumpkin. Fire of Nimrod, instead of burning H. Ibrahīm, protected him from itself, because of its looking at him without eyes. If the river Nile had no sight to see, how could it have differentiated between the Copts and the children of Isrā’il? If the hills and rocks were not seeing, they would not have become friendly with H. Dāwood. If earth were not to have eyes, it would not have swallowed Qārūn. If Hannana (a dry log of wood), were not to have the eye of the heart, how could it have found out the separation of that wise Prophet Muhammed, standing upon which, he used to give sermons. If the pieces of stones were not seeing, they would not have given the evidence of the prophethood of H. Muhammed when they were in his fist. Therefore, O wisdom! Take into account all these facts and open your wings and feathers, and read in the Surah Zilzaal: “When the earth is shaken to her utmost convulsion”: “izaa zulzilatil ardhu zilzaalaha”: (Surah 99). This earth stands as a witness for the good and vicious on the doomsday. Can it do so without seeing them? Would it speak of its situations and informations and show its mysteries to us? Then H. Músā continued to speak to Pharoah: “My being sent before a ruler like you is given as a proof that my Sender is well aware of matters. For such an injury that you have, I alone can be the ointment required. You have seen the incidents that occurred earlier, in the light of which, you can see that God has sent me to you. I shall carry my staff and the brightness of my hand and break your arrogant horns.

sections.heading: Warning Through Dreams
paras: Many frightening dreams were shown to you by the lord of religion, in accordance with your faith and rebellious nature, so that you may know that they were suitable for you. So also, you may know that the well informed and wise might provide medicine to bring you back to health from sickness. But you were only making interpretations to refuse to understand and remain as blind and deaf and be in deep sleep. Your physicians and astrologers through the light of their learning found out the true meanings, but out of greed, they had them from you. They told you that it is beyond your kingship and authority to be impacted by unpalatable situations. It is because of indigestion or unhealthy food; mind gets upset and shows such bad dreams. They did so, because they found you to be unamenable to good advice. You are very haughty and cruel lacking peaceful instinct.

sections.heading: Kings Should Be Moderate
paras: “Kings resort to killings by keeping some peaceful objects in view. Their mercy precedes their wrath. Anger does not dominate upon them like a devil so that they may cause bloodshed without purpose. One should take all these things into consideration in the matters of life. And at the same time, one should not be with the self-control of impotent, so that his wife and maid may not resort to bad habits. But you have made your chest a house for the devil and made ill-will as the direction of your worship (Qibla). Your horn has pierced the hearts of many and spoiled them. Now, my staff has broken your horn.”

chapters.title: Infidels’ Attacks on the Faithful
chapters.subtitle: Aggression of the men of this world upon those of that world upto the other end of their fort, which is the boundary of the other world; and their carelessness about their place of refuge, and their avoidance to perform jihad resulting in the beatings by the infidels

paras: Army of the men of physical forces organized an attack on the fort of the men of spiritual forces, so as to capture the gates of the sources of hidden powers; so that not a single clean- hearted may come from that side. When the faithful reduce their acts of jihād, the infidels take an about-turn and attack them instead.

sections.heading: Faithful’s Forbearance, Not Weakness
paras: Those faithful one’s did not attack you, out of their forbearance, inspite of your being a follower of a false religion. You became bold enough to attack on the gates of the sources of unseen benefits, so that the unseen brave one’s may not come from there. You extended your hands upon the backs and wombs of the people so that the sources of your troubles may remain closed. But you did not think as to how you can close that highway which the Lord of Majesty and Grandeur has kept open. O quarrelsome fellow! You closed the door; yet you remained blind; and one soldier came out from there. Now, you may see! I am that soldier to have come to upset your design. Now, I shall destroy your name and fame upon the name of that Lord. Be careful to shut the doors tightly and be pleased for some time and turn your moustache. Your fate will pluck out every hair of your moustache, to make you know that fate blinds the eyes. Think whether your moustache is sharper or that of the people of ‘Aad, with whose name cities used to shiver in fear. Think whether you are better fighter or the Thamud, the like of whom did not take birth. I can say a hundred examples like these, but you are deaf. You will hear and overhear them. I repent upon what all I have said to you; and without telling you, I shall prepare the medicine for you.

sections.heading: All Acts Get a Recompense
paras: I shall keep this upon your raw sore, so that it may ripen so that your wound and your beard may burn out for ever. So that you may know, my enemy, that He knows you very well and provides to everything what is most suitable to it. There is no occasion when you commit a wrong and spread-out mischief for which you may not see the appropriate result. There was no occasion you sent some good act upon the sky even for a moment, the good reward for which has not come. If you reflect upon your own deeds and remain alert, you will get the recompense of your act every moment. When you take care of your own actions and hold on to the rope of safety, there is no need for you to wait for the arrival of the doomsday. Every such moment decides the good and bad results of your actions. There is no need for one to be told in detail who has the capacity to understand with hints.

sections.heading: Sins Will Not Go Unpunished
paras: This calamity has come upon you for your foolishness, as you did not understand the hints and gestures. Know this well that in such places boldness is not required when the heart has become black due to sinful acts. Yet, if you show dareness instead of regretting and repenting, this blackness will become an arrow to punish you for your dareness. If an arrow has not hit you, you may consider that it is due to the grace of God and not that your sin has not been seen. Therefore, if you want the safety and security of your heart, you may be watchful to your heart, because every minor or major act of yours creates something of use in you. And, if you have greater courage to be more careful, you will go to a higher level than mere watchfulness and reflections.

chapters.title: Polishing of Heart with Wisdom
chapters.subtitle: To explain that the clayish body of man is like steel, which can become a good mirror in which, this world, paradise, hell, doomsday etc, can be seen, not just as imagination but as real objects

sections.heading: Polishing Makes a Mirror of Iron
paras: Your body is black like iron. But you may polish it repeatedly so that your heart is filled up with faces like a mirror and with slivery bodies on all sides. Iron was black and dull initially but polishing removed its blackness. Iron received polishing and made its face pleasing, to such an extent that, one can see one’s face in it. So also, if your body is black and ugly, you may polish it too, as has the capacity to receive polish so that faces from the unseeable non- physical world may be visible in it like the reflections of houries and angels. God has given you the polish of wisdom so that you may brighten the sheets of the heart with it. But instead of this you have shut the doors of polishing and stretched both of your arms to embrace desires. If you shut the doors of desires, your hands will stretch to go for polishing.

sections.heading: Mirror of the Heart
paras: When the iron of your heart becomes a mirror of unseeable world. All faces and shapes from it will fall on it. But you blackened it, got it rusted and closed the doors and felled yourself among those who strive to do mischief on earth: “wa yas‘awna fil ardhi fasaadan”: (Maida: 5: 33). You have done all this so far; but donot do it hereafter. You have polluted the water; and do not pollute it further. Donot stir and disturb it so that it may remain clean and undisturbed, upon which you will see the moon and stars moving in it. Man is like water in the stream, which does not show its bed when polluted. The bed of water is full of gems and pearls and donot disturb it and allow it to remain clean and clear. Man’s soul is like air, which becomes a curtain for the sky when it is filled with dust. It comes in the way of your looking at the sun and gets restored to cleanliness and purity when the dust passes off. The sum and substance of this talk is that you should never stop polishing; and be sure that God is aware of what all is hidden your breast.

chapters.title: Revelation of Pharaoh’s Secrets
chapters.subtitle: H.Músā further talk to Pharoah by revealing his hidden secrets to him and further incidents so that he may develop faith thereafter. And the story of the negro who shit on the mirror

paras: H. Músā continued: “Inspite of your being completely black of character, God exhibits before you some incidents so that you may find out the path of deliverance. He showed to you through the black iron such incidents, that spoke of what was to happen later, so that you may not continue your cruelties and vicious acts. You saw all that but became worse. There were dreams which showed ugly faces, which you hated to see, which were your real affairs. Your case was like that of a negro who looked at his own ugly face in a mirror and contemptuously shit on it saying: “how ugly you are to look at? You are worthy of this alone!” but that blind fellow did not realize that it was his own face. He considered his ugliness as the quality of the mirror. The mirror said: “The cruelty that you did with the mirror is your own face.” If was not on the mirror, because it has a clean, bright face.

sections.heading: Warnings to Pharaoh
paras: “In similar manner, you saw in your dream, your garments catching fire and your mouth and eyes stitched. You found yourself being hounded by beasts, and sometimes your head in the grips of their jaws. Sometimes you fell flat in the latrine and sometimes swimming in water mixed with blood. Sometimes, you fell down flat from the terrace and both your hands tied between wrenches. Sometimes you saw yourself chained and under yokes; and sometimes your head being beaten like a drum. Sometimes, a voice came to you from the clear sky telling repeatedly that you were accursed. Sometimes, calls came from the hills that you belong to the sinful people of the left side. Sometimes, every non-living thing caried out that Pharoah fell into the hell forever. Sometimes, every plant caried out that Pharoah died as a chased away fellow from grace.

sections.heading: Warnings Hardened Pharoah
paras: “There were many incidents worse than these which I feel ashamed of to speak out, but instead of making you good they made you worse and your blind nature made you still more cruel. O the one to accept good things! I have said very little, so that, with these few, you may know that I am well aware all these things. You have made yourself blind and dead to avoid to take lessons from what you saw in the dreams and what incidents you met with. How long do you avoid this? The lack of the insight of your cheating and fraudulent- planning-wisdom has come and stood before you.”

chapters.title: Door of Repentance Is Open
chapters.subtitle: To explain that the door of repentance and seeking of grants is open with the grace of God

paras: H. Músā continued: “At least now, give up what all you have done so far. At least now, try to protect yourself, as the door of forgiveness is still open. The door of repentance is open on the western side for all the creatures until the doomsday. This will continue to be open till the sun rises from the west. The door is open now and do not go away from it.

sections.heading: Eight Doors of Paradise
paras: Paradise has eight doors for entrance, and one of them is the door of repentance. Other seven doors sometimes open and sometimes close; but the door of repentance is always open. Make use of this opportunity right now and carry your baggage of repentance and throw dust into the eyes of the jealous, who out of jealousy are obstructing your path to this door. Do it fast before the door of wrath opens and shuts the door of repentance. If you delay to do so, all your sighs and cries will not be heard by anyone after the door of repentance closes. Return from rejection of grants and enter into this door so that due to your misfortune, you may not be chased away from count of the Great Lord.”

chapters.title: One Advice with Four Graces
chapters.subtitle: H. Mūsā’s telling Pharoah to accept one advice from him and get four graces in return. And Pharaoh’s enquiring about the four graces

paras: H. Mūsā continued to say: “Take one advice from me and hold on to it; and take from me four graces”. Pharoah asked: “What is that advice. Explain a little about it to me”.

sections.heading: Greatness and Domination of Good
paras: Then H. Mūsā said: “That one is: you make an open declaration that there is no god other than God who is the all in all. Creator of the heavens, and the stars in heights; and of men, devils, fairies and birds. Creator of rivers, mountains, forests and fields. His dominion has no limits and He is incomparable. He is the Protector of everything, every man and all places; and Provider of the needs of living beings in the world. He is the guard of the earth and sky and bringer of flowers from grass. He is aware of the thoughts of the hearts and is a ruler of and dominant upon the oppressors and the mighty of the world. He is the King of all kings and every action is as per His order. God does whatever He wills: “wa yaf‘alul laahu maa yashā’u”: (Ibrāhim: 14: 27)
